params.name: aaa_url
params.doc: URL of the diameter client: the configuration file, with an optional extra-avps-file, where the Diameter client is configured.

params.name: answer_timeout
params.doc: Time, in milliseconds, after which a function call with no received reply will time out and return a -2 code.

params.name: fd_log_level
params.doc: This parameter measures the quietness of the logging done by the freeDiameter library. Possible values:

params.name: peer_identity
params.doc: The identity (realm subdomain) of the Diameter server peer, to which the OpenSIPS Diameter client peer will connect.

params.name: realm
params.doc: The unique realm to be used by all participating Diameter peers.

functions.name: dm_send_answer
functions.doc: Send back a Diameter answer message to the interconnected peer in a non-blocking fashion, in response to its request.

functions.name: dm_send_request
functions.doc: Perform a blocking Diameter request over to the interconnected peer and return the Result-Code AVP value from the reply.

params.name: fetch_all_values
params.doc: For the output sets, this parameter controls if all the values (for the same RADIUS AVP) should be returned (otherwise only the first value will be returned). When enabling this options, be sure that the variable you use to get the RADIUS output can store multiple values (like the AVP variables).

params.name: radius_config
params.doc: Radiusclient configuration file.

params.name: sets
params.doc: Sets of Radius AVPs to be used when building custom RADIUS requests (set of input RADIUS AVPs) or when fetching data from the RADIUS reply (set of output RADIUS AVPs).

params.name: syslog_name
params.doc: Enable logging of the client library to syslog, using the given log name.

functions.name: radius_send_acct
functions.doc: This function can be used from the script to make custom radius authentication request. The function takes only one string parameter that represents the name of the set that contains the list of attributes and pvars that will form the accounting request.

functions.name: radius_send_auth
functions.doc: This function can be used from the script to make custom radius authentication request. The function takes two parameters.

params.name: aaa_url
params.doc: This is the url representing the AAA protocol used and the location of the configuration file of this protocol.

params.name: acc_callid_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the request's Callid value.

params.name: acc_from_tag_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the From header TAG parameter.

params.name: acc_method_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the request's method name as string.

params.name: acc_sip_code_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the final reply's numeric code value in string format.

params.name: acc_sip_reason_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the final reply's reason phrase value.

params.name: acc_time_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the time stamp of the transaction completion in date-time format.

params.name: acc_to_tag_column
params.doc: Column name in accounting table to store the To header TAG parameter.

params.name: db_table_acc
params.doc: Table name of accounting successful calls -- database specific.

params.name: db_table_avp
params.doc: Exported by `acc`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: db_table_missed_calls
params.doc: Table name for accounting missed calls -- database specific.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: SQL address -- database specific. If is set to NULL or empty string, the SQL support is disabled.

params.name: detect_direction
params.doc: Controls the direction detection for sequential requests. If enabled (non zero value), for sequential requests with upstream direction (from callee to caller), the FROM and TO will be swapped (the direction will be preserved as in the original request).

params.name: early_media
params.doc: Should be early media (any provisional reply with body) accounted too ?

params.name: extra_fields
params.doc: Defines the tag-log_value set to be used in extra fields accounting. See for a detailed description of the Extra accounting.

params.name: leg_fields
params.doc: Defines the tag-log_value set to be used in multi-leg accounting. See for a detailed description of the Multi Call-Legs accounting.

params.name: log_facility
params.doc: Log facility to which accounting messages are issued to syslog. This allows to easily seperate the accounting specific logging from the other log messages.

params.name: log_level
params.doc: Log level at which accounting messages are issued to syslog.

params.name: report_cancels
params.doc: By default, CANCEL reporting is disabled -- most accounting applications wants to see INVITE's cancellation status. Turn on if you explicitly want to account CANCEL transactions.

params.name: service_type
params.doc: AAA service type used for accounting.

functions.name: acc_aaa_request
functions.doc: Like acc_log_request , acc_aaa_request reports on a request. It reports to aaa server as configured in aaa_url .

functions.name: acc_db_request
functions.doc: Like acc_log_request , acc_db_request reports on a request. The report is sent to database at db_url , in the table referred to in the second action parameter.

functions.name: acc_evi_request
functions.doc: Like acc_log_request , acc_evi_request reports on a request. The report is packed as an event sent through the OpenSIPS Event Interface as E_ACC_EVENT if the reply code is a positive one (lower than 300), or E_ACC_MISSED_EVENT for negative or no codes. More information on this in .

functions.name: acc_load_ctx_from_dlg
functions.doc: The function loads and exposes the accounting context of the currently in-use dialog. By dialog context, it means, from script level, you will read/write the accounting variables from the other dialog. The current accounting context is stashed until an unload operation is done.

functions.name: acc_log_request
functions.doc: acc_request reports on a request, for example, it can be used to report on missed calls to off-line users who are replied 404 - Not Found. To avoid multiple reports on UDP request retransmission, you would need to embed the action in stateful processing.

functions.name: acc_new_leg
functions.doc: Creates a new leg and increments only if multi-leg accounting is used. All values of the new leg will be initialized to null.

functions.name: acc_unload_ctx_from_dlg
functions.doc: The function off-loads a previosuly loaded accounting context, exposing whatever accounting context was present before doing the load.

functions.name: do_accounting
functions.doc: do_accounting() replaces all the *_flag and, *_missed_flag, cdr_flag, failed transaction_flag and the db_table_avp modparams. Just call do_accounting(), select where and how you want the accounting to take place, and the function will do all the work for you.

functions.name: drop_accounting
functions.doc: drop_accounting() resets flags and types of accounting set with do_accounting(). If called with no arguments all accounting will be stopped. If called with only one argument all accounting for that type will be stopped. If called with two arguments normal accounting will still be enabled.

params.name: aaa_url
params.doc: This is the url representing the connection to the AAA server. Note: Currently the module only supports connections to a Diameter server. The path to the AVPs configuration file is also required, otherwise the module will not start, or not work properly.

params.name: realm
params.doc: The Realm used in the Origin Diameter commands.

params.name: alias_domain_column
params.doc: Name of the column storing alias domain.

params.name: alias_user_column
params.doc: Name of the column storing alias username.

params.name: append_branches
params.doc: If the alias resolves to many SIP IDs, the first is replacing the R-URI, the rest are added as branches.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: Name of the column storing user's domain.

params.name: domain_prefix
params.doc: Specifies the prefix to be stripped from the domain in R-URI before doing the search.

params.name: user_column
params.doc: Name of the column storing username.

functions.name: alias_db_find
functions.doc: The function is very similar to alias_db_lookup() , but instead of using fixed input (RURI) and output (RURI) is able to get the input SIP URI from a pseudo-variable and place the result back also in a pseudo-variable.

functions.name: alias_db_lookup
functions.doc: The function takes the R-URI and search to see whether it is an alias or not. If it is an alias for a local user, the R-URI is replaced with user's SIP uri.

params.name: calculate_ha1
params.doc: This parameter tells the server whether it should expect plaintext passwords in the pseudo-variable or a pre-calculated HA1 string.

params.name: disable_nonce_check
params.doc: By setting this parameter you disable the security mechanism that protects against intrusion sniffing and does not allow nonces to be reused. But, because of the current implementation, having this enabled breaks auth for an architecture where load is balanced by having more servers with the same dns name. This parameter has to be set in this case.

params.name: nonce_expire
params.doc: Nonces have limited lifetime. After a given period of time nonces will be considered invalid. This is to protect replay attacks. Credentials containing a stale nonce will be not authorized, but the user agent will be challenged again. This time the challenge will contain stale parameter which will indicate to the client that it doesn't have to disturb user by asking for username and password, it can recalculate credentials using existing username and password.

params.name: password_spec
params.doc: This name of the pseudo-variable that will hold the password.

params.name: realm_prefix
params.doc: Prefix to be automatically strip from realm. As an alternative to SRV records (not all SIP clients support SRV lookup), a subdomain of the master domain can be defined for SIP purposes (like sip.mydomain.net pointing to same IP address as the SRV record for mydomain.net). By ignoring the realm_prefix sip. , at authentication, sip.mydomain.net will be equivalent to mydomain.net .

params.name: rpid_avp
params.doc: Full AVP specification for the AVP which stores the RPID value. It used to transport the RPID value from authentication backend modules (auth_db or auth_radius) or from script to the auth function append_rpid_hf and is_rpid_user_e164.

params.name: rpid_prefix
params.doc: Prefix to be added to Remote-Party-ID header field just before the URI returned from either radius or database.

params.name: rpid_suffix
params.doc: Suffix to be added to Remote-Party-ID header field after the URI returned from either radius or database.

params.name: secret
params.doc: Exported by `auth`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: username_spec
params.doc: This name of the pseudo-variable that will hold the username.

functions.name: append_rpid_hf
functions.doc: This function is the same as . The only difference is that it accepts two parameters--prefix and suffix to be added to Remote-Party-ID header field. This function ignores rpid_prefix and rpid_suffix parameters, instead of that allows to set them in every call.

functions.name: append_rpid_hf_no_params
functions.doc: Appends to the message a Remote-Party-ID header that contains header 'Remote-Party-ID: ' followed by the saved value of the SIP URI received from the database or radius server followed by the value of module parameter radius_rpid_suffix. The function does nothing if no saved SIP URI exists.

functions.name: consume_credentials
functions.doc: This function removes previously authorized credentials from the message being processed by the server. That means that the downstream message will not contain credentials there were used by this server. This ensures that the proxy will not reveal information about credentials used to downstream elements and also the message will be a little bit shorter. The function must be called after www_authorize or proxy_authorize .

functions.name: is_rpid_user_e164
functions.doc: The function checks if the SIP URI received from the database or radius server and will potentially be used in Remote-Party-ID header field contains an E164 number (+followed by up to 15 decimal digits) in its user part. Check fails, if no such SIP URI exists (i.e. radius server or database didn't provide this information).

functions.name: proxy_challenge
functions.doc: The function challenges a user agent. It will generate a Proxy-Authorize header field containing a digest challenge, it will put the header field into a response generated from the request the server is processing and will send the reply. Upon reception of such a reply the user agent should compute credentials and retry the request. For more information regarding digest authentication see RFC2617, RFC3261 and RFC8760.

functions.name: pv_proxy_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617 . If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call proxy_challenge which will challenge the user again. For more about the negative return codes, see the above function.

functions.name: pv_www_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617 . If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call www_challenge which will challenge the user again.

functions.name: www_challenge
functions.doc: The function challenges a user agent. It will generate one or more WWW-Authorize header fields containing a digest challenges, it will put the header field(s) into a response generated from the request the server is processing and will send the reply. Upon reception of such a reply the user agent should compute credentials and retry the request. For more information regarding digest authentication see RFC2617, RFC3261 and RFC8760.

params.name: aaa_url
params.doc: This is the url representing the AAA protocol used and the location of the configuration file of this protocol.

params.name: auth_service_type
params.doc: This is the value of the Service-Type aaa attribute to be used when performing an authentication operation. The default should be fine for most people. See your aaa client include files for numbers to be put in this parameter if you need to change it.

params.name: check_service_type
params.doc: AAA service type used by aaa_does_uri_exist and aaa_does_uri_user_exist checks.

params.name: digest_qop_name
params.doc: Exported by `auth_aaa`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: use_ruri_flag
params.doc: When this parameter is set to the value other than "NULL" and the request being authenticated has flag with matching number set via setflag() function, use Request URI instead of uri parameter value from the Authorization / Proxy-Authorization header field to perform AAA authentication. This is intended to provide workaround for misbehaving NAT / routers / ALGs that alter request in the transit, breaking authentication. At the time of this writing, certain versions of Linksys WRT54GL are known to do that.

functions.name: aaa_does_uri_exist
functions.doc: Checks from Radius if the SIP URI stored in the "sip_uri" parameter (or user@host part of the Request-uri if "sip_uri" is not given) belongs to a local user. Can be used to decide if 404 or 480 should be returned after lookup has failed. If yes, loads AVP based on SIP-AVP reply items returned from Radius. Each SIP-AVP reply item must have a string value of form:

functions.name: aaa_does_uri_user_exist
functions.doc: Similar to aaa_does_uri_exist, but check is done based only on Request-URI user part or user stored in "sip_uri". The user should thus be unique among all users, such as an E.164 number.

functions.name: aaa_proxy_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617 . If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call proxy_challenge which will challenge the user again. For more about the negative return codes, see the above function.

functions.name: aaa_www_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC2617 . If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call www_challenge which will challenge the user again.

params.name: async_timeout
params.doc: The amount of milliseconds an asynchronous call should wait for getting an authentication vector.

params.name: default_algorithm
params.doc: The default algorithm to be advertise during challenge, if the functions do not provide them explicitly. Note that at least one of the algorithms provided should be an AKA one, otherwise it makes no sense to use this module.

params.name: default_av_mgm
params.doc: The default AV Manager used in case the functions do not provide them explicitly.

params.name: default_qop
params.doc: The default qop parameter used during challenge, if the functions do not provide them explicitly.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash that stores the AVs for each user. Must be a power of 2 number.

params.name: sync_timeout
params.doc: The amount of milliseconds a synchronous call should wait for getting an authentication vector.

functions.name: aka_av_add
functions.detail: aka_av_add(public_identity, private_identity, authenticate, authorize, confidentiality_key, integrity_key[, algorithms])
functions.doc: Adds an authentication vector for the user identitied by public_identity and private_identity .

functions.name: aka_av_drop
functions.doc: Drops the authentication vector corresponding to the authenticate/nonce value for an user identitied by public_identity and private_identity .

functions.name: aka_av_drop_all
functions.doc: Drops all authentication vectors for an user identitied by public_identity and private_identity . This function is useful when a synchronization must be done.

functions.name: aka_av_fail
functions.doc: Marks the engine that an authentication vector query for a user has failed, unlocking the processing of the message.

functions.name: aka_proxy_authorize
functions.doc: The function behaves the same as , but it authenticates the user from a proxy perspective. It receives the same parameters, with the same meaning, and returns the same values.

functions.name: aka_proxy_challenge
functions.doc: The function behaves the same as , but it challenges the user from a proxy perspective. It receives the same parameters, with the same meaning, the only difference being that in case of the realm is missing, then it is taken from the the To domain , rather than from From domain . The header added is Proxy-Authenticate , rather than WWW-Authenticate The rest of the parameters, behavior, as well as return values are the same.

functions.name: aka_www_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies credentials according to RFC3310 , by using an authentication vector priorly allocated by an aka_www_challenge() call, using the av_mgm manager. If the credentials are verified successfully the function will succeed, otherwise it will fail with an appropriate error code, as follows:

functions.name: aka_www_challenge
functions.doc: The function challenges a user agent. It fetches an authentication vector for each algorigthm used through the av_mgm Manager and generate one or more WWW-Authenticate header fields containing digest challenges. It will put the header field(s) into a response generated from the request the server is processing and will send the reply. Upon reception of such a reply the user agent should compute credentials using the used authentication vector annd retry the request. For more information regarding digest authentication see RFC2617, RFC3261, RFC3310 and RFC8760.

params.name: calculate_ha1
params.doc: This parameter tells the server whether it should considered the loaded password (for authentification) as plaintext passwords or a pre-calculated HA1 string.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: This is URL of the database to be used. Value of the parameter depends on the database module used. For example for mysql and postgres modules this is something like mysql://username:password@host:port/database. For dbtext module (which stores data in plaintext files) it is directory in which the database resides.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: This is the name of the column in a 'SUBSCRIBER' like table holding the domains of users. Default value is fine for most people. Use the parameter if you really need to change it.

params.name: hash_column_sha256
params.doc: The name of the column holding SHA-256 HA1 hashes ( RFC 8760 support).

params.name: hash_column_sha512t256
params.doc: The name of the column holding SHA-512/256 HA1 hashes. ( RFC 8760 support).

params.name: load_credentials
params.doc: This parameter specifies credentials to be fetched from database when the authentication is performed. The loaded credentials will be stored in AVPs. If the AVP name is not specificaly given, it will be used a NAME AVP with the same name as the column name.

params.name: password_column
params.doc: This is the name of the column in a "subscriber" like table holding MD5 HA1 hash strings or plaintext passwords. An MD5 HA1 hash is an MD5 hash of username, password and realm. Storing hashes in the DB (as opposed to passwords directly) is much more secure, because the server does not need to know plaintext passwords and because it is computationally infeasible for an attacker to reverse-obtain a password from an HA1 string.

params.name: skip_version_check
params.doc: This parameter specifies not to check the auth table version. This parameter should be set when a custom authentication table is used.

params.name: uri_domain_column
params.doc: Column holding domain in an 'URI' like table.

params.name: uri_uriuser_column
params.doc: Column holding uri username in an 'URI' like table.

params.name: uri_user_column
params.doc: Column holding usernames in an 'URI' like table.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: If true (not 0), domain will be also used when looking up in the subscriber table. If you have a multi-domain setup, it is strongly recommended to turn on this parameter to avoid username overlapping between domains.

params.name: user_column
params.doc: This is the name of the column in a 'SUBSCRIBER' like table holding the usernames. Default value is fine for most people. Use the parameter if you really need to change it.

functions.name: db_does_uri_exist
functions.doc: Checks if the username@domain from the given uri is an existing user in a 'SUBSCRIBER' like table.

functions.name: db_get_auth_id
functions.doc: Checks given uri-string username against an 'URI' like table. Returns true if the user exists in the database, and sets the given variables to the authentication id and realm corresponding to the given uri.

functions.name: db_is_from_authorized
functions.doc: Similar to but instead of checking the TO header URI, the FROM header URI is checked.

functions.name: db_is_to_authorized
functions.doc: The function checks against a 'URI' like table to see if the username extracted from the To header URI is allowed/authorized to use the credentials (authentication username) validated by .

functions.name: proxy_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies the received credentials against a "SUBSCRIBER"-like table according to digest authentication as per RFC2617 . If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call proxy_challenge which will challenge the user again.

functions.name: www_authorize
functions.doc: The function verifies the received credentials against a "SUBSCRIBER"-like table according to digest authentication as per RFC2617 . If the credentials are verified successfully then the function will succeed and mark the credentials as authorized (marked credentials can be later used by some other functions). If the function was unable to verify the credentials for some reason then it will fail and the script should call www_challenge which will challenge the user again.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: If set to 0, the module won't connect to the Database for reading the Keys for decoding JWTs - only jwt_script_authorize will be usable from the script.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: This is URL of the database to be used. Value of the parameter depends on the database module used. For example for mysql and postgres modules this is something like mysql://username:password@host:port/database. For dbtext module (which stores data in plaintext files) it is directory in which the database resides.

params.name: end_ts_column
params.doc: column holding the jwt secret end unix timestamp.

params.name: load_credentials
params.doc: This parameter specifies credentials to be fetched from the JWT profiles table when the authentication is performed. The loaded credentials will be stored in AVPs. If the AVP name is not specificaly given, it will be used a NAME AVP with the same name as the column name.

params.name: profiles_table
params.doc: Name of the DB table containing the jwt profiles

params.name: secret_column
params.doc: Column holding the actual jwt signing secret.

params.name: secret_tag_column
params.doc: Column holding the JWT secret associated tag.

params.name: secrets_table
params.doc: Name of the DB table containing the jwt secrets

params.name: start_ts_column
params.doc: Column holding the JWT secret start UNIX timestamp.

params.name: tag_claim
params.doc: The JWT claim which will be used to identify the JWT profile

params.name: tag_column
params.doc: Column holding the JWT profile tag.

params.name: username_column
params.doc: Column holding the JWT profile associated SIP username.

functions.name: extract_pub_key_from_cert
functions.doc: The function will read the first param ( certificate ), decode it and then try to extract the public key with the certificate. If the extraction is succesful, the out_public_key will be populated. Useful to be used in conjuction with the jwt_script_authorize function, since most providers make their certificates public, but the JWTs are signed with the actual public key embeded in the certificate. Return codes are : -1 : Failure in extracting the pub key 1 : out_public_key succesfully populated

functions.name: jwt_db_authorize
functions.doc: The function will read the first param ( jwt_token ), extract the tag claim and then try to authenticate it against the DB secrets for the respective profile tag. In case of success, it populates the out_decoded_token pvar with the decoded JWT ( in plaintext format header_json.payload_json ) and the out_sip_username with the SIP username corresponding to that JWT profile.

functions.name: jwt_script_authorize
functions.doc: The function will read the first param ( jwt_token ), decode it and then try to validate it against the provided key. If the JWT decoding is succesful, the out_decoded_token pvar will be populated. Return codes are : -2 : Failure in decoding the JWT ( out_decoded_token will not be populated ) -1 : Failure in validating the JWT ( out_decoded_token will be populated ) 1 : JWT succesfully validated with the key ( out_decoded_token will be populated )

params.name: advertised_contact
params.doc: Contact to use in generated messages for UA session started with the MI function.

params.name: b2b_key_prefix
params.doc: The string to use when generating the key ( it is inserted in the SIP messages as callid or to tag. It is useful to set this prefix if you use more instances of opensips B2BUA cascaded in the same architecture. Sometimes opensips B2BUA looks at the callid or totag to see if it has the format it uses to determine if the request was sent by it.

params.name: cachedb_key_prefix
params.doc: Prefix to use for every key set in the NoSQL database.

params.name: cachedb_url
params.doc: URL of a NoSQL database to be used. Only Redis is supported at the moment.

params.name: client_hsize
params.doc: The size of the hash table that stores the b2b client entities. It is the 2 logarithmic value of the real size.

params.name: cluster_id
params.doc: The ID of the cluster this instance belongs to. Setting this parameter enables clustering support for the OpenSIPS B2BUA by replicating the B2B entities (B2B dialogs) between instances. This also ensures restart persistency through the clusterer module's data "sync" mechanism.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: The B2B modules have support for the 3 type of database storage

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The name of the table that will be used for storing B2B entities

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL. It is not compulsory, if not set data is not stored in database.

params.name: passthru_prack
params.doc: Exported by `b2b_entities`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: script_reply_route
params.doc: The name of the b2b script route that will be called when B2B replies are received.

params.name: script_req_route
params.doc: The name of the b2b script route that will be called when B2B requests are received.

params.name: server_hsize
params.doc: The size of the hash table that stores the b2b server entities. It is the 2 logarithmic value of the real size.

params.name: ua_default_timeout
params.doc: Default timeout, in seconds, for UA session started with the function or the MI function. After this interval a BYE will be sent and the session will be deleted.

params.name: update_period
params.doc: The time interval at which to update the info in database.

functions.name: ua_session_reply
functions.doc: Sends a reply for a UA session started with the function or the MI function.

functions.name: ua_session_server_init
functions.doc: This function initializes a new UA session by processing an initial INVITE. Further requests/replies received belonging to this session will only be handled via the event.

functions.name: ua_session_terminate
functions.doc: Terminate a UA session started with the function or the MI function.

functions.name: ua_session_update
functions.doc: Sends a sequential request for a UA session started with the function or the MI function.

params.name: b2bl_early_update
params.doc: Allow bridging of calls in early stage by issuing a "UPDATE" request

params.name: b2bl_from_spec_param
params.doc: The name of the pseudo variable for storing the new From header. The PV must be set before calling b2b_init_request .

params.name: b2bl_th_init_timeout
params.doc: Call setup timeout for topology hiding scenario.

params.name: cachedb_key_prefix
params.doc: Prefix to use for every key set in the NoSQL database.

params.name: cachedb_url
params.doc: URL of a NoSQL database to be used. Only Redis is supported at the moment.

params.name: cleanup_period
params.doc: The time interval at which to search for an hanged b2b context. A session is considered expired if the duration of a session exceeds its defined lifetime. At that moment, BYE is sent in all the dialogs from that context and the context is deleted.

params.name: contact_user
params.doc: If set to 1, adds user from From: header to generated Contact:

params.name: custom_headers
params.doc: A list of SIP header names delimited by ';' that should be passed from the dialog of one side to the other side. There are a number of headers that are passed by default. They are: Max-Forwards (it is decreased by 1) Content-Type Supported Allow Proxy-Require Session-Expires Min-SE Require RSeq If you wish some other headers to be passed also you should define them by setting this parameter.

params.name: custom_headers_regexp
params.doc: Regexp to search SIP header by names that should be passed from the dialog of one side to the other side. There are a number of headers that are passed by default. They are: Max-Forwards (it is decreased by 1) Content-Type Supported Allow Proxy-Require Session-Expires Min-SE Require RSeq If you wish some other headers to be passed also you should define them by setting this parameter.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: The B2B modules have support for the 3 type of database storage

params.name: db_table
params.doc: Name of the database table to be used

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table that stores the session entities.

params.name: init_callid_hdr
params.doc: The module offers the possibility to insert the original callid in a header in the generated Invites. If you want this, set this parameter to the name of the header in which to insert the original callid.

params.name: max_duration
params.doc: The maximum duration of a call.

params.name: old_entity_term_delay
params.doc: When the b2b_bridge_request is being used with the late_bye flag, this parameter can delay the moment when the BYE is being sent to the terminating entity. Thus, instead of terminating it when the new entity is established, the BYE is delayed with the value of this param, expressed in seconds.

params.name: script_reply_route
params.doc: The name of the script route to be called when replies belonging to an ongoing B2B session are received.

params.name: script_req_route
params.doc: The name of the script route to be called when requests belonging to an ongoing B2B session are received.

params.name: server_address
params.doc: The IP address of the machine that will be used as Contact in the generated messages. This is compulsory only when OpenSIPS starts a call from the middle. For scenarios triggered by received calls, if it is not set, it is constructed dynamically from the socket where the initiating request was received. This socket will be used to send all the requests, replies for that session. This parameter support Pseudo-Variables.

params.name: update_period
params.doc: The time interval at which to update the info in database.

functions.name: b2b_bridge
functions.doc: This function bridges two entities, in the context of an existing B2B session (the initial entities are already connected). At least one of the two entities has to be a new client entity.

functions.name: b2b_bridge_request
functions.doc: This function will bridge an initial INVITE with one of the particapnts from an existing b2b session.

functions.name: b2b_bridge_retry
functions.doc: This function can be used to retry a failed bridging action by contacting a new destination. A new client entity must be created before running this function with .

functions.name: b2b_client_new
functions.doc: This function creates a new client entity (dialog where OpenSIPS acts as a UAC) to be used for initializing a new B2B session or for a bridge action. The function can be used before calling or .

functions.name: b2b_delete_entity
functions.doc: This function deletes the entity that sent the current request.

functions.name: b2b_end_dlg_leg
functions.doc: This function sends a BYE request to the entity that sent the current request. It is not required to also call in order to delete the current entity.

functions.name: b2b_handle_reply
functions.doc: This function processes the received reply by taking the appropriate actions for the current state of the ongoing B2B session (pass reply to peer, send INVITE or ACK to comeplete an ongoing bridge action etc.). The function should be called for all replies, if a b2b_logic reply route is defined.

functions.name: b2b_init_request
functions.doc: This function initializes a new B2B session based on an initial INVITE. A new server entity and a new client entity must be created before running this function, with and , respectively. These are the initial entities to be connected and further scenario logic can be implemented in the b2b_logic dedicated routes.

functions.name: b2b_pass_request
functions.doc: This function passes a request belonging to an existing B2B session to the peer entity. The function should be called for all requests unless a different action is required to implement the scenario logic (eg. a bridge action).

functions.name: b2b_send_reply
functions.doc: This function sends a reply to the entity that sent the current request.

functions.name: b2b_server_new
functions.doc: This function creates a new server entity (dialog where OpenSIPS acts as a UAS) to be used for initializing a new B2B session. It should only be used for initial INVITES, before calling .

functions.name: b2b_trigger_scenario
functions.doc: This function triggers a certain scenario from routing script, e.g. out-of-dialog REFERs.

It will bridge the current "appearance" call with the existing "shared" call and the old "appearance" call will be disconnected (see the call from alice2 in the above diagram).

params.name: enable
params.doc: Even when the module is loaded, benchmarking is not enabled per default. This variable may have three different values: -1 - Globally disable benchmarking 0 - Enable per-timer enabling. Single timers are inactive by default and can be activated through the MI interface as soon as that feature is implemented. 1 - Globally enable benchmarking

params.name: granularity
params.doc: Logging normally is not done for every reference to the log_timer() function, but only every n'th call. n is defined through this variable. A sensible granularity seems to be 100.

params.name: loglevel
params.doc: Set the log level for the benchmark logs. These levels should be used: -3 - L_ALERT -2 - L_CRIT -1 - L_ERR 1 - L_WARN 2 - L_NOTICE 3 - L_INFO 4 - L_DBG

functions.name: bm_log_timer
functions.doc: This function logs the timer with the given ID. The following data are logged: Last msgs is the number of calls in the last logging interval. This equals the granularity variable. Last sum is the accumulated duration in the current logging interval (i.e. for the last granularity calls). Last min is the minimum duration between start/log_timer calls during the last interval. Last max - maximum duration. Last average is the average duration between bm_start_timer() and bm_log_timer() since the last logging. Global msgs number of calls to log_timer. Global sum total duration in microseconds. Global min ... You get the point. :) Global max also obvious. Global avg possibly the most interesting value.

functions.name: bm_start_timer
functions.doc: Start timer name . A later call to bm_log_timer() logs this timer..

params.name: connect_timeout
params.doc: The timeout in ms that will be triggered in case a connection attempt fails.

params.name: exec_threshold

params.name: query_retries

params.name: query_timeout
params.doc: The timeout in ms that will be triggered in case a Cassandra query takes too long.

params.name: rd_consistency_level
params.doc: The consistency level desired for write operations. Options are : all - Returns the record after all replicas have responded. The read operation will fail if a replica does not respond. quorum - Returns the record after a quorum of replicas from all datacenters has responded. local_quorum - Returns the record after a quorum of replicas in the current datacenter as the coordinator has reported. Avoids latency of inter-datacenter communication. one - Returns a response from the closest replica, as determined by the snitch. By default, a read repair runs in the background to make the other replicas consistent. two - Returns the most recent data from two of the closest replicas. three - Returns the most recent data from three of the closest replicas. local_one - Returns a response from the closest replica in the local datacenter. serial - Allows reading the current (and possibly uncommitted) state of data without proposing a new addition or update. If a SERIAL read finds an uncommitted transaction in progress, it will commit the transaction as part of the read. Similar to QUORUM. local_serial - Same as SERIAL, but confined to the datacenter. Similar to LOCAL_QUORUM. Default value is one .

params.name: wr_consistency_level
params.doc: The consistency level desired for write operations. Options are : all - A write must be written to the commit log and memtable on all replica nodes in the cluster for that partition. each_quorum - Strong consistency. A write must be written to the commit log and memtable on a quorum of replica nodes in each datacenter. quorum - A write must be written to the commit log and memtable on a quorum of replica nodes across all datacenters. local_quorum - Strong consistency. A write must be written to the commit log and memtable on a quorum of replica nodes in the same datacenter as the coordinator. Avoids latency of inter-datacenter communication. one - A write must be written to the commit log and memtable of at least one replica node. two - A write must be written to the commit log and memtable of at least two replica node. three - A write must be written to the commit log and memtable of at least three replica node. local_one - A write must be sent to, and successfully acknowledged by, at least one replica node in the local datacenter. any - A write must be written to at least one node. If all replica nodes for the given partition key are down, the write can still succeed after a hinted handoff has been written. If all replica nodes are down at write time, an ANY write is not readable until the replica nodes for that partition have recovered. Default value is one .

params.name: cachedb_url
params.doc: The urls of the server groups that OpenSIPS will connect to in order to use the from script cache_store,cache_fetch, etc operations. It can be set more than one time. The prefix part of the URL will be the identifier that will be used from the script. The format of the URL is couchbase[:identifier]://[username:password@]IP:Port/bucket_name

params.name: exec_threshold

params.name: lazy_connect
params.doc: Delay connecting to a bucket until the first time it is used. Connecting to many buckets at startup can be time consuming. This option allows for faster startup by delaying connections until they are needed. This option can be dangerous for untested bucket configurations/settings. Always test first without lazy_connect. This option will show errors in the log during the first access made to a bucket. Default is 0 ( Connect to all buckets on startup )

params.name: timeout
params.doc: The max duration in microseconds that a couchbase op is expected to last. Default is 3000000 ( 3 seconds )

params.name: cache_clean_period

params.name: ccf_skill_column
params.doc: Name to be used for the "skill" column in the flows table.

params.name: chat_dispatch_policy
params.doc: A parameter to tell what should be the policy on dispatching the chat/MSRP sessions to the agents, considering that an agent may handle multiple such sessions/chats in the same time.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: SQL address to the DB server -- database specific. This must be the Database holding the provisioning tables (cc_flows, cc_agents and cc_calls tables).

params.name: internal_call_dispatching
params.doc: A parameter to tell if the internal/buit-in call dispatching to agent should be used or not. If enabled, the module will automatically dispatch (by itself) the queued/incoming calls to the available agents. If disabled, the module will not do such dispaching by itself and it is expected to use the MI command to dispatch the queued calls to agents. This allows the implementation of an external, custom dispatching logic. The value of this setting may be changed during runtime via the MI command.

params.name: queue_pos_param
params.doc: The name of an SIP URI parameter to be used to report the position in the waiting queue when sending the call to media server for onwait/queue playback. The position 0 means it is the next call to be delivered to an agent.

params.name: reject_on_no_agents
params.doc: A parameter to tell if an incoming call should be rejected or quueued if there are no logged in agents. Basically this allows call queueing on flows with no agents yet.

params.name: rt_db_url
params.doc: SQL address/URL of the DB server (database specific) where the runtime tables (non provisioning tables) are located. The runtime tables are the tables populated by OpenSIPS with data learned during runtime. To be more specific, the only runtime table we have so far is the "cc_calls" table.

params.name: wrapup_time
params.doc: Time for an agent between finishing a call and receiving the next call from the system. Even if there are queued calls, the module will not deliver call to agent during this wrapup interval.

functions.name: cc_agent_login
functions.doc: This function sets the login (on or off) state for an agent.

functions.name: cc_handle_call
functions.doc: This must be used only for initial INVITE requests - the function pushes the call to be handled by the call center module (via a certain flow/queue).

params.name: call_limit_avp
params.doc: Specification of the AVP which holds an optional application defined call limit. When this is set, it will be passed to the CallControl application and if the limit is reached the call_control function will return an error code of -4.

params.name: call_token_avp
params.doc: Specification of the AVP which holds an optional application defined token. This token will be used to check if two calls with the same CallID actually refer to the same call. If call_control() is called multiple times for the same call (thus same CallID) the token needs to be the same or call_control will return -3 error, indicating that the CallID is duplicated.

params.name: canonical_uri_avp
params.doc: Specification of the AVP which holds an optional application defined canonical request URI. When this is set, it will be used as the destination when computing the call price, otherwise the request URI will be used. This is useful when the username of the ruri needs to have a different, canonical form in the rating engine computation than it has in the ruri.

params.name: disable
params.doc: Boolean flag that specifies if callcontrol should be disabled. This is useful when you want to use the same OpenSIPS configuration in two different context, one using callcontrol, the other not. In the case callcontrol is disabled, calls to the call_control() function will return a code indicating that there is no limit associated with the call, allowing the use of the same configuration without changes.

params.name: diverter_avp
params.doc: Specification of the AVP which holds an optional application defined diverter SIP URI. When this is set, it will be used by the rating engine as the billing party when finding the rates to apply to a given call, otherwise, the caller's URI taken from the From field will be used. When set, this AVP should contain a value in the form user@domain (no sip: prefix should be used).

params.name: init
params.doc: This parameter is used to describe custom call control initialize messages. It represents a list of key value pairs and has the following format:

params.name: prepaid_account_flag
params.doc: The flag that is used to specify whether the account making the call is prepaid or postpaid. Setting this to a non-null value will determine the module to pass the flag's value to the external application. This will allow the external application to compare OpenSIPS's and the rating engine's views on whether the account calling is prepaid or not and take appropriate action if they conflict. The flag should be set from the OpenSIPS configuration for a prepaid account and reset for a postpaid one.

params.name: signaling_ip_avp
params.doc: Specification of the AVP which holds the IP address from where the SIP signaling originated. If this AVP is set it will be used to get the signaling IP address, else the source IP address from where the SIP message was received will be used. This AVP is meant to be used in cases where there are more than one proxy in the call setup path and the proxy that actually starts callcontrol doesn't receive the SIP messages directly from the UA and it cannot determine the NAT IP address from where the signaling originated. In such a case attaching a SIP header at the first proxy and then copying that header's value into the signaling_ip_avp on the proxy that starts callcontrol will allow it to get the correct NAT IP address from where the SIP signaling originated.

params.name: socket_name
params.doc: It is the path to the filesystem socket where the callcontrol application listens for commands from the module.

params.name: socket_timeout
params.doc: How much time (in milliseconds) to wait for an answer from the callcontrol application.

params.name: start
params.doc: This parameter is used to describe custom call control start messages. It represents a list of key value pairs and has the following format:

params.name: stop
params.doc: This parameter is used to describe custom call control stop messages. It represents a list of key value pairs and has the following format:

functions.name: call_control
functions.doc: Trigger the use of callcontrol for the dialog started by the INVITE for which this function is called (the function should only be called for the first INVITE of a call). Further in-dialog requests will be processed automatically using internal bindings into the dialog state machine, allowing callcontrol to update its internal state as the dialog progresses, without any other intervention from the script.

params.name: match_param
params.doc: The parameter used to match the different calls together. This is mainly using in the param mode, but it is also used internally to store different values inside the transferred dialog - make sure it does not overlap with existing dialog values.

params.name: mode
params.doc: This parameter can be used to change the mode that the module uses to match a transferred leg. Supported values are: param / 0 - when doing a blind transfer, the destination sent in the refer message will contain a parameter used to identify the dialog that is being replaced. this parameter will be automatically removed when the new call is received. manual / 1 - the user will create its own logic to match the new calls, and will call the function to make OpenSIPS aware of the pair. Note that this mode does not handle automatically the Notify refer either, so you also have to use the function to handle them. callid / 2 - similar to the param value, except that instead of storing in the Request URI the dialog id of the call to be transfered, the actual callid is used as identifier.

functions.name: call_attended_transfer
functions.doc: This function triggers an attended call transfer by sending a REFER message during an ongoing call. The function needs to be run inside the context of the dialog you are transferring.

functions.name: call_blind_replace
functions.doc: When manual mode is used, this function is called to create a mapping between the transferring call and the transferred call. It should be called when OpenSIPS receives a new call that is transferring an existing call.

functions.name: call_blind_transfer
functions.doc: This function triggers a blind call transfer by sending a REFER message during an ongoing call. The function needs to be run inside the context of the dialog you are transferring.

functions.name: call_transfer_notify
functions.doc: When manual mode is used, this function should be called on in-dialog NOTIFY requests for an Event: refer header, to handle them accordingly.

params.name: carrier_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the carrier id.

params.name: carrier_id_col
params.doc: The name of the column in the carrier table containing the carrier id.

params.name: carrier_name_col
params.doc: The name of the column in the carrier table containing the carrier name.

params.name: carrier_table
params.doc: The name of the table containing the existing carriers, consisting of the ids and corresponding names.

params.name: comment_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing an optional comment (useful in large routing tables) The comment is also displayed by the fifo cmd "cr_dump_routes".

params.name: config_file
params.doc: Specifies the path to the config file.

params.name: config_source
params.doc: Specifies whether the module loads its config data from a file or from a database. Possible values are file or db.

params.name: db_failure_table
params.doc: Name of the table where the failure routing data is stored.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: Name of the table where the routing data is stored.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Url to the database containing the routing data.

params.name: default_tree
params.doc: The name of the carrier tree used per default (if the current subscriber has no preferred tree)

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the rule domain. You can define several routing domains to have different routing rules. Maybe you use domain 0 for normal routing and domain 1 if domain 0 failed.

params.name: failure_carrier_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the carrier id.

params.name: failure_comment_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing an optional comment.

params.name: failure_domain_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the rule domain. You can define several routing domains to have different routing rules. Maybe you use domain 0 for normal routing and domain 1 if domain 0 failed.

params.name: failure_flags_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the flags.

params.name: failure_host_name_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the host name of the last routing destination.

params.name: failure_id_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the id identifier.

params.name: failure_mask_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the flags mask.

params.name: failure_next_domain_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the next routing domain.

params.name: failure_reply_code_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the reply code.

params.name: failure_scan_prefix_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the scan prefixes. Scan prexies define the matching portion of a phone number, e.g. we have the scan prefixes 49721 and 49, the called number is 49721913740, it matches 49721, because the longest match is taken. If no prefix matches, the number is not failure routed. To prevent this, an empty prefix value of could be added.

params.name: fallback_default
params.doc: This parameter defines the behaviour when using user-based tree lookup. If the user has a non-existing tree set and fallback_default is set to 1, the default tree is used. Otherwise, cr_user_rewrite_uri returns an error.

params.name: flags_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the flags.

params.name: id_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the id identifier.

params.name: mask_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the flags mask.

params.name: prob_column
params.doc: Name of column containing probability. The probability value is used to distribute the traffic between several gateways. Let's say 70 % of the traffic shall be routed to gateway A, the other 30 % shall be routed to gateway B, we define a rule for gateway A with a prob value of 0.7 and a rule for gateway B with a prob value of 0.3.

params.name: rewrite_host_column
params.doc: Name of column containing rewrite host value. An empty field represents a blacklist entry, anything else is put as domain part into the Request URI of the SIP message.

params.name: rewrite_prefix_column
params.doc: Name of column containing rewrite prefixes. Here you can define a rewrite prefix for the localpart of the SIP URI.

params.name: rewrite_suffix_column
params.doc: Name of column containing rewrite suffixes. Here you can define a rewrite suffix for the localpart of the SIP URI.

params.name: scan_prefix_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the scan prefixes. Scan prefixes define the matching portion of a phone number, e.g. when we have the scan prefixes 49721 and 49, the called number is 49721913740, it matches 49721, because the longest match is taken. If no prefix matches, the number is not routed. To prevent this, an empty prefix value of could be added.

params.name: strip_column
params.doc: Name of the column containing the number of digits to be stripped of the userpart of an URI before prepending rewrite_prefix.

params.name: subscriber_carrier_col
params.doc: The name of the column in the subscriber table containing the carrier id of the subscriber.

params.name: subscriber_domain_col
params.doc: The name of the column in the subscriber table containing the domain of the subscriber.

params.name: subscriber_table
params.doc: The name of the table containing the subscribers

params.name: subscriber_user_col
params.doc: The name of the column in the subscriber table containing the usernames.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: When using tree lookup per user, this parameter specifies whether to use the domain part for user matching or not.

functions.name: cr_next_domain
functions.detail: cr_next_domain(carrier, domain, prefix_matching, host, reply_code, dst_avp)
functions.doc: This function searches for the longest match for the user given in prefix_matching at the given domain in the given carrier failure tree. It tries to find a next domain matching the given host, reply_code and the message flags. The matching is done in this order: host, reply_code and then flags. The more wildcards in reply_code and the more bits used in flags, the lower the priority. Returns -1 if there is no data found or an empty next_domain on the longest match is found. Otherwise the next domain is stored in the given AVP. This function is only usable with prefix_matching containing a valid numerical only string.

functions.name: cr_prime_route
functions.doc: This function searches for the longest match for the user given in prefix_matching at the given domain in the given carrier tree. The Request URI is rewritten using rewrite_user and the given hash source and algorithm. Returns -1 if there is no data found or an empty rewrite host on the longest match is found. Otherwise the rewritten host is stored in the given AVP (if obmitted, the host is not stored in an AVP). This function is only usable with rewrite_user and prefix_matching containing a valid numerical only string. It uses the prime hash algorithm to calculate the hash values.

functions.name: cr_route
functions.doc: This function searches for the longest match for the user given in prefix_matching at the given domain in the given carrier tree. The Request URI is rewritten using rewrite_user and the given hash source and algorithm. Returns -1 if there is no data found or an empty rewrite host on the longest match is found. Otherwise the rewritten host is stored in the given AVP (if obmitted, the host is not stored in an AVP). This function is only usable with rewrite_user and prefix_matching containing a valid numerical only string. It uses the standard crc32 algorithm to calculate the hash values.

functions.name: cr_user_carrier
functions.doc: This function loads the carrier and stores it in an AVP. It cannot be used in the config file mode, as it needs a mapping of the given user to a certain carrier. The is derived from a database entry belonging to the user parameter. This mapping must be available in the table that is specified in the subscriber_table variable. This data is not cached in memory, that means for every execution of this function a database query will be done.

params.name: hash_file
params.doc: The config file name for that a hash value should be calculated on startup.

params.name: initial_probability
params.doc: The initial value of the probability.

params.name: lock_pool_size
params.doc: The number of dynamic script locks to be allocated at OpenSIPS startup. This number must be a power of 2. (i.e. 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 ...)

params.name: shv_hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table used to store the shared variables ($shv).

params.name: shvset
params.doc: Set the value of a shared variable ($shv(name)). The parameter can be set many times.

params.name: varset
params.doc: Set the value of a script variable ($var(name)). The parameter can be set many times.

functions.name: abort
functions.doc: Debugging function that aborts the server. Depending on the configuration of the server a core dump will be created.

functions.name: check_time_rec
functions.doc: The function returns a positive value if the specified time recurrence string matches the current time, or a negative value otherwise.

functions.name: get_accurate_time
functions.doc: Fetch the current Unix time epoch with microsecond precision. Optionally, print this value as a floating point number (3rd parameter).

functions.name: get_dynamic_lock
functions.doc: Acquire the dynamic lock corresponding to "key". In case the lock is taken by another process, script execution will halt until the lock is released. Attempting to acquire the lock a second time by the same process, without releasing it first, will result in a deadlock.

functions.name: get_static_lock
functions.doc: Acquire the static lock which corresponds to "key". In case the lock is taken by another process, script execution will halt until the lock is released. Attempting to acquire the lock a second time by the same process, without releasing it first, will result in a deadlock.

functions.name: pkg_status
functions.doc: Debugging function that dumps the status for the private (PKG) memory. This information is logged to the default log facility, depending on the general log level and the memlog setting. You need to compile the server with activated memory debugging to get detailed informations.

functions.name: rand_event
functions.doc: Generates a random floating point value between 0 - 100 and returns true if the value is less or equal to the currently set probability. If "probability" parameter is given, it will override the global parameter set by .

functions.name: rand_get_prob
functions.doc: Return the current probability setting, e.g. for logging purposes.

functions.name: rand_reset_prob
functions.doc: Reset the probability back to the value.

functions.name: rand_set_prob
functions.doc: Set the probability of the decision.

functions.name: release_dynamic_lock
functions.doc: Release the dynamic lock corresponding to "key". Nothing will happen if the lock is not acquired.

functions.name: release_static_lock
functions.doc: Release the static lock corresponding to "key". Nothing will happen if the lock is not acquired.

functions.name: set_count
functions.doc: Counts the number of values of a given variable. It makes sense to call this function only for variables that can take more values (AVPs, headers).

functions.name: set_select_weight
functions.doc: This function selects an element from a set formed by the integer values of the given "int_list_var" variable. It applies the genetic algorithm - roulette-wheel selection to choose an element from a set. The probability of selecting a certain element is proportionate with its weight. It will return the index of that selected element.

functions.name: shm_status
functions.doc: Debugging function that dumps the status for the shared (SHM) memory. This information is logged to the default log facility, depending on the general log level and the memlog setting. You need to compile the server with activated memory debugging to get detailed informations.

functions.name: shuffle_avps
functions.doc: Randomly shuffles AVPs with name .

functions.name: sleep
functions.doc: Waits "time" seconds.

functions.name: strings_share_lock
functions.doc: A function used to test if two strings will generate the same hash value. Its purpose is to prevent deadlocks resulted when a process successively acquires two dynamic locks on two strings which happen to point to the same lock.

functions.name: ts_usec_delta
functions.doc: This function returns the absolute difference between the two given timestamps. The result is expressed as microseconds and can be returned as either string or integer.

functions.name: usleep
functions.doc: Waits "time" micro-seconds.

params.name: bind_ip
params.doc: IP used to bind the socket that communicates with the CGRateS engines. This is useful to set when the engine is runing in a local, secure LAN, and you want to use that network to communicate with your servers. The parameter is optional.

params.name: cgrates_engine
params.doc: This parameter is used to specify a CGRateS engine connection. The format is IP[:port] . The port is optional, and if missing, 2014 is used.

params.name: compat_mode
params.doc: Indicates whether OpenSIPS should use the old (compat_mode) CGRateS version API (pre-rc8).

params.name: max_async_connections
params.doc: The maximum number of simultaneous asynchronous connections to a CGRateS engine.

params.name: retry_timeout
params.doc: The number of seconds after which a disabled connection/engine is retried.

functions.name: cgrates_acc
functions.doc: cgrates_acc() starts an accounting session on the CGRateS engine for the current dialog. It also ends the session when the dialog is ended. This function requires a dialog, so in case create_dialog() was not previously used, it will internally call that function.

functions.name: cgrates_auth
functions.doc: cgrates_auth() does call authorization through using the CGRateS engine.

functions.name: cgrates_cmd
functions.doc: cgrates_cmd() can send arbitrary commands to the CGRateS engine.

params.name: cluster_id_col
params.doc: The name of the column to store the id of a cluster.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: Specifies whether the node information for the local instance, as well as other instances in the cluster, should be loaded from the database or configured in the script(see and ). A value of 0 means that DB is not used and the cluster topology in terms of node information will be discovered dynamically at runtime.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The name of the table storing the clustering information.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url.

params.name: description_col
params.doc: The name of the column containing a node description.

params.name: dispatch_jobs
params.doc: Enables the dispatching of jobs(processing replicated data packets) from the receiving TCP worker process to free opensips workers (including UDP, timer processes etc.).

params.name: enable_rerouting
params.doc: If packets should be rerouted via another node if a direct route to destination is unavailible. Disabling may improve stability in two-node topologies. Set it to zero to disable or to non-zero to enable it.

params.name: enable_stats
params.doc: If the statistics support should be enabled or not. Via statistic variables, the module provide information about the cluster nodes. Set it to zero to disable or to non-zero to enable it.

params.name: flags_col
params.doc: The name of the column containing the node flags.

params.name: id_col
params.doc: The name of the column storing an id for the table rows.

params.name: my_node_id
params.doc: The id of the local instance. This parameter must be equal to one of the node_id fields in the database.

params.name: my_node_info
params.doc: Node specification similar to the information provided by a row in the clusterer DB table corresponding to the local instance. This parameter can be set multiple times in order to include the local node in multiple clusters.

params.name: neighbor_node_info
params.doc: Node specification similar to the information provided by a row in the clusterer DB table corresponding to another instance in the cluster. This node will be the entry point in the cluster for the local instance in the dynamic node learning process. This parameter can be set multiple times to define multiple neigbors to connect to (or the same neighbor but in different clusters).

params.name: no_ping_retries_col
params.doc: The name of the column containing the maximum number of ping retries before the link with the neighbour node is considered down.

params.name: node_id_col
params.doc: The name of the column to store the id of an instance. The values must be greater than 0.

params.name: node_timeout
params.doc: The time in seconds to wait before pinging is restarted for a failed node.

params.name: ping_interval
params.doc: The interval in seconds between regular pings sent to a neighbour node.

params.name: ping_timeout
params.doc: The time in milliseconds to wait for a reply to a previously sent ping before retrying or considering the link with the neighbour node down. This is also the interval between successive retries if the send fails.

params.name: priority_col
params.doc: The name of the column storing the node priority to be chosen as next hop in case of same length(number of hops) paths when rerouting messages.

params.name: seed_fallback_interval
params.doc: Only relevant for "seed" nodes. The time, in seconds, to wait for a suitable donor node before falling back to a "synced" state, following a node restart or an MI cluster sync command.

params.name: sharing_tag
params.doc: The definition of a sharing tag. The sharing tag is managed by the clusterer module, but can be used (in terms of reading its state) by any module build on top of clusterer engine, like dialog or presence.

params.name: sip_addr_col
params.doc: The name of the column containing a SIP address for the node.

params.name: state_col
params.doc: The name of the column storing the state of the node(enabled/disabled).

params.name: sync_packet_size
params.doc: The maximum size of the BIN packets sent while doing data synchronization. This is only a suggested value as the actual size of the packets may be slightly larger.

params.name: sync_timeout
params.doc: The inteval, in seconds, since the last sync data packet received after which to consider the sync process as failed and revert the node to the not synced state.

params.name: url_col
params.doc: The name of the column containing the instance url. The values must be greater than 0.

functions.name: cluster_broadcast_req
functions.doc: This function has a similar behaviour to the cluster_send_req() function with the exception that the message is sent to all the nodes in the specified cluster.

functions.name: cluster_check_addr
functions.doc: This function checks whether the given IP address belongs to one of the nodes in the cluster.

functions.name: cluster_send_req
functions.doc: This function is used to send a generic, request-like message, containing custom data, to a specific node in a cluster, directly from the script. The message is not a "request" per se but according to the logic on the receiving side, that node can send back a reply. In order to correlate a received reply with the request sent out, the function returns, through the tag parameter, a randomly generated communication tag, which is sent along in the the original message, that can be checked against the tag received in a reply.

functions.name: cluster_send_rpl
functions.doc: This function is used to send a generic, reply-like message, containing custom data, to a specific node in a cluster, directly from the script. The message is marked as a "reply" so this function should ony be used for replying to a previously request-like message received. In order for the other node, which initially sent a request, to be able to correlate it with this reply, a communication tag, received along with the request, should be passed to the function.

params.name: compression_level
params.doc: Exported by `compression`; not documented in the module README.

functions.name: mc_compact
functions.doc: This function will realise four different things: headers which are not mandatory and are not in the whitelist will be removed, headers of same type will be merged together, separated by ',', header names which have a short form will be reduced to that short form (unless the n flag has been set) and SDP rtpmap attribute headers which contain a value lower than 96 will be removed, because they are not mandatory. Lumps are not affected by this function, because it is applied after all messages changes are processed. done. The mc_compact supported short forms are: c - Content-Type (RFC 3261) f - From (RFC 3261) i - Call-ID (RFC 3261) k - Supported (RFC 3261) l - Content-Length (RFC 3261) m - Contact (RFC 3261) s - Subject (RFC 3261) t - To (RFC 3261) v - Via (RFC 3261) x - Session-Expires (RFC 4028)

functions.name: mc_compress
functions.doc: This function will compress the current message as specified in the parameters. Keep in mind that the compression is done just before the message is sent, so that all your lumps can be applied.

functions.name: mc_decompress
functions.doc: This function does the reverse of mc_compress, meaning that it does base64 decoding and gzip/deflate decompression. Keep in mind that gzip decompression is a little bit more efficient because it is being known the size of the compressed buffer as against deflate which does not hold the size of the buffer, so the decompression will be made in a static buffer.

params.name: case_sensitive
params.doc: Tells if the username matching should be perform case sensitive or not. Set it to a non zero value to force a case sensitive handling of usernames.

params.name: cpl_bin_column
params.doc: Indicates the name of the column used for storing the the binary version of the cpl script (compiled version).

params.name: cpl_dtd_file
params.doc: Points to the DTD file describing the CPL grammar. The file name may include also the path to the file. This path can be absolute or relative (be careful the path will be relative to the starting directory of OpenSIPS).

params.name: cpl_xml_column
params.doc: Indicates the name of the column used for storing the the XML version of the cpl script.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: Indicates the name of the table that store the CPL scripts. This table must be locate into the database specified by db_url parameter. For more about the format of the CPL table please see the modules/cpl_c/init.mysql file.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: A SQL URL have to be given to the module for knowing where the database containing the table with CPL scripts is locates. If required a user name and password can be specified for allowing the module to connect to the database server.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: Indicates the name of the column used for storing the domain.

params.name: log_dir
params.doc: Points to a directory where should be created all the log file generated by the LOG CPL node. A log file per user will be created (on demand) having the name username.log.

params.name: lookup_append_branches
params.doc: Tells if the lookup tag should append branches (to do parallel forking) if user_location lookup returns more than one contact. Set it to a non zero value to enable parallel forking for location lookup tag.

params.name: lookup_domain
params.doc: Used by lookup tag to indicate where to perform user location. Basically this is the name of the usrloc domain (table) where the user registrations are kept.

params.name: proxy_recurse
params.doc: Tells for how many time is allow to have recurse for PROXY CPL node If it has value 2, when doing proxy, only twice the proxy action will be re-triggered by a redirect response; the third time, the proxy execution will end by going on REDIRECTION branch. The recurse feature can be disable by setting this parameter to 0

params.name: proxy_route
params.doc: Before doing proxy (forward), a script route can be executed. All modifications made by that route will be reflected only for the current branch.

params.name: realm_prefix
params.doc: Defines a prefix for the domain part which should be ignored in handling users and scripts.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: Indicates if the domain part of the URI should be used in user identification (otherwise only username part will be used).

params.name: username_column
params.doc: Indicates the name of the column used for storing the username.

functions.name: cpl_process_register
functions.doc: This function MUST be called only for REGISTER requests. It checks if the current REGISTER request is related or not with CPL script upload/download/ remove. If it is, all the needed operation will be done. For checking if the REGISTER is CPL related, the function looks fist to "Content-Type" header. If it exists and has a the mime type set to "application/cpl+xml" means this is a CPL script upload/remove operation. The distinction between to case is made by looking at "Content-Disposition" header; id its value is "script;action=store", means it's an upload; if it's "script;action=remove", means it's a remove operation; other values are considered to be errors. If no "Content-Type" header is present, the function looks to "Accept" header and if it contains the "*" or "application/cpl-xml" the request it will be consider one for downloading CPL scripts. The functions returns to script only if the REGISTER is not related to CPL. In other case, the function will send by itself the necessary replies (stateless - using sl), including for errors.

functions.name: cpl_process_register_norpl
functions.doc: Same as cpl_process_register without internally generating the reply. All information (script) is appended to the reply but without sending it out.

functions.name: cpl_run_script
functions.doc: Starts the execution of the CPL script. The user name is fetched from new_uri or requested uri or from To header -in this order- (for incoming execution) or from FROM header (for outgoing execution). Regarding the stateful/stateless message processing, the function is very flexible, being able to run in different modes (see below the"mode" parameter). Normally this function will end script execution. There is no guaranty that the CPL script interpretation ended when OpenSIPS script ended also (for the same INVITE ;-)) - this can happen when the CPL script does a PROXY and the script interpretation pause after proxying and it will be resume when some reply is received (this can happen in a different process of OpenSIPS).

params.name: auto_reload
params.doc: The auto-reload will close and reopen a Berkeley DB when the files inode has changed. The operation occurs only duing a query. Other operations such as insert or delete, do not invoke auto_reload.

params.name: journal_roll_interval
