params.doc: The journal_roll_interval will close and open a new log file. The roll operation occurs only at the end of writing a log, so it is not guaranteed to to roll 'on time'.

params.name: log_enable
params.doc: The log_enable boolean controls when to create journal files. The following operations can be journaled: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE. Other operations such as SELECT, do not. This journaling are required if you need to recover from a corrupt DB file. That is, bdb_recover requires these to rebuild the db file. If you find this log feature useful, you may also be interested in the METADATA_LOGFLAGS bitfield that each table has. It will allow you to control which operations to journal, and the destination (like syslog, stdout, local-file). Refer to bdblib_log() and documentation on METADATA.

params.name: cachedb_url
params.doc: Exported by `db_cachedb`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: delimiter
params.doc: Delimiter used to separate the values.

params.name: flush
params.doc: Enable or disable flushing after each write.

params.name: prefix
params.doc: The table name prefix. Can be a pseudo variable.

params.name: single_file
params.doc: Specifies if all the processes should dump the data into a single file.

params.name: suffix
params.doc: The suffix appended to the table name. Can be a pseudo variable.

params.name: SSL
params.doc: Whether or not to use SSL.

params.name: cap_insert_update
params.doc: Whether or not the server supports insert_update capabilities.

params.name: cap_last_inserted_id
params.doc: Whether or not the server supports last_inserted_id capabilities.

params.name: cap_raw_query
params.doc: Whether or not the server supports raw queries.

params.name: cap_replace
params.doc: Whether or not the server supports replace capabilities.

params.name: disable_expect
params.doc: Disables automatic 'Expect: 100-continue' behavior in libcurl for requests over 1024 bytes in size. This can help reduce latency by saving a network round-trip for large records. For more information on this behavior please seee rfc2616 section 8.2.3.

params.name: field_delimiter
params.doc: Character to be used to delimit fields in the reply.Only one char may be set.

params.name: quote_delimiter
params.doc: Character to be used to quote fields that require quoting in the reply.Only one char may be set.

params.name: row_delimiter
params.doc: Character to be used to delimit rows in the reply.Only one char may be set.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: The maximum number of milliseconds that the HTTP ops are allowed to last

params.name: value_delimiter
params.doc: The delimiter used to separate multiple fields of a single variable (see ). Only one char may be set.

params.name: exec_query_threshold
params.doc: If queries take longer than 'exec_query_threshold' microseconds, warning messages will be written to logging facility.

params.name: max_db_queries
params.doc: The maximum number of retries to execute a failed query due to connections problems. If this parameter is set improperly, it is set to default value.

params.name: max_db_retries
params.doc: The maximum number of database connection retries. If this parameter is set improperly, it is set to default value.

params.name: ps_max_col_size
params.doc: The maximum size of a column's data, when fetched using prepared statements. Particularly relevant for variable-length data, such as CHAR, BLOB, etc.

params.name: timeout_interval
params.doc: Time interval after which a connection attempt (read or write request) is aborted. The value counts three times, as several retries are done from the driver before it gives up.

params.name: use_tls
params.doc: Setting this parameter will allow you to use TLS for MySQL connections. In order to enable TLS for a specific connection, you can use the " tls_domain= dom_name" URL parameter in the db_url of the respective OpenSIPS module. This should be placed at the end of the URL after the '?' character. Additionally, the query string may include the " tls_opts= PKEY,CERT,CA,CA_DIR,CIPHERS" CSV parameter, in order to control/limit the amount of TLS options passed to the TLS library.

params.name: reconnect
params.doc: Timeout value for connect (create session) operation.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Timeout value for any operation with BD.

params.name: exec_query_threshold
params.doc: If queries take longer than 'exec_query_threshold' microseconds, warning messages will be written to logging facility.

params.name: max_db_queries
params.doc: The maximum number of database queries to be executed. If this parameter is set improperly, it is set to default value.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: The number of seconds the PostgreSQL library waits to connect and query the server. If the connection does not succeed within the given timeout, the connection fails.

params.name: use_tls
params.doc: Parameter to control the way the SSL support is used when connecting to the Postgres server, as follows:

params.name: alloc_limit
params.doc: Since the library does not support a function to return the number of rows in a query, this number is obtained using "count(*)" query. If we use multiple processes there is the risk ,since "count(*)" query and the actual "select" query, the number of rows in the result query to have changed, so realloc will be needed if the number is bigger. Using alloc_limit parameter you can specify the number with which the number of allocated rows in the result is raised.

params.name: load_extension
params.doc: This parameter enables extension loading, similiar to ".load" functionality in sqlite3, extenions like sqlite3-pcre which enables REGEX function. In order to use this functionality you must specify the library path (.so file) and the entry point which represents the function to be called by the sqlite library (read more at sqlite load_extension official documentation), separated by ";" delimiter. The entry point paramter can miss, so you won't need to use the delimitier in this case.

params.name: buffer_size
params.doc: Size of the buffer used to read the text file.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: Set caching mode (0) or non-caching mode (1). In caching mode, data is loaded at startup. In non-caching mode, the module check every time a table is requested whether the corresponding file on disk has changed, and if yes, will re-load table from file.

params.name: auto_reconnect
params.doc: Turns on or off the auto_reconnect mode.

params.name: use_escape_common
params.doc: Escape values in query using internal escape_common() function. It escapes single quote ''', double quote '"', backslash '\', and NULL characters.

params.name: db_max_consec_retrys
params.doc: Exported by `db_virtual`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: db_probe_time
params.doc: Exported by `db_virtual`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: db_urls
params.doc: Exported by `db_virtual`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: cachedb_url
params.doc: Enables distributed dialog profiles and specifies the backend that should be used by the CacheDB interface.

params.name: call_id_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the dialogs' callid.

params.name: cluster_auto_sync
params.doc: Specifies whether to automatically issue a sync request (for dialogs marked with a sharing tag in backup state) when a node becomes reachable. A value of 1 means enabled and 0 disabled.

params.name: db_flush_vals_profiles
params.doc: Pushes dialog values, profiles and flags into the database along with other dialog state information (see db_mode 1 and 2).

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: Describe how to push into the DB the dialogs' information from memory.

params.name: db_update_period
params.doc: The interval (seconds) at which to update dialogs' information if you chose to store the dialogs' info at a given interval. A too short interval will generate intensive database operations, a too large one will not notice short dialogs.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: If you want to store the information about the dialogs in a database a database url must be specified.

params.name: default_timeout
params.doc: The default dialog timeout (in seconds) if no custom one is set.

params.name: delete_delay
params.doc: The interval (seconds) to delay a dialog deletion / removal from memory AFTER its termination. Once terminated, the dialog will be kept in a read only state (no action, no changes), but it will still be able to match and route late in-dialog requests.

params.name: dialog_replication_cluster
params.doc: Specifies the cluster ID for dialog replication using the clusterer module. This enables sending and receiving all the dialog-related events (creation, update and deletion) in the cluster.

params.name: dlg_extra_hdrs
params.doc: A string containing the extra headers (full format, with EOH) to be added in the requests generated by the module (like BYEs).

params.name: dlg_id_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the dialogs' id information.

params.name: dlg_match_mode
params.doc: How the seqential requests should be matched against the known dialogs. The modes are a combination between matching based on a cookie (DID) stored as cookie in Record-Route header and the matching based on SIP elements (as in RFC3261).

params.name: enable_stats
params.doc: If the statistics support should be enabled or not. Via statistic variables, the module provide information about the dialog processing. Set it to zero to disable or to non-zero to enable it.

params.name: flags_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the dialogs' flags.

params.name: from_contact_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the caller's contact uri.

params.name: from_cseq_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the cseq from caller side.

params.name: from_route_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the route records from caller side (proxy to caller).

params.name: from_sock_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the information about the local interface receiving the traffic from caller.

params.name: from_tag_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the From tag from the Invite request.

params.name: from_uri_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the caller's sip address.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table internally used to keep the dialogs. A larger table is much faster but consumes more memory. The hash size must be a power of 2 number.

params.name: log_profile_hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table internally used to store profile->dialog associations. A larger table can provide more parallel operations but consumes more memory. The hash size is provided as the base 2 logarithm(e.g. log_profile_hash_size =4 means the table has 2^4 entries).

params.name: mflags_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the dialogs' module flags.

params.name: options_ping_interval
params.doc: The interval (seconds) at which OpenSIPS will generate in-dialog OPTIONS pings for one or both of the involved parties.

params.name: profile_no_value_prefix
params.doc: Specifies what prefix should be added to the profiles without value when they are inserted into CacheDB backed. This is only used when distributed profiles are enabled.

params.name: profile_replication_cluster
params.doc: Specifies the cluster ID for profile replication using the clusterer module. This enables sending and receiving the profile information (value, dialog count) in the cluster.

params.name: profile_size_prefix
params.doc: Specifies what prefix should be added to the entity that holds the profiles with value size in CacheDB backed. This is only used when distributed profiles are enabled.

params.name: profile_timeout
params.doc: Specifies how long a dialog profile should be kept in the CacheDB until it expires. This is only used when distributed profiles are enabled.

params.name: profile_value_prefix
params.doc: Specifies what prefix should be added to the profiles with value when they are inserted into CacheDB backed. This is only used when distributed profiles are enabled.

params.name: profiles_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the dialogs' profiles.

params.name: profiles_no_value
params.doc: List of names (alphanumerical/-/_) for profiles without values. Flags /b or /s allow sharing profiles between OpenSIPS instances using the clusterer module or a CacheDB backend, respectively.

params.name: profiles_with_value
params.doc: List of names (alphanumerical/-/_) for profiles with values. Flags /b or /s allow sharing profiles between OpenSIPS instances using the clusterer module or a CacheDB backend, respectively.

params.name: race_condition_timeout
params.doc: Exported by `dialog`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: reinvite_ping_interval
params.doc: The interval (seconds) at which OpenSIPS will generate in-dialog Re-INVITE pings for one or both of the involved parties.

params.name: replicate_profiles_buffer
params.doc: Used to specify the length of the buffer used by the binary replication, in bytes. Usually this should be big enough to hold as much data as possible, but small enough to avoid UDP fragmentation. The recommended value is the smallest MTU between all the replication instances.

params.name: replicate_profiles_check
params.doc: Timer in seconds, used to specify how often the module should check whether old, replicated profiles values are obsolete and should be removed. should replicate its profiles to the other instances.

params.name: replicate_profiles_expire
params.doc: Timer in seconds, used to specify when the profiles counters received from a different instance should no longer be taken into account. This is used to prevent obsolete values, in case an instance stops replicating its counters.

params.name: replicate_profiles_timer
params.doc: Timer in milliseconds, used to specify how often the module should replicate its profiles to the other instances.

params.name: rr_param
params.doc: Name of the Record-Route parameter to be added with the dialog cookie. It is used for fast dialog matching of the sequential requests.

params.name: sflags_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the dialogs' script flags.

params.name: start_time_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the dialogs' start time information.

params.name: state_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the dialogs' state information.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: If you want to store the information about the dialogs in a database a table name must be specified.

params.name: timeout_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the dialogs' timeout.

params.name: timer_bulk_del_no
params.doc: The number of dialogs that should be attempted to be deleted at the same time ( a single query ) from the DB back-end.

params.name: to_contact_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the callee's contact uri.

params.name: to_cseq_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the cseq from callee side.

params.name: to_route_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the route records from callee side (proxy to callee).

params.name: to_sock_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store information about the local interface receiving the traffic from callee.

params.name: to_tag_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the To tag from the 200 OK response to the Invite request, if present.

params.name: to_uri_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the calee's sip address.

params.name: vars_column
params.doc: The column's name in the database to store the dialogs' vars.

functions.name: create_dialog
functions.doc: The function creats the dialog for the currently processed request. The request must be an initial request. Optionally,the function also receives a string parameter, which specifies special behavior to be done for the current dialog.

functions.name: dlg_on_answer
functions.doc: The function arms a script route to be executed when the current dialog will be later answered. When the route will be executed, the dialog context will be exposed, but with no valid SIP message (just a phony one).

functions.name: dlg_on_hangup
functions.doc: The function arms a script route to be executed when the current dialog will be terminated. When the route will be executed, the dialog context will be exposed, but with no valid SIP message (just a phony one). Note that the dialog will be already terminated and there is nothing you can do about it besides reading data from its context.

functions.name: dlg_on_timeout
functions.doc: The function arms a script route to be executed when (and if) the current dialog will timeout (as duration). When the route will be executed, the dialog context will be exposed, but with no valid SIP message (just a phony one)

functions.name: dlg_send_sequential
functions.doc: Used to send an in-dialog request towards one if the dialog's legs. The function assumes that is runs inside a dialog context - if you are running it from a different context (such as an event_route), make sure you first load the dialog context using the function.

functions.name: fetch_dlg_value
functions.doc: Fetches from the dialog the value of attribute named name . The values attached to dialogs are dialog persistent and they can be accessed (read and write) for all requests belonging to the dialog.

functions.name: fix_route_dialog
functions.doc: The function forces an in dialog SIP message to contain the ruri, route headers and dst_uri, as specified by the internal data of the dialog it belongs to. The function will prevent the existence of bogus injected in-dialog requests ( like malicious BYEs )

functions.name: get_dialog_by_profile
functions.doc: The function looks up through the whole dialog table for dialogs configured to be within the provided dialog profile name, and optionally with the provided profile value. The function returns all the $DLG_ctx_json variables for the matched dialogs, storing them in the provided out_avp. The total number of matched dialogs is returned in the out_dlgs_no variable

functions.name: get_dialog_by_val
functions.doc: The function looks up through the whole dialog table for dialogs containing a $dlg_val with the provided name and value, and returns all the $DLG_ctx_json variables for the matched dialogs, storing them in the provided out_avp. The total number of matched dialogs is returned in the out_dlgs_no variable

functions.name: get_dialog_info
functions.doc: The function extracts a dialog value from another dialog. It first searches through all existing (ongoing) dialogs for all dialogs that have a dialog variable named "key" with the value "key_val" (so a dialog where $dlg_val(key)=="key_val"). If found, it returns the value of the dialog variable "attr" from all the founds dialog in the "avp" pseudo-variable, otherwise nothing is written in "avp", and a negative error code is returned.

functions.name: get_dialog_vals
functions.doc: The function fetches all the dialog variables of another dialog. It first searches through all existing (ongoing) dialogs based on the given SIP CallID. If found, it returns all the dialog variables as two parallel arrays of names and values (using the given variables "names" and "vals"). As these variables have to hold arrays, they must be AVPs.

functions.name: get_profile_size
functions.doc: Returns the number of dialogs belonging to a profile. If the profile supports values, the check can be reinforced to take into account a specific value - how many dialogs were inserted into the profile with a specific value. If not value is passed, only simply belonging of the dialog to the profile is checked. Note that the profile does not supports values, this will be silently discarded.

functions.name: is_dlg_flag_set
functions.doc: Returns true if the dialog flag named flag is set. The dialog flags are dialog persistent and they can be accessed (set and test) for all requests belonging to the dialog.

functions.name: is_in_profile
functions.doc: Checks if the current dialog belongs to a profile. If the profile supports values, the check can be reinforced to take into account a specific value - if the dialog was inserted into the profile for a specific value. If no value is passed, only simply belonging of the dialog to the profile is checked. Note that if the profile does not support values, this will be silently discarded.

functions.name: load_dialog_ctx
functions.doc: The function loads and switches to the context of the given dialog. The context of a dialog is given by the dialog flags, variables, profiles and any other value/state related to the dialog. By switching to the context of another dialog, you will see at the script level, by default, all the data from the new dialog.

functions.name: match_dialog
functions.doc: This function is to be used to match a sequential (in-dialog) request to an ongoing dialog.

functions.name: reset_dlg_flag
functions.doc: Resets the dialog flag named flag to false. The dialog flags are dialog persistent and they can be accessed (set and test) for all requests belonging to the dialog.

functions.name: set_dlg_flag
functions.doc: Sets the dialog flag named flag to true. The dialog flags are dialog persistent and they can be accessed (set and test) for all requests belonging to the dialog.

functions.name: set_dlg_profile
functions.doc: Inserts the current dialog into a profile. Note that if the profile does not support values, this will be silently discarded. A dialog may be inserted in the same profile multiple times.

functions.name: set_dlg_sharing_tag
functions.doc: Marks the current dialog with the sharing tag tag_name . From this point on, actions like in-dialog pinging, BYEs on timeout etc. will depend on the tag state(no action in "backup" state, normal operation in "active" state).

functions.name: store_dlg_value
functions.doc: Attaches to the dialog the value from the variable val under the name name . The values attached to dialogs are dialog persistent and they can be accessed (read and write) for all requests belonging to the dialog.

functions.name: test_and_set_dlg_flag
functions.doc: Atomically checks if the dialog flag named flag is equal to value . If true, changes the value with the opposite one. This operation is done under the dialog lock.

functions.name: unload_dialog_ctx
functions.doc: The function off-loads the loaded context of another dialog, exposing whatever dialog context was present before doing the load.

functions.name: unset_dlg_profile
functions.doc: Removes the current dialog from a profile.

functions.name: validate_dialog
functions.doc: The function checks the current received requests against the dialog (internal data) it belongs to. Performing several tests, the function will help to detect the bogus injected in-dialog requests (like malicious BYEs).

params.name: attrs_col
params.doc: The column name to store rule-specific attributes.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The default DB connection of the module, overriding the global 'db_default_url' setting. Once specified, partitions which are missing the 'db_url' property will inherit their URL from this value.

params.name: disabled_col
params.doc: The column name that indicates if the dialplan rule is disabled.

params.name: dpid_col
params.doc: The column name to store the dialplan ID group.

params.name: match_exp_col
params.doc: The column name to store the rule match expression.

params.name: match_flags_col
params.doc: The column name to store various matching flags. Currently 0 - case sensitive matching, 1 - case insensitive matching.

params.name: match_op_col
params.doc: The column name to store the type of matching of the rule.

params.name: partition
params.doc: Specify a new dialplan partition (data source). This parameter may be set multiple times. Each partition may have a specific "db_url" and "table_name". If not specified, these values will be inherited from , db_default_url or , respectively. The name of the default partition is 'default'.

params.name: pr_col
params.doc: The column name to store the priority of the corresponding rule from the table row. Smaller priority values have higher precedence.

params.name: repl_exp_col
params.doc: The column name to store the rule's replacement expression.

params.name: subst_exp_col
params.doc: The column name to store the rule's substitution expression.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: The default name of the table from which to load translation rules. Partitions which are missing the 'table_name' property will inherit their table name from this value.

params.name: timerec_col
params.doc: The column name that indicates an additional time recurrence check within the rule (column values are RFC 2445-compatible strings). The value format is identical to the input of the check_time_rec() function of the cfgutils module, including the optional use of logical operators linking multiple such strings into a larger expression.

functions.name: dp_translate
functions.doc: Will try to translate the src string into dest string according to the translation rules with dialplan ID equal to id.

params.name: algo_route
params.doc: Exported by `dispatcher`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: attrs_avp
params.doc: The name of the avp to contain the attributes string of the current destination. When a destination is selected, automatically, this AVP will provide the attributes string - this is an opaque string (from OpenSIPS point of view) : it is loaded from destination definition ( via DB) and blindly provided in the script. Setting this parameter will only change the default partition's attrs_avp. Use the partition parameter to create and alter other partitions.

params.name: attrs_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the attributes (opaque string) for destination uri.

params.name: cluster_id
params.doc: The ID of the cluster the module is part of. The clustering support is used in dispatcher module for two purposes: for sharing the status of the destinations and for controlling the pinging to destinations.

params.name: cluster_probing_mode
params.doc: This paramter controls how the probing/pinging should be done when using the clustering support. It is about which node in the cluster pings which gateway/destination.

params.name: cluster_sharing_tag
params.doc: The name of the sharing tag (as defined per clusterer modules) to control which node is responsible for perform the self-triggered actions in the module. Such actions may be the destination probing (see also the parameter) or sharing the changes in the destination status. If defined, only the node with active status of this tag will perform the actions (pinging and sharing status).

params.name: cnt_avp
params.doc: This is mainly for internal usage and represents the name of the avp storing the number of destination addresses kept in dst_avp avps. Setting this parameter will only change the default partition's cnt_avp. Use the partition parameter to create and alter other partitions.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The default DB connection of the module, overriding the global 'db_default_url' setting. Once specified, partitions which are missing the 'db_url' property will inherit their URL from this value.

params.name: description_col
params.doc: Exported by `dispatcher`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: destination_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the destination's sip uri.

params.name: ds_define_blacklist
params.doc: Defines a blacklist based on a dispatching setid from the 'default' partition. This list will contain the IPs (no port, all protocols) of the destinations matching the given setid. Use the 'partition' parameter if you want to define blacklists based on other partitions' sets.

params.name: ds_ping_from
params.doc: With this Method you can define the "From:"-Line for the request, sent to the failed gateways. This method is only available, if compiled with the probing of failed gateways enabled.

params.name: ds_ping_interval
params.doc: With this Method you can define the interval for sending a request to a failed gateway. This parameter is only used, when the TM-Module is loaded. If set to 0 , the pinging of failed requests is disabled.

params.name: ds_ping_maxfwd
params.doc: This parameter allows you to enforce a specific Max-Forward value for the SIP pinging requests generated by the Dispatcher modules. If not explicitly set, no value will be enforced and it let the Transaction Layer (TM module) to set a default Max-Forward value.

params.name: ds_ping_method
params.doc: With this Method you can define, with which method you want to probe the failed gateways. This method is only available, if compiled with the probing of failed gateways enabled.

params.name: ds_probing_list
params.doc: Defines a list of one or more setids that limits which destinations are probed if probing is active. This is useful when multiple proxies share the same dispatcher table, but you want to limit which ones are responsible for probing specific destinations.

params.name: ds_probing_mode
params.doc: Controls what gateways are tested to see if they are reachable. If set to 0, only the gateways with state PROBING are tested, if set to 1, all gateways are tested. If set to 1 and the response is 408 (timeout), an active gateway is set to PROBING state.

params.name: ds_probing_sock
params.doc: A socket description [proto:]host[:port] of the local socket (which is used by OpenSIPS for SIP traffic) to be used (if multiple) for sending the probing messages from.

params.name: ds_probing_threshhold
params.doc: Exported by `dispatcher`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: ds_probing_threshold
params.doc: If you want to set a gateway into probing mode, you will need a specific number of requests until it will change from "active" to probing. The number of attempts can be set with this parameter.

params.name: dst_avp
params.doc: This is mainly for internal usage and represents the name of the avp which will hold the list with addresses, in the order they have been selected by the chosen algorithm. If use_default is 1, the value of last dst_avp_id is the last address in destination set. The first dst_avp_id is the selected destinations. All the other addresses from the destination set will be added in the avp list to be able to implement serial forking. Setting this parameter will only change the default partition's dst_avp. Use the partition parameter to create and alter other partitions.

params.name: fetch_freeswitch_stats
params.doc: If enabled, FreeSWITCH destinations may have dynamic dispatching weights, refreshed at runtime, using the FreeSWITCH Event Socket Layer. For these destinations, an Event Socket Layer URL must be provisioned into the "weight" column, instead of an integer string. Some example values: "fs://:password@freeswitch.example.com" or "fs://user:password@127.0.0.1:8021" . The default ESL port is 8021.

params.name: grp_avp
params.doc: This is mainly for internal usage and represents the name of the avp storing the group id of the destination set. Good to have it for later usage or checks. Setting this parameter will only change the default partition's grp_avp. Use the partition parameter to create and alter other partitions.

params.name: hash_pvar
params.doc: String with PVs used for the hashing algorithm 7.

params.name: max_freeswitch_weight
params.doc: The maximum weight of a FreeSWITCH ESL-enabled destination. This value is also used during startup/reload, when no stats from FreeSWITCH are available yet.

params.name: options_reply_codes
params.doc: This parameter must contain a list of SIP reply codes separated by comma. The codes defined here will be considered as valid reply codes for OPTIONS messages used for pinging, apart for 200.

params.name: partition
params.doc: Define a new partition (data source) with the following properties: "db_url", "table_name", "dst_avp", "grp_avp", "cnt_avp", "sock_avp", "attrs_avp", "script_attrs", "ds_define_blacklist". All these properties are optional, having appropriate default values.

params.name: persistent_state
params.doc: Specifies whether the state column should be loaded at startup and flushed during runtime or not for the "default" partition.

params.name: priority_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the priority for destination uri.

params.name: probe_mode_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the probe_mode (as string) for destination.

params.name: pvar_algo_pattern
params.doc: This parameter is used by the PVAR(9) algorithm to specify the pseudovariable pattern used to detect the load of each destination. The name of the pseudovariable should contain the string %u , which will be internally replaced by the module with the uri of the destination. The string %i can also be used and will be replaced with the set ID of the destination (useful in cases where same uri exists in multiple sets).

params.name: script_attrs_avp
params.doc: Name of the avp to contain the script attributes string of the current destination. When a destination is selected, automatically, this AVP will provide the attributes string - this is an opaque string (from OpenSIPS point of view) : it is provided via the ds_push_script_attrs MI or SCRIPT function.

params.name: setid_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the gateway's group id.

params.name: setid_pvar
params.doc: The name of the PV where to store the set ID (group ID) when calling ds_is_in_list() without group parameter (third parameter).

params.name: sock_avp
params.doc: This is mainly for internal usage and represents the name of the avp storing the sockets to be used for the destination addresses kept in dst_avp avps. Setting this parameter will only change the default partition's sock_avp. Use the partition parameter to create and alter other partitions.

params.name: socket_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the socket (as string) for destination uri.

params.name: state_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the state of the destination uri.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: The default name of the table from which to load dispatcher destinations. Partitions which are missing the 'table_name' property will inherit their table name from this value.

params.name: weight_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the weight for destination uri.

functions.name: ds_count
functions.doc: Returns the number of active, inactive or probing destinations in a partition's set, or combinations between these properties.

functions.name: ds_get_script_attrs
functions.doc: Get the script attrs for the dispatcher entry defined by the URI, setid and partition.

functions.name: ds_is_in_list
functions.doc: This function returns true only if "ip" and "port" point to a host from the given dispatcher "set".

functions.name: ds_mark_dst
functions.doc: Mark the last used address from partition's destination set as inactive ("i"/"I"/"0"), active ("a"/"A"/"1") or probing ("p"/"P"/"2"). With this function, an automatic detection of failed gateways can be implemented. When an address is marked as inactive or probing, it will be ignored by and . If "partition" is omitted, the default partition will be used. This function is using the flags set in or .

functions.name: ds_next_domain
functions.doc: Takes the next destination address from the AVPs with id partition.'dst_avp_id' and sets the domain part of the request uri. If "partition" is omitted, the default partition will be used.This function is using the flags set in ds_select_dst or ds_select_domain.

functions.name: ds_next_dst
functions.doc: Takes the next destination address from the AVPs with id partition.'dst_avp_id' and sets the dst_uri (outbound proxy address). If "partition" is omitted, the default partition will be used.This function is using the flags set in ds_select_dst or ds_select_domain.

functions.name: ds_push_script_attrs
functions.doc: Set the script attrs for the dispatcher entry defined by IP, Port, setid and partition.

functions.name: ds_select_domain
functions.doc: The method selects a destination from addresses set and rewrites the hostname and port parts of the Request-URI ( $ru ). Its parameters have same meaning as in .

functions.name: ds_select_dst
functions.doc: The method selects a destination from the given set of addresses. It will overwrite the destination URI ( $du ) of a SIP request.

params.name: suffix
params.doc: The suffix to be appended to the end of the header field. You can use the parameter to specify additional parameters to be added to the header field, see the example.

functions.name: add_diversion
functions.doc: The function adds a new diversion header field before any other existing Diversion header field in the message (the newly added Diversion header field will become the topmost Diversion header field). The inbound (without any modifications done by the proxy server) Request-URI will be used as the Diversion URI.

params.name: blacklist_timeout
params.doc: The number of seconds that a failed DNS query will be kept in cache. Default is 3600.

params.name: cachedb_url
params.doc: The url of the key-value back-end that will be used for storing the DNS records.

params.name: attrs_col
params.doc: Exported by `domain`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: db_mode
params.doc: Exported by `domain`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Exported by `domain`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: domain_col
params.doc: Exported by `domain`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: domain_table
params.doc: Exported by `domain`; not documented in the module README.

functions.name: is_domain_local
functions.doc: This function checks if the domain contained in the first parameter is local.

functions.name: is_from_local
functions.doc: Checks based on domain table if host part of From header uri is one of the local domains that the proxy is responsible for. The argument is optional and if present it should contain a writable variable that will be populated with the attributes from the database.

functions.name: is_uri_host_local
functions.doc: If called from route or failure route block, checks based on domain table if host part of Request-URI is one of the local domains that the proxy is responsible for. If called from branch route, the test is made on host part of URI of first branch, which thus must have been appended to the transaction before is_uri_host_local() is called. The argument is optional and if present it should contain a writable variable that will be populated with the attributes from the database.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: This is URL of the database to be used.

params.name: domain_prefix_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP which contains a domain prefix.

params.name: domain_replacement_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP which contains a domain replacement.

params.name: domain_suffix_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP which contains a domain suffix.

params.name: dp_col_att
params.doc: Name of column containing the AVP's name. If the rule stored in this row triggers, than dp_can_connect() will add an AVP with that name.

params.name: dp_col_rule
params.doc: Name of column containing the domain policy rule name which is equal to the URI as published in the domain policy NAPTRs.

params.name: dp_col_type
params.doc: Name of column containing the domain policy rule type. In the case of federation names, this is "fed". For standard referrals according to draft-lendl-speermint-technical-policy-00, this is "std". For direct domain lookups, this is "dom".

params.name: dp_col_val
params.doc: Name of column containing the value for AVPs created by dp_can_connect().

params.name: dp_table
params.doc: Name of table containing the local support domain policy setup.

params.name: port_override_avp
params.doc: This parameter defines the name of the AVP where dp_apply_policy() will look for an override port number.

params.name: send_socket_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP which contains a send_socket. The format of the send socket (the payload of this AVP) must be in the format [proto:]ip_address[:port]. The function dp_apply_policy will look for this AVP and if defined, it will force the send socket to its value (smilar to the force_send_socket core function).

params.name: transport_override_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP which contains the override transport setting.

functions.name: dp_apply_policy
functions.doc: This function sets the destination URI according to the policy returned from the dp_can_connect() function. Parameter exchange between dp_can_connect() and dp_apply_policy() is done via AVPs. The AVPs can be configured in the module's parameter section.

functions.name: dp_can_connect
functions.doc: Checks the interconnection policy of the caller. It uses the domain in the request URI to perform the DP-DDDS algorithm according to draft-lendl-domain-policy-ddds-02 to retrieve the domain's policy announcements. As of this version, only records conforming to draft-lendl-speermint-federations-02 and draft-lendl-speermint-technical-policy-00 are supported.

params.name: carrier_id_avp
params.doc: AVP to be populate with the ID string for the carrier the current GW belongs to.

params.name: cluster_id
params.doc: The ID of the cluster the module is part of. The clustering support is used in drouting module for two purposes: for sharing the status of the gateways/carriers and for controlling the pinging to gateways.

params.name: cluster_probing_mode
params.doc: This paramter controls how the probing/pinging should be done when using the clustering support. It is about which node in the cluster pings which gateway/destination.

params.name: cluster_sharing_tag
params.doc: The name of the sharing tag (as defined per clusterer modules) to control which node is responsible for perform the self-triggered actions in the module. Such actions may be the gateway probing (see also the parameter) or sharing the gateway/carrier status changes. If defined, only the node with active status of this tag will perform the actions (pinging and sharing status).

params.name: db_partitions_table
params.doc: The name of the table containing partition definitions. To be used with use_partitions and db_partitions_url .

params.name: db_partitions_url
params.doc: The url to the database containing partition-specific information. (partition-specific information includes partition name, url to the database where information about the partition is preserved, the names of the tables in which it is preserved and the AVPs that can be accessed using the .cfg script). The use_partitions parameter must be set to 1.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url.

params.name: default_group
params.doc: Group to be used if the caller (FROM user) is not found in the GROUP table.

params.name: define_blacklist
params.doc: Defines a blacklist based on a list of GW types - the blacklist will be populated with the IPs (no port, all protocols) of the GWs having the specified types.

params.name: drc_table
params.doc: The name of the db table storing definitions of the carriers that will be used directly by the routing rules.

params.name: drd_table
params.doc: The name of the db table storing gateway addresses.

params.name: drg_domain_col
params.doc: The name of the column in group db table where the domain is stored.

params.name: drg_grpid_col
params.doc: The name of the column in group db table where the group id is stored.

params.name: drg_table
params.doc: The name of the db table storing groups.

params.name: drg_user_col
params.doc: The name of the column in group db table where the username is stored.

params.name: drr_table
params.doc: The name of the db table storing routing rules.

params.name: enable_restart_persistency
params.doc: Parameter set to enable restart persistency for the Dynamic Routing module. When this parameter is set, the drouting module no longer loads the data from the database after restart, but uses the persistent storage file, and loads data from it on demand , improving the startup performance.

params.name: extra_id_chars
params.doc: A set of extra characters to be allowed in both Gateway and Carrier unique string identifiers, on top of alphanumeric characters.

params.name: extra_prefix_chars
params.doc: List of ASCII (0-127) characters to be additionally accepted in the prefixes. By default only '0' - '9' chars (digits) are accepted.

params.name: force_dns
params.doc: Force DNS resolving of GW/destination names (if not IPs) during startup. If not enabled, the GW name will be blindly used during routing.

params.name: generate_data_checksum
params.doc: If enabled, it will generate a checksum ( MD5 ) for drouting loaded data, attach that to the reload_status MI command output and to the reload generated status reports

params.name: gw_id_avp
params.doc: The name of the avp for storing the id of the current selected gateway/destination - once a new destination is selected (via the use_next_gw() function), the AVP will be updated with the ID of the new selected gateway/destination.

params.name: gw_priprefix_avp
params.doc: The name of the avp for storing the PRI prefix of the current selected destination/gateway - once a new destination is selected (via the use_next_gw() function), the AVP will be updated with the PRI prefix of the new used destination.

params.name: gw_sock_avp
params.doc: The name of the avp for storing sockets for alternative destinations defined by ruri_avp.

params.name: gw_socket_filter_mode
params.doc: This parameter controls the gateway filtering during DB loading, or which gateways are loaded or not into memory depending on the configured socket they have.

params.name: no_concurrent_reload
params.doc: If enabled, the module will not allow do run multiple dr_reload MI commands in parallel (with overlapping) Any new reload will be rejected (and discarded) while an existing reload is in progress.

params.name: partition_id_pvar
params.doc: Variable which will store the name of the name partition when wildcard(*) operatior is used. Use_partitions must be set in order to use this parameter.

params.name: persistent_state
params.doc: Specifies whether the state column should be loaded at startup and flushed during runtime or not.

params.name: probing_from
params.doc: The FROM SIP URI to be advertised in the SIP probing requests.

params.name: probing_interval
params.doc: How often (in seconds) the probing of a destination should be done. If set to 0, the probing will be disabled as functionality (for all destinations)

params.name: probing_method
params.doc: The SIP method to be used for the probing requests.

params.name: probing_reply_codes
params.doc: A comma separted list of SIP reply codes. The codes defined here will be considered as valid reply codes for probing messages, apart for 200.

params.name: probing_socket
params.doc: A socket description [proto:]host[:port] of the local socket (which is used by OpenSIPS for SIP traffic) to be used (if multiple) for sending the probing messages from.

params.name: rule_id_avp
params.doc: The name of the avp for storing the id of the current matched routing rule (see dr_rules table).

params.name: rule_prefix_avp
params.doc: The actual prefix that matched the routing rule (the part from RURI username that matched the routing rule).

params.name: rule_tables_query
params.doc: This parameter offers a dynamic, SQL-based way of building a set of dr_rules -compatible table names, to be each loaded and then merged into a single "dr_rules" table, for any given partition.

params.name: ruri_avp
params.doc: The name of the avp for storing Request URIs to be later used (alternative destiantions for the current one).

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: Flag to configure whether to use domain match when querying database for user's routing group.

params.name: use_partitions
params.doc: Flag to configure whether to use partitions for routing. If this flag is set then the db_partitions_url and db_partitions_table variables become mandatory.

functions.name: do_routing
functions.doc: Function to trigger routing of the message according to the rules in the database table and the configured parameters.

functions.name: dr_disable
functions.doc: Marks as disabled the last destination that was used for the current call. The disabling done via this function will prevent the destination to be used for usage from now on. The probing mechanism can re-enable this peer (see the probing section in the beginning)

functions.name: dr_is_gw
functions.doc: The function checks if the SIP URI hostname part stored inside the "src_pv" pseudo-variable is a gateway from a certain group.

functions.name: dr_match
functions.doc: The function tries to match/check the given number against the rules from the database.

functions.name: goes_to_gw
functions.doc: Function returns true if the destination of the current request (destination URI or Request URI) points (as IP) to one of the gateways. There no DNS lookups done if the domain part of the URI is not an IP.

functions.name: is_from_gw
functions.doc: The function checks if the sender of the message (source IP + source port) is a gateway from a certain group.

functions.name: route_to_carrier
functions.doc: Function to trigger the direct routing to a given set carriers (one or more). So, the routing is not done prefix based, but carrier based (call will be sent to the GWs of that carrier, based on carrier policy).

functions.name: route_to_gw
functions.doc: Function to trigger the direct routing to a given gateway (or list of gateways). Attributes and per-gw processing will be available.

functions.name: use_next_gw
functions.doc: The function takes the next available destination (set by do_routing, as alternative destinations) and pushes it into the RURI. Note that the function just sets the RURI (nothing more).

params.name: call_htable_size
params.doc: Exported by `emergency`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: callorigin
params.doc: Exported by `emergency`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: contingency_hostname
params.doc: The contingency_hostname is the url of the server que will route the call to the PSTN using the number of contingency.

params.name: db_table_provider
params.doc: The name of the db table that stores the nodes information of organization involved in emergency calls.

params.name: db_table_report
params.doc: The name of the db table that stores the emergency call report.

params.name: db_table_routing
params.doc: The name of the db table storing routing information to emergency calls.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url must be specified.

params.name: emergency_call_server
params.doc: The emergency_call_server is the url of the Routing Proxy/Redirect Server that will handle the emergency call in cenario II. Its is mandatory if Opensips act as Call Server in scenario II (proxy_role = 1 and flag_third_enterprise = 0) or Call Server in scenario III (proxy_role = 2).

params.name: emergency_codes
params.doc: Local emergency number. Opensips uses this number to recognize a emergency call beyond the username default defined by RFC-5031 (urn:service.sos.). Along with the number should be given a brief description about this code. The format is code_number-description. It can register multiple emergency numbers.

params.name: proxy_role
params.doc: This parameter define what role the opensips will take to treat emergency call: 0 – The opensips is the Call Server in scenario I. In this role the opensips implements the V2 interface, directly queries the VPC for ESGWRI/ESQK, selects the proper ESGW given the ESGWRI and routes calls Via the PSTN using the LRO if routing fails. 1 – The opensips is the Call Server in scenario II that sends the INVITE on emergency call to a Routing Proxy provider. The Routing Proxy provider implements the V2 interface. 2 - The opensips is the Routing Proxy in scenario II. In this role the opensips implements the V2 interface, directly queries the VPC for ESGWRI/ESQK, selects the proper ESGW given the ESGWRI and routes calls Via the PSTN using the LRO if routing fails. 3 - The opensips is the Redirect Proxy in scenario III that receives the INVITE on emergency call from Call Server. The Redirect Server obtains the ESGWRI/ESQK from the VPC and sends in the SIP 3xx response to the Call Server. 4 - The opensips is the Call Server in scenario III that sends the INVITE on emergency call to a Redirect Server. The Redirect Server obtains the ESGWRI/ESQK from the VPC. It returns the call to the opensips with the ESGWRI/ESQK in the header contact in the SIP response. The opensips selects the proper ESGW based on the ESGWRI.

params.name: subs_htable_size
params.doc: Exported by `emergency`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: Sets the time interval polling to make the copy in memory of the db_table_routing.

params.name: url_vpc
params.doc: The VPC url that opensips request the routing information to emergency call. This VPC url has IP:Port format

functions.name: emergency_call
functions.doc: Checks whether the incoming call is an emergency call, case it is treats, and routes the call to the destination determined by VPC. The function returns true if is a emergency call and the treat was Ok.

functions.name: failure
functions.doc: This function is used when trying to route the emergency call to the destination specified by the VPC and doesn't work, then uses this function to make one last attempt for a contingency number. The function returns true if the contingency treat was OK.

params.name: bl_algorithm
params.doc: This parameter determines which algorithm i_enum_query() will use to select the position in the DNS tree where the infrastructure tree branches off the user ENUM tree.

params.name: branchlabel
params.doc: This parameter determines which label i_enum_query() will use to branch off to the infrastructure ENUM tree.

params.name: domain_suffix
params.doc: The domain suffix to be added to the domain name obtained from the digits of an E164 number. Can be overridden by a parameter to enum_query.

params.name: i_enum_suffix
params.doc: The domain suffix to be used for i_enum_query() lookups. Can be overridden by a parameter to i_enum_query.

params.name: isn_suffix
params.doc: The domain suffix to be used for isn_query() lookups. Can be overridden by a parameter to isn_query.

params.name: tel_uri_params
params.doc: A string whose contents is appended to each new tel URI in the request as tel URI parameters.

functions.name: enum_query
functions.doc: The function performs an ENUM query on a given E.164 "number" (or R-URI username if "number" is missing) and rewrites the Request-URI with the result of the query. See for more information.

functions.name: i_enum_query
functions.doc: The function performs an enum query and rewrites the Request-URI with the result of the query. This the Infrastructure-ENUM version of enum_query(). The only difference to enum_query() is in the calculation of the FQDN where NAPTR records are looked for.

functions.name: is_from_user_enum
functions.doc: Checks if the user part of from URI is found in an enum lookup. Returns 1 if yes and -1 if not.

functions.name: isn_query
functions.doc: The function performs a ISN query and rewrites the Request-URI with the result of the query. See for more information.

params.name: delimiter
params.doc: Sets the separator between the parameters of the event in the logging file.

params.name: file_permissions
params.doc: Sets the permissions for the newly created logs. It expects a string representation of a octal value.

params.name: max_open_sockets
params.doc: Defines the maximum number of simultaneously opened files by the module. If the maximum limit is reached, an error message will be thrown, and further subscriptions will only be possible after at least one of the current subscriptions will expire.

params.name: suppress_event_name
params.doc: Suppresses the name of the event in the log file.

params.name: broker_id
params.doc: This parameter specifies the configuration for a Kafka broker (or cluster) that can be used to publish messages directly from the script, using the function.

functions.name: kafka_publish
functions.doc: Publishes a message to a Kafka broker (or cluster). As the actual send operation is done in an asynchronous manner, a report route may be provided in order to check the message delivery status.

params.name: connect_timeout
params.doc: The maximally allowed duration (in milliseconds) for the establishment of a TCP connection with a RabbitMQ server.

params.name: heartbeat
params.doc: Enables heartbeat support for the AMQP communication. If the client does not receive a heartbeat from server within the specified interval, the socket is automatically closed by the rabbitmq-client. This prevents OpenSIPS from blocking while waiting for a response from a dead rabbitmq-server. The value represents the heartbit interval in seconds.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Indicates the timeout (in milliseconds) of any command (i.e. publish) sent to the RabbitMQ server.

params.name: use_tls
params.doc: Setting this parameter will allow you to use TLS for broker connections. In order to enable TLS for a specific connection, you can use the "tls_domain= dom_name " parameter in the configuration specified through the .

functions.name: notify_on_event
functions.doc: This function creates a subscription to a given Event. A filter can be used (over the attributes of the Event) in order to filter even more the needed notifications (only Events matching the filter will be notified to this subscriber).

params.name: event_param
params.doc: By default, the name of the event subscribed to is not send in the JSON-RPC command. If one needs to send the name of the event as well, you can use this parameter to specify the name of JSON object within the params that will contain the name of the event.

params.name: reliable_mode
params.doc: This parameter controls the way the event_stream module communicates with the JSON-RPC server. If enabled, (set to 1 ), each event is translated to a JSON-RPC request. If disabled, each event will be sent as a JSON-RPC notification - there will be no reply expected by our client.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Specified the amount of milliseconds the module waits for a command to complete. In reliable_mode , it specifies the time module waits the request to be sent and a reply received. In non- reliable_mode , it represents only the time opensips takes to send the JSON-RPC notification.

params.name: failover_timeout
params.doc: The minimum duration in seconds that a failed subscriber is skipped for further notifications. This parameter only affects the FAILOVER policy.

params.name: use_struct_param
params.doc: When raising an event, pack the name and value of the parameters in a XMLRPC structure. This provides an easier way for some XMLRPC server implementations to interpret the parameters. Set it to zero to disable or to non-zero to enable it.

params.name: setvars
params.doc: Set to 1 to enable setting all above-mentioned environment variables for all executed commands.

params.name: time_to_kill
params.doc: If set, this parameter specifies the longest time (in seconds) that a program is allowed to execute. Once this duration is exceeded, the program is terminated (SIGTERM).

functions.name: exec
functions.doc: Executes an external command. The input is passed to the standard input of the new process, if specified, and the output is saved in the output variable.

params.name: calldur_thresh_crit_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the critical threshold value for call duration.

params.name: calldur_thresh_warn_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the warning threshold value for call duration.

params.name: concalls_thresh_crit_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the critical threshold value for the number of concurrent calls.

params.name: concalls_thresh_warn_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the warning threshold value for the number of concurrent calls.

params.name: cpm_thresh_crit_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the critical threshold value for calls per minute.

params.name: cpm_thresh_warn_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the warning threshold value for calls per minute.

params.name: days_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the week days in which the fraud rule's interval is available.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database where to load the rules from.

params.name: end_h_col
params.doc: Exported by `fraud_detection`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: pid_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the fraud profile's id.

params.name: prefix_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the prefix for which the fraud rule will match.

params.name: rid_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the fraud rule's id.

params.name: seqcalls_thresh_crit_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the critical threshold value for the number of sequential calls.

params.name: seqcalls_thresh_warn_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the warning threshold value for the number of sequential calls.

params.name: start_h_col
params.doc: Exported by `fraud_detection`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: If you want to load the rules from the database you must set this parameter as the database name.

params.name: totalc_thresh_crit_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the critical threshold value for the number of total calls.

params.name: totalc_thresh_warn_col
params.doc: The column's name in the database storing the warning threshold value for the number of total calls.

params.name: use_utc_time
params.doc: Set this parameter to non-zero in order to enable UTC-based interval matching and statistics resets, rather than local time-based.

functions.name: check_fraud
functions.doc: This method should be called each time a given user calls a given number . It will try to match a fraud rule within the given fraud profile and update the stats (see above). Furthermore, the stats will be checked against the rule's thresholds. If any of the stats is above its threshold value, the appropriate event will also be raised (see further details below).

params.name: esl_cmd_polling_itv
params.doc: The sleep interval used when polling for an ESL command response. Since the value of this parameter imposes a minimal duration for any ESL command, you should run OpenSIPS in debug mode in order to first determine an expected response time for an arbitrary ESL command, then tune this parameter accordingly.

params.name: esl_cmd_timeout
params.doc: The maximally allowed duration for the execution of an ESL command. This interval does not include the connect duration.

params.name: esl_connect_timeout
params.doc: The maximally allowed duration for the establishment of an ESL connection.

params.name: event_heartbeat_interval
params.doc: The expected interval between FreeSWITCH HEARTBEAT event arrivals.

params.name: db_col_events
params.doc: The SQL column name for the comma-separated, case-sensitive FreeSWITCH event names which OpenSIPS will subscribe to.

params.name: db_col_ip
params.doc: The SQL column name for the "ip" ESL connect information.

params.name: db_col_password
params.doc: The SQL column name for the "password" ESL connect information.

params.name: db_col_port
params.doc: The SQL column name for the "port" ESL connect information.

params.name: db_col_username
params.doc: The SQL column name for the "username" ESL connect information.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The SQL table name for this module.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: An SQL database URL which the module will use in order to load a set of FreeSWITCH ESL sockets and their event subscriptions.

params.name: fs_subscribe
params.doc: Add a FreeSWITCH ESL URL to which OpenSIPS will connect at startup. The URL syntax includes support for specifying a list of events to subscribe to and follows this pattern: [fs://][[username]:password@]host[:port][?event1[,event2]...]

functions.name: freeswitch_esl
functions.doc: Run an arbitrary command on an arbitrary FreeSWITCH ESL socket. The socket need not necessarily be defined in the database or through . However, if this is the case, then the "password" part of the URL becomes mandatory.

params.name: initial
params.doc: The initial value of global flags bitmap.

functions.name: is_gflag
functions.doc: Check if bit at the position flag in global flags is set.

functions.name: reset_gflag
functions.doc: Reset the bit at the position flag in global flags.

functions.name: set_gflag
functions.doc: Set the bit at the position flag in global flags.

params.name: aaa_url
params.doc: This is the url representing the AAA protocol used and the location of the configuration file of this protocol.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: url of the database table to be used.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: Name of the table column holding domains.

params.name: group_column
params.doc: Name of the table column holding groups.

params.name: multiple_gid
params.doc: If enabled (non zero value) the regular-expression matching will return all group IDs that match the user; otherwise only the first will be returned.

params.name: re_exp_column
params.doc: Name of the re_table column holding the regular expression used for user matching.

params.name: re_gid_column
params.doc: Name of the re_table column holding the group IDs.

params.name: re_table
params.doc: Name of the table holding definitions for regular-expression based groups. If no table is defined, the regular-expression support is disabled.

params.name: table
params.doc: Name of the table holding strict definitions of groups and their members.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: If enabled (set to non zero value) then domain will be used also used for strict group matching; otherwise only the username part will be used.

params.name: user_column
params.doc: Name of the table column holding usernames.

functions.name: aaa_is_user_in
functions.doc: This function checks group membership, using AAA support. The function returns true if username in the given "uri" is member of the given group and false if not.

functions.name: db_get_user_group
functions.doc: This function is to be used for regular expression based group membership, using DB support. The function returns true if the username in the given "uri" belongs to at least one group.

functions.name: db_is_user_in
functions.doc: This function is to be used for script group membership. The function returns true if username in the given uri is member of the given group and false if not.

params.name: base_dn
params.doc: Base LDAP DN to start LDAP search for H.350 entries. For best performance, this should be set to the direct ancestor of the H.350 objects.

params.name: ldap_session
params.doc: Name of the LDAP session to be used for H.350 queries, as defined in the LDAP module configuration file.

params.name: search_scope
params.doc: LDAP search scope for H.350 queries, one of "one", "base", or "sub".

params.name: ip
params.doc: The listening IPv4 address.

params.name: max_headers_size
params.doc: The maximum amount of bytes allowed for all header field names and values combined in a single HTTP/2 request processed by the server. Once this threshold is reached, extra headers will no longer be provided at script level and will be reported as errors instead.

params.name: port
params.doc: The listening port.

params.name: response_timeout
params.doc: The maximum amount of time, in milliseconds, that the library will allow the opensips.cfg processing to take for a given HTTP/2 request.

params.name: tls_cert_path
params.doc: File path to the TLS certificate, in PEM format.

params.name: tls_key_path
params.doc: Exported by `http2d`; not documented in the module README.

functions.name: http2_send_response
functions.doc: Sends a response for the HTTP/2 request being processed. The ":status" header field will be automatically included by the module as 1st header, so it must not be included in the headers_json array.

params.name: buf_size
params.doc: It specifies the maximum length (in bytes) of the buffer used to write in the html response.

params.name: conn_timeout
params.doc: Auto-close TCP connections which are idle for more than the designated timeout, in seconds. Set to zero to never close any connections.

params.name: ip
params.doc: The IP address used by the HTTP server to listen for incoming requests.

params.name: port
params.doc: The port number used by the HTTP server to listen for incoming requests.

params.name: post_buf_size
params.doc: It specifies the length (in bytes) of the POST HTTP requests processing buffer. For large POST request, the default value might require to be increased.

params.name: tls_cert_file
params.doc: Public certificate file for httpd. It will be used as server-side certificate for incoming TLS connections.

params.name: tls_ciphers
params.doc: You can specify the list of algorithms for authentication and encryption that you allow. To obtain a list of ciphers and then choose, use the gnutls-cli application:

params.name: tls_key_file
params.doc: Private key of the above certificate. I must be kept in a safe place with tight permissions!

params.name: authCert
params.doc: Filename of certificate which belongs to privKey . This file must be in PEM format.

params.name: caList
params.doc: File containing all trusted (root) certificates for the verifier. Certificates must be in PEM format.

params.name: certUri
params.doc: URI from which the certificate of the authentication service can be acquired. This string will be placed in the Identity-Info header.

params.name: crlList
params.doc: File containing certificate revocation lists (crls) for the verifier. Setting this parameter is only necessary if useCrls is set to 1 .

params.name: privKey
params.doc: Filename of private RSA-key of authentication service. This file must be in PEM format.

params.name: useCrls
params.doc: Switch to decide whether to use revocation lists ( 1 ) or not ( 0 ).

params.name: verCert
params.doc: Path containing certificates for the verifier. Certificates must be in PEM format. The URI in the Identity-Info header field is used to find the corresponding certificate for the request. For this purpose the verifier replaces every character which is not alphanumeric, no _ and no . with a - . A . at the beginning of the URI is forbidden. If the URI is http://www.test.com/cert.pem the verifier will look for the file http---www.test.com-cert.pem , for example. It is also possible to store a whole certificate chain in a file. In this case certificates must be in right order, end certificate first.

functions.name: authservice
functions.doc: This function performs the steps of an authentication service. Before you call this function, you have to ensure that

functions.name: verifier
functions.doc: This function performs the steps of an verifier. The returned code tells you the result of the verification:

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The power of 2 to get the size of the hash table used for storing members and rooms.

params.name: imc_cmd_start_char
params.doc: The character which indicates that the body of the message is a command.

params.name: members_table
params.doc: The name of the table storing IMC members.

params.name: outbound_proxy
params.doc: The SIP address used as next hop when sending the message. Very useful when using OpenSIPS with a domain name not in DNS, or when using a separate OpenSIPS instance for imc processing. If not set, the message will be sent to the address in destination URI.

params.name: rooms_table
params.doc: The name of the table storing IMC rooms.

functions.name: imc_manager
functions.doc: Handles Message method.It detects if the body of the message is a conference command.If so it executes it, otherwise it sends the message to all the members in the room.

params.name: aliases
params.doc: Aliases for im networks.

params.name: cache_time
params.doc: Cache time of a Jabber connection.

params.name: check_time
params.doc: Time between checking the status of JabberGW workers (in seconds).

params.name: db_url
params.doc: SQL url of database.

params.name: delay_time
params.doc: Time to keep a sip message (in seconds).

params.name: jaddress
params.doc: ip or hostname of Jabber server -- it must be the same as the value from  tag of Jabber server config file.

params.name: jdomain
params.doc: Format: jabber.sipserver.com=. If the destination is for Jabber network the uri should be like: usernamejabber_server@jdomain or nicknameroomnameconference_server@jdomain

params.name: jport
params.doc: Port number of Jabber server.

params.name: max_jobs
params.doc: Maximum jobs per worker.

params.name: priority
params.doc: Presence priority for Jabber gateway.

params.name: proxy
params.doc: Outbound proxy address.

params.name: registrar
params.doc: The address in whose behalf the INFO and ERROR messages are sent.

params.name: sleep_time
params.doc: Time between expired Jabber connections checking (in seconds).

params.name: workers
params.doc: Number of workers.

functions.name: jab_exit_jconf
functions.doc: Leave a Jabber conference--the nickname, room name and conference server address should be included in To header as: nickname%roomname%conference_server@jdomain .

functions.name: jab_go_offline
functions.doc: Log off from Jabber server the associated Jabber ID of the sip user.

functions.name: jab_go_online
functions.doc: Register to the Jabber server with associated Jabber ID of the sip user.

functions.name: jab_join_jconf
functions.doc: Join a Jabber conference--the nickname, room name and conference server address should be included in To header as: nickname%roomname%conference_server@jdomain . If the nickname is missing, then the sip username is used.

functions.name: jab_send_message
functions.doc: Converts sip MESSAGE message to a Jabber message and sends it to Jabber server.

params.name: enable_long_quoting
params.doc: Enable this parameter if your input JSONs contain signed integers which do not fit into 4 bytes (e.g. larger than 2147483647, etc.). If the parameter is enabled, 4-byte integers will continue to be returned as integers, while larger values will be returned as strings, in order to avoid the integer overflow.

functions.name: json_link
functions.doc: This function can be used to link json objects together. This will work simillar to setting a value to an object, the only difference is that the second object is not copied, only a reference is created.

params.name: connect_timeout
params.doc: The amount of milliseconds OpenSIPS waits to connect to the the JSON-RPC server, until it times out.

params.name: read_timeout
params.doc: The amount of milliseconds OpenSIPS waits for the JSON-RPC server to respond to a JSON-RPC request, until it times out. Note that these parameter only affects the jsonrpc_request command.

params.name: write_timeout
params.doc: The amount of milliseconds OpenSIPS waits to send a RPC command to the JSON-RPC server, until it times out.

functions.name: jsonrpc_notification
functions.doc: Does a JSON-RPC notification to the JSON-RPC server indicated in the destination parameter, but unlike , it does not wait for a reply from the JSON-RPC server.

functions.name: jsonrpc_request
functions.doc: Does a JSON-RPC request to the JSON-RPC server indicated in the destination parameter, and waits for a reply from it.

params.name: connect_wait
params.doc: The time to wait (in miliseconds) when connecting to the LD service. An initial failure in connecting to the LD service may be addressed by increasing this wait value.

params.name: ld_log_level
params.doc: The LaunchDarkly specific log level to be used by the LD SDK/libray to log its internal messages. Note that these log produced by the LD library (according to this ld_log_level) will be further subject to filtering according to the overall OpenSIPS log_level.

params.name: re_init_interval
params.doc: The minimum time interval (in seconds) to try again to init the LD client in the situation when the module was not able to init the LC connection at startup. In case of such failure, the module will automatically re-try to init its LD client on-demand, whnever the feature flag is checked from script, but not sooner than `re_init_interval`. Note: if there are no flag checkings to be performed, the re-init may be attempted longer than `re_init_interval`.

params.name: sdk_key
params.doc: The LaunchDarkly SDK key used to connect to the service. This is a mandatory parameter.

functions.name: ld_feature_enabled
functions.doc: Function to evaluate a LaunchDarkly boolean feature flag

params.name: config_file
params.doc: Full path to LDAP configuration file.

params.name: max_async_connections
params.doc: Number of maximum asynchronous connections that will be started with the ldap server for executing asynchronous ldap_search calls. The number of connections is per process, so if there are 8 worker processes with 20 max_async_connections, there will be a maximum of 160 connections to the ldap server.

params.name: cluster_id
params.doc: The ID of the cluster the module is part of. The clustering support is used in load-balancer module for two purposes: for sharing the status of the destinations and for controlling the pinging to destinations.

params.name: cluster_sharing_tag
params.doc: The name of the sharing tag (as defined per clusterer modules) to control which node is responsible for perform the self-triggered actions in the module. Such actions may be the destination probing or sharing the changes in the destination status. If defined, only the node with active status of this tag will perform the actions (pinging and sharing status).

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The name of the DB table containing the load-balancing rules.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The URL pointing to the database where the load-balancing rules are stored.

params.name: fetch_freeswitch_stats
params.doc: If enabled, the maximum value of a resource may also consist of FreeSWITCH Event Socket Layer URLs, e.g. "channels=fs://:password@freeswitch.example.com" or "channels=fs://user:password@127.0.0.1:8021" . The default ESL port is 8021.

params.name: initial_freeswitch_load
params.doc: This parameter is only relevant for some seconds after module startup/reload, when no statistics from newly loaded FreeSWITCH ESL sockets have arrived, yet the routing of calls must remain unaffected. Any FreeSWITCH-enabled resource will inherit this value for the entire interval mentioned above (up to 20 seconds!).

params.name: lb_define_blacklist
