params.name: ssl_lifetime
params.doc: The ssl_lifetime (integer) parameter defines the lifetime, in seconds, of a single SSL session key. Once this time limit is exceeded, the OSP module will negotiate a new session key. Communication exchanges in progress will not be interrupted when this time limit expires. This is an optional field with default value is 200 seconds.

params.name: support_nonsip_protocol
params.doc: The support_nonsip_protocol (integer) parameter is used to tell the OSP module if non-SIP signaling protocol destination devices are supported. The default value is 0.

params.name: switchid_location
params.doc: The switchid_location (integer) parameter instructs the OSP module where the destination switch ID should be appended. The default value is 2

params.name: switchid_parameter
params.doc: The switchid_parameter (string) parameter instructs the OSP module to use which parameter name in outbound destination URIs to append destination switch ID. The default value is "switchid"

params.name: timeout
params.doc: The timeout (integer) parameter defines the maximum time in milliseconds, to wait for a response from a peering server. If no response is received within this time, the current connection is aborted and the OSP module attempts to contact the next peering server. The default value is 10 seconds.

params.name: token_format
params.doc: When OpenSIPS receives a SIP INVITE with a peering token, the OSP module will validate the token to determine whether or not the call has been authorized by a peering server. Peering tokens may, or may not, be digitally signed. The token_format (integer) parameter defines if OpenSIPS will validate signed or unsigned tokens or both. The values for token format are defined below. The default value is 2.

params.name: use_number_portability
params.doc: The use_number_portability (integer) parameter instructs the OSP module how to use the number portability parameters in the Request URI of the SIP INVITE message. If this value is set to 1, the OSP module uses the number portability parameters in the Request URI when these parameters exist. If this value is set to 0, the OSP module will not use the number portability parameters. The default value is 1.

params.name: use_security_features
params.doc: The use_security_features (integer) parameter instructs the OSP module how to use the OSP security features. If this value is set to 1, the OSP module uses the OSP security features. If this value is set to 0, the OSP module will not use the OSP security features. The default value is 0.

params.name: user_group_avp
params.doc: These parameter is used to tell the OSP module which AVP is used to store source user group information. The default value is "$avp(_osp_user_group_)". All pseudo variables are described in https://opensips.org/Resources/DocsCoreVar.

params.name: user_id_avp
params.doc: These parameter is used to tell the OSP module which AVP is used to store source user ID information. The default value is "$avp(_osp_user_id_)". All pseudo variables are described in https://opensips.org/Resources/DocsCoreVar.

params.name: validate_callid
params.doc: Exported by `osp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: work_mode
params.doc: The work_mode (integer) parameter instructs the OSP module what mode it should work in. If this value is set to 0, the OSP module works in direct mode. If this value is set to 1, the OSP module works in indirect mode. The default value is 0.

functions.name: checkcallingtranslation
functions.doc: This function is used to check if the calling number is translated. Before calling checkcallingtranslation, prepareosproute should be called. If the calling number does been translated, the original Remote-Party-ID, if it exists, should be removed from the INVITE message. And a new Remote-Party-ID header should be added (a RPID value for the RPID AVP has been set by prepareosproute). If the calling number is not translated, nothing should be done.

functions.name: checkospheader
functions.doc: This function checks for the existence of the OSP-Auth-Token header field.

functions.name: checkosproute
functions.doc: This function is used to check if there is any route for the call.

functions.name: getlocaladdress
functions.doc: This function gets the receiving IP address of SIP response and stores it as proxy egress address.

functions.name: prepareallosproutes
functions.doc: This function tries to prepare all the routes in the list returned by the peering server. The message is then forked off to the destinations. If unsuccessful in preparing the routes a SIP 500 is sent back and a trace message is logged.

functions.name: prepareospresponse
functions.doc: This function tries to prepare all the routes in the list returned by the peering server into SIP 300 Redirect or SIP 380 Alternative Service message. The message is then replied to the source. If unsuccessful in preparing the routes a SIP 500 is sent back and a trace message is logged.

functions.name: prepareosproute
functions.doc: This function tries to prepare the INVITE to be forwarded using the destination in the list returned by the peering server. If the calling number is translated, a RPID value for the RPID AVP will be set. If the route could not be prepared, the function returns 'FALSE' back to the script, which can then decide how to handle the failure. Note, if checkosproute has been called and returns 'TRUE' before calling prepareosproute, prepareosproute should not return 'FALSE' because checkosproute has confirmed that there is at least one route.

functions.name: processsubscribe
functions.doc: This function should be called after receiving a SUBSCRIBE for CNAM message and there is a cached CNAM record for this message. This function generates a NOTIFY message including the cached CNAM record, then sends the NOTIFY message to the device sending the SUBSCRIBE message.

functions.name: reportospusage
functions.doc: This function should be called after receiving a BYE message. If the message contains an OSP cookie, the function will forward originating and/or terminating duration usage information to a peering server. The function returns TRUE if the BYE includes an OSP cookie. The actual usage message will be send on a different thread and will not delay BYE processing. The function should be called before relaying the message.

functions.name: requestosprouting
functions.doc: This function launches a query to the peering server requesting the IP address of one or more destination peers serving the called party. If destination peers are available, the peering server will return the IP address and a peering authorization token for each destination peer. The OSP-Auth-Token Header field is inserted into the SIP message and the SIP uri is rewritten to the IP address of destination peer provided by the peering server.

functions.name: setrequestdate
functions.doc: This function gets the receiving IP address of SIP response and stores it as proxy egress address.

functions.name: validateospheader
functions.doc: This function validates an OSP-Token specified in the OSP-Auth-Tokenheader field of the SIP message. If a peering token is present, it will be validated locally. If no OSP header is found or the header token is invalid or expired, -1 is returned; on successful validation 1 is returned.

params.name: enable_double_path
params.doc: There are some situations when the server needs to insert two Path header fields instead of one. For example when using two disconnected networks or doing cross-protocol forwarding from UDP->TCP. This parameter enables inserting of 2 Paths.

params.name: use_received
params.doc: If set to 1, the received parameter of the first Route uri is evaluated and used as destination-uri if present.

functions.name: add_path
functions.doc: This function adds a Path header in the form Path:  .

functions.name: add_path_received
functions.doc: This function adds a Path header in the form Path:  , setting 'user' as username part of address, it's own outgoing address as domain-part, and the address the request has been received from as received-parameter.

params.name: aaa_url
params.doc: This is the url representing the AAA protocol used and the location of the configuration file of this protocol.

params.name: verify_destination_service_type
params.doc: This is the value of the Service-Type AAA attribute to be used, when sender of SIP Request verifies request's destination using verify_destination() function.

params.name: verify_source_service_type
params.doc: Exported by `peering`; not documented in the module README.

functions.name: verify_destination
functions.doc: Function verify_destination() queries from broker's AAA server if domain (host part) of Request URI is served by a trusted peer. AAA request contains the following attributes/values:

functions.name: verify_source
functions.doc: Function verify_source() queries from broker's AAA server if SIP request was received from a trusted peer. AAA request contains the following attributes/values:

params.name: filename
params.doc: This is the file name of your script. This may be set once only, but it may include an arbitary number of functions and use as many Perl module as necessary.

params.name: modpath
params.doc: The path to the Perl modules included (OpenSIPS.pm et.al). It is not absolutely crucial to set this path, as you may install the Modules in Perl's standard path, or update the %INC variable from within your script. Using this module parameter is the standard behavior, though.

functions.name: perl_exec
functions.doc: Calls a perl function with passing it the current SIP message. The SIP message is reflected by a Perl module that gives you access to the information in the current SIP message (OpenSIPS::Message).

functions.name: perl_exec_simple
functions.doc: Calls a perl function without passing it the current SIP message. May be used for very simple simple requests that do not have to fiddle with the message themselves, but rather return information values about the environment.

params.name: address_table
params.doc: Name of database table containing matching rules used by allow_register function. Since version 2.2, this table name also represents the default table name for partitions without a 'table_name' setting.

params.name: allow_suffix
params.doc: Suffix to be appended to basename to create filename of the allow file when version with one parameter of either allow_routing or allow_register is used.

params.name: check_all_branches
params.doc: If set then allow_routing functions will check Request-URI of all branches (default). If disabled then only Request-URI of the first branch will be checked.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The URL of the database to be used for loading the data related to IP-based checking ( address table).

params.name: default_allow_file
params.doc: Default allow file used by functions without parameters. If you don't specify full pathname then the directory in which is the main config file is located will be used.

params.name: default_deny_file
params.doc: Default file containing deny rules. The file is used by functions without parameters. If you don't specify full pathname then the directory in which the main config file is located will be used.

params.name: deny_suffix
params.doc: Suffix to be appended to basename to create filename of the deny file when version with one parameter of either allow_routing or allow_register is used.

params.name: grp_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containing group identifier of the address.

params.name: info_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containing a string that is added as value to a pvar given as argument to check_address or check_source_address in case the function succedes.

params.name: ip_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containing IP address part of the address.

params.name: mask_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containing network mask of the address. Possible values are 0-128. It should be up to 32 if the IP is v4 and up to 128 if the IP is v6.

params.name: partition
params.doc: Specify a new IP-based checking partition (data source). This parameter may be set multiple times. Each partition may have a specific "db_url" and "table_name". If not specified, these values will be inherited from , db_default_url or , respectively. The name of the default partition is 'default'.

params.name: pattern_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containinga a pattern (a shell wildcard pattern, like the ones used for file name matching) that is matched against the arguments received by check_address or check_source_address .

params.name: port_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containing port part of the address.

params.name: proto_col
params.doc: Name of address table column containing transport protocol that is matched against transport protocol of received request. Possible values that can be stored in proto_col are any , udp , tcp , tls , sctp , and none . Value any matches always and value none never.

functions.name: allow_register
functions.doc: The function returns true if all pairs constructed as described in have appropriate permissions according to the configuration files given as parameters.

functions.name: allow_routing
functions.doc: Returns true if all pairs constructed as described in have appropriate permissions according to the configuration files. This function uses default configuration files specified in default_allow_file and default_deny_file .

functions.name: allow_routing_1
functions.doc: Returns true if all pairs constructed as described in have appropriate permissions according to the configuration files given as parameters.

functions.name: allow_uri
functions.doc: Returns true if the pair constructed as described in have appropriate permissions according to the configuration files specified by the parameter.

functions.name: check_address
functions.doc: Returns 1 if group id, IP address, port and protocol given as arguments match an IP subnet found in cached address table, as described in . The function takes 4 mandatory arguments and 3 optional ones.

functions.name: check_source_address
functions.doc: Equivalent to check_address(group_id, "$si", "$sp", "$socket_in(proto)", context_info, pattern, partition).

functions.name: get_source_group
functions.doc: Checks if an entry with the source ip/port/protocol is found in cached address or subnet table in any group. If yes, returns that group in the variable parameter. If not returns -1. Port value 0 in cached address and subnet table matches any port. Optionally, you can also specify the partition. If no partition specified, the default one will be used.

params.name: framework
params.doc: Specifies the full path for xml framework descriptor.

params.name: pi_http_method
params.doc: Specifies the HTTP request method to be used: 0 - use GET HTTP request 1 - use POST HTTP request

params.name: pi_http_root
params.doc: Specifies the root path for pi HTTP requests. The link to the OpenSIPS provisioning web interface must be constructed using the following patern: http://[opensips_IP]:[opensips_mi_port]/[pi_http_root]

params.name: check_route
params.doc: The name of the script route to be triggers (in automatic way) when a package is received from the network. If you do a "drop" in this route, it will indicate to the module that the source IP of the package does not need to be monitored. Otherwise, the source IP will be automatically monitered.

params.name: pike_log_level
params.doc: Log level to be used by module to auto report the blocking (only first time) and unblocking of IPs detected as source of floods.

params.name: remove_latency
params.doc: For how long the IP address will be kept in memory after the last request from that IP address. It's a sort of timeout value.

params.name: reqs_density_per_unit
params.doc: How many requests should be allowed per sampling_time_unit before blocking all the incoming request from that IP. Practically, the blocking limit is between ( let's have x=reqs_density_per_unit) x and 3*x for IPv4 addresses and between x and 8*x for ipv6 addresses.

params.name: sampling_time_unit
params.doc: Time period used for sampling (or the sampling accuracy ;-) ). The smaller the better, but slower. If you want to detect peaks, use a small one. To limit the access (like total number of requests on a long period of time) to a proxy resource (a gateway for ex), use a bigger value of this parameter.

functions.name: pike_check_req
functions.doc: Process the source IP of the current request and returns false if the IP was exceeding the blocking limit.

params.name: active_watchers_table
params.doc: The name of the db table where active subscription information are stored.

params.name: bla_fix_remote_target
params.doc: Polycom has a bug in the bla implementation. It inserts the remote IP contact in the Notify body and when a phone picks up a call put on hold by another phone in the same BLA group, it sends an Invite directly to the remote IP. OpenSIPS BLA server tries to prevent this by replacing the IP contact with the domain, when this is possible.

params.name: bla_presentity_spec
params.doc: By default the presentity uri for BLA subscribes (event=dialog;sla) is computed from contact username + from domain. In some cases though, this way of computing the presentity might not be right (for example if you have a SBC in front that masquerades the contact). So we added this parameter that allows defining a custom uri to be used as presentity uri for BLA subscribes. You should set this parameter to the name of a pseudovariable and then set this pseudovariable to the desired URI before calling the function.

params.name: clean_period
params.doc: The period at which to clean the expired subscription dialogs.

params.name: cluster_be_active_shtag
params.doc: The name of a cluster sharing tag to be used to indicate when this node (as part of the cluster) should be active or not. If the sharing tag is off (or as backup), the node will become inactive from clustering perspective, meaning not sending and not accepting any presence related cluster traffic.

params.name: cluster_federation_mode
params.doc: When enabling the federation mode, nodes inside the presence cluster will start broadcasting the data to other nodes via the clustering support.

params.name: cluster_id
params.doc: The ID of the cluster this presence server belongs to. This parameter is to be used only if clustering mode is needed. In order to understand th concept of a cluster ID, please see the clusterer module.

params.name: cluster_pres_events
params.doc: Comma Separated Value (CSV) list with the events to considered by the federated cluster - only presentities advertising one of these events will be broadcasted via the cluster.

params.name: contact_user
params.doc: This is the username that will be used in the Contact header for the 200 OK replies to SUBSCRIBE and in the following in-dialog NOTIFY requests. The IP address, port and transport for the Contact will be automatically determined based on the interface where the SUBSCRIBE was received.

params.name: db_update_period
params.doc: The period at which to synchronize cached subscriber info with the database.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url.

params.name: enable_sphere_check
params.doc: This parameter is a flag that should be set if permission rules include sphere checking. The sphere information is expected to be present in the RPID body published by the presentity. The flag is introduced as this check requires extra processing that should be avoided if this feature is not supported by the clients.

params.name: end_sub_on_timeout
params.doc: If a presence subscription should be automatically terminated (destroyed) when receiving a SIP timeout (408) for a sent NOTIFY requests.

params.name: expires_offset
params.doc: The extra time to store a subscription/publication.

params.name: fallback2db
params.doc: Setting this parameter enables a fallback to db mode of operation. In this mode, in case a searched record is not found in cache, the search is continued in database. Useful for an architecture in which processing and memory load might be divided on more machines using the same database.

params.name: max_expires_publish
params.doc: The the maximum admissible expires value for PUBLISH messages.

params.name: max_expires_subscribe
params.doc: The the maximum admissible expires value for SUBSCRIBE messages.

params.name: mix_dialog_presence
params.doc: This module parameter enables a very nice feature in the presence server - generating presence information from dialogs state. If this parameter is set, the presence server will tell you if a buddy is in a call even if his phone did not send a presence Publish with this information. You will need to load the dialoginfo modules, presence_dialoginfo, pua_dialoginfo, dialog and pua.

params.name: notify_offline_body
params.doc: If this parameter is set, when no published info is found for a user, the presence server will generate a dummy body with status 'closed' and use it when sending Notify, instead of notifying with no body.

params.name: pres_htable_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table to store publish records. This parameter will be used as the power of 2 when computing table size.

params.name: presentity_table
params.doc: The name of the db table where Publish information are stored.

params.name: subs_htable_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table to store subscription dialogs. This parameter will be used as the power of 2 when computing table size.

params.name: waiting_subs_daysno
params.doc: The number of days to keep the record of a subscription in server database if the subscription is in pending or waiting state (no authorization policy was defined for it or the target user did not register sice the subscription and was not informed about it).

params.name: watchers_table
params.doc: The name of the db table where subscription states are stored.

functions.name: handle_publish
functions.doc: The function handles PUBLISH requests. It stores and updates published information in database and calls functions to send NOTIFY messages when changes in the published information occur.

functions.name: handle_subscribe
functions.doc: This function is to be used for handling SUBSCRIBE requests. It stores or updates the watcher/subscriber information in database. Additionally, in response to initial SUBSCRIBE requests (creating a new subscription session), the function also sends back the NOTIFY (with the presence information) to the wathcer/subscriber.

params.name: call_info_timeout_notification
params.doc: Enables or disables call_info event timeout notifications.

params.name: disable_dialog_support_for_sca
params.doc: Disables the internal publishing of the "call-info" events (generated by the dialog module). The publishing is expected to be done via SIP PUBLISH from a third-party. See the wroking mode described in the beginning of this document.

params.name: line_hash_size
params.doc: Allows you to controll the size of the internal hash table used for storing the information about the lines and indexes (in the internal publishing mode).

params.name: line_seize_timeout_notification
params.doc: Enables or disables line_seize event timeout notifications.

functions.name: sca_set_called_line
functions.doc: The function (to be used only in internal publishing mode) is setting for the current new call (initinal INVITE) the inbound line - the line the call was received on.

functions.name: sca_set_calling_line
functions.doc: The function (to be used only in internal publishing mode) is setting for the current new call (initinal INVITE) the outbound line - the line used for calling out.

params.name: get_route
params.doc: The name of the script route to be run in order to retrieve the status of a feature.

params.name: set_route
params.doc: The name of the script route to be run when a feature status update from a SIP phone is received.

params.name: force_single_dialog
params.doc: By default the module aggregates all available dialog info into a single dialog-info document containing multiple "dialog" elements. If the phone does not support this, you can activate this parameter.

params.name: aggregate_presentities
params.doc: Exported by `presence_reginfo`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: Exported by `presence_reginfo`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: force_active
params.doc: This parameter is used for permissions when handling Subscribe messages. If set to 1, subscription state is considered active and the presentity is not queried for permissions(should be set to 1 if not using an xcap server). Otherwise,the xcap server is queried and the subscription states is according to user defined permission rules. If no rules are defined for a certain watcher, the subscriptions remains in pending state and the Notify sent will have no body.

params.name: generate_offline_body
params.doc: This parameter should be set to 0 if you want to prevent OpenSIPS from automatically generating a PIDF body when a publication expires or is explicitly terminated (a PUBLISH request is received with Expires: 0).

params.name: pidf_manipulation
params.doc: Setting this parameter to 1 enables the features described in RFC 4827. It gives the possibility to have a permanent state notified to the users even in the case in which the phone is not online. The presence document is taken from the xcap server and aggregated together with the other presence information, if any exist, for each Notify that is sent to the watchers. It is also possible to have information notified even if not issuing any Publish (useful for services such as email, SMS, MMS).

params.name: pres_rules_auid
params.doc: This parameter should be configured if you are using the non integrated xcap mode and you need to use another pres-rules auid than the default 'pres-rules'.

params.name: pres_rules_filename
params.doc: This parameter should be configured if you are using the non integrated xcap mode and you need to configure another filename than the default 'index'.

params.name: xcap_server
params.doc: The address of the xcap servers used for storage. This parameter is compulsory if the integrated_xcap_server parameter is not set. It can be set more that once, to construct an address list of trusted XCAP servers.

params.name: delimiter
params.doc: Specifies the delimiter to be used to separate prefix and group_prefix .

params.name: group_label
params.doc: Specifies the label used to store the group when group_mode is 2.

params.name: group_mode
params.doc: Specifies how the group of the statistic should be provisioned to Prometheus. Available modes are: 0 - do not send the statistics groups. 1 - send the group in the name of the statstic. For example, timestamp statistic from the core group would be exported as opensips_core_timestamp . Note that the group_prefix is still attached to the group's name. 2 - send the group as a label of the statstic. The name of the label is specified by the group_label parameter.

params.name: group_prefix
params.doc: Appends a prefix to the name of the group the statistic belongs to.

params.name: labels
params.doc: Rules that define how to convert the name of a statistic within a group to obtain the name and set of labels to be pushed in Prometheus.

params.name: prefix
params.doc: Appends a prefix to each statistic exported.

params.name: root
params.doc: Specifies the root metrics path Promethus uses to query the stats: http://[opensips_IP]:[opensips_httpd_port]/[root]

params.name: script_route
params.doc: Specifies the route name to be used to for adding custom prometheus information.

params.name: script_route_avp_result
params.doc: Specifies the AVP spec name to be used to for returning custom prometheus information.

params.name: statistics
params.doc: The statistics that are being exported by OpenSIPS, separated by space. The list can also contain statistics groups's names - to do that, you shall add a colon ( : ) at the end of the groups's name.

params.name: bin_async
params.doc: Specifies whether the TCP connect and write operations should be done in an asynchronous mode (non-blocking connect and write) or not. If disabled, OpenSIPS will block and wait for TCP operations like connect and write.

params.name: bin_async_local_connect_timeout
params.doc: If bin_async is enabled, this specifies the number of milliseconds that a connect will be tried in blocking mode (optimization). If the connect operation lasts more than this, the connect will go to async mode and will be passed to TCP MAIN for polling.

params.name: bin_async_local_write_timeout
params.doc: If bin_async is enabled, this specifies the number of milliseconds that a write op will be tried in blocking mode (optimization). If the write operation lasts more than this, the write will go to async mode and will be passed to bin MAIN for polling.

params.name: bin_async_max_postponed_chunks
params.doc: If bin_async is enabled, this specifies the maximum number of BIN messages that can be stashed for later/async writing. If the connection pending writes exceed this number, the connection will be marked as broken and dropped.

params.name: bin_max_msg_chunks
params.doc: The maximum number of chunks in which a BIN message is expected to arrive via TCP. If a received packet is more fragmented than this, the connection is dropped (either the connection is very overloaded and this leads to high fragmentation - or we are the victim of an ongoing attack where the attacker is sending very fragmented traffic in order to decrease server performance).

params.name: bin_port
params.doc: The default port to be used by all TCP listeners.

params.name: bin_send_timeout
params.doc: Time in milliseconds after a TCP connection will be closed if it is not available for blocking writing in this interval (and OpenSIPS wants to send something on it).

params.name: bins_async
params.doc: Specifies whether the TCP/TLS connect and write operations should be done in an asynchronous mode (non-blocking connect and write) or not. If disabled, OpenSIPS will block and wait for TCP/TLS operations like connect and write.

params.name: bins_async_handshake_timeout
params.doc: If tls_async is enabled, this specifies the number of milliseconds that a TLS handshake should be tried in blocking mode (optimization). If the handshake operation lasts more than this, the write will go to async mode and will be passed to tls MAIN for polling.

params.name: bins_async_local_connect_timeout
params.doc: If bin_async is enabled, this specifies the number of milliseconds that a connect will be tried in blocking mode (optimization). If the connect operation lasts more than this, the connect will go to async mode and will be passed to TCP MAIN for polling.

params.name: bins_async_max_postponed_chunks
params.doc: If bins_async is enabled, this specifies the maximum number of BINS messages that can be stashed for later/async writing. If the connection pending writes exceed this number, the connection will be marked as broken and dropped.

params.name: bins_handshake_timeout
params.doc: Sets the timeout (in milliseconds) for the SSL/TLS handshake sequence to complete. It may be necessary to increase this value when using a CPU intensive cipher for the connection to allow time for keys to be generated and processed.

params.name: bins_max_msg_chunks
params.doc: The maximum number of chunks in which a BINS message is expected to arrive via TCP. If a received packet is more fragmented than this, the connection is dropped (either the connection is very overloaded and this leads to high fragmentation - or we are the victim of an ongoing attack where the attacker is sending very fragmented traffic in order to decrease server performance).

params.name: bins_port
params.doc: The default port to be used by all BINS listeners.

params.name: bins_send_timeout
params.doc: Sets the timeout (in milliseconds) for blocking send operations to complete.

params.name: trace_destination
params.doc: Trace destination as defined in the tracing module. Currently the only tracing module is proto_hep . Network events such as connect, accept and connection closed events shall be traced along with errors that could appear in the process. For each connection that is created an event containing information about the client and server certificates, master key and network layer information shall be sent.

params.name: trace_on
params.doc: This controls whether tracing for tls is on or not. You still need to define in order to work, but this value will be controlled using mi function .

params.name: compressed_payload
params.doc: Exported by `proto_hep`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: hep_async
params.doc: Specifies whether the TCP connect and write operations should be done in an asynchronous mode (non-blocking connect and write) or not. If disabled, OpenSIPS will block and wait for TCP operations like connect and write.

params.name: hep_async_local_connect_timeout
params.doc: If hep_async is enabled, this specifies the number of milliseconds that a connect will be tried in blocking mode (optimization). If the connect operation lasts more than this, the connect will go to async mode and will be passed to TCP MAIN for polling.

params.name: hep_async_local_write_timeout
params.doc: If hep_async is enabled, this specifies the number of milliseconds that a write op will be tried in blocking mode (optimization). If the write operation lasts more than this, the write will go to async mode and will be passed to bin MAIN for polling.

params.name: hep_async_max_postponed_chunks
params.doc: If hep_async is enabled, this specifies the maximum number of HEP messages that can be stashed for later/async writing. If the connection pending writes exceed this number, the connection will be marked as broken and dropped.

params.name: hep_capture_id
params.doc: The parameter indicate the capture agent ID for HEPv2/v3 protocol. Limitation: 16-bit integer.

params.name: hep_id
params.doc: Specify a destination for HEP packets and the version of HEP protocol used. All parameters inside hep_id must be separated by ; . The parameters are given in key-value format, the possible keys being uri , transport and version , except destiantion's URI which doesn't have a key and is in host:port . transport key can be TCP , UDP or TLS . TCP and TLS works only for HEP version 3. Version is the hep protocol version and can be 1 , 2 or 3 .

params.name: hep_max_msg_chunks
params.doc: The maximum number of chunks in which a HEP message is expected to arrive via TCP. If a received packet is more fragmented than this, the connection is dropped (either the connection is very overloaded and this leads to high fragmentation - or we are the victim of an ongoing attack where the attacker is sending very fragmented traffic in order to decrease server performance).

params.name: hep_port
params.doc: The default port to be used by all TCP/UDP/TLS listeners.

params.name: hep_send_timeout
params.doc: Time in milliseconds after a TCP connection will be closed if it is not available for blocking writing in this interval (and OpenSIPS wants to send something on it).

params.name: homer5_delim
params.doc: In case homer5_on is set (different than 0), with this parameter you will be able to set the delmiter between different payload parts.

params.name: homer5_on
params.doc: Specify how the data should be encapsulated in the HEP packet. If set to 0 , then the JSON based HOMER 6 format will be used. Otherwise, if set to anything different than 0 , the plain text HOMER 5 format will be used for encapsulation. On the capturing node, this parameter affects the behavior of the report_capture function from the sipcapture module.

functions.name: correlate
functions.doc: Send a hep message with an extra correlation id containing the two correlation given as arguments. The two types must differ. This will help on the capturing side to correlate two calls for example, being given their callid as correlation ids.

params.name: allowed_algorithms
params.doc: Whitelists the authentication and encryption algorithms that can be used for IPSec.

params.name: default_client_port
params.doc: Default port value to be used when we act as clients in the IPSec communication.

params.name: default_server_port
params.doc: Default port value to be used when we act as server in the IPSec communication.

params.name: disable_deprecated_algorithms
params.doc: Indicates whether we should ignore deprecated algorithms, as defined in TS 33.203 (3G Security: Access Security for IP-based Services). At the moment, this disables the following algorithms: hmac-md5-96 and hmac-sha-1-96 authentication algorithms des-ede3-cbc and aes-cbc encryption algorithms

params.name: max_spi
params.doc: This parameter represents the maximum value for the Security Association's (SA) SPI parameter. In conjunction with the min_spi setting, it defines the SPI range [min_spi, max_spi] that must be unique within the system.

params.name: min_spi
params.doc: This parameter represents the minimum value for the Security Association's (SA) SPI parameter. In conjunction with the max_spi setting, it defines the SPI range [min_spi, max_spi] that must be unique within the system.

params.name: port
params.doc: Default IPSec port used when no prot is being specified in the socket global parameter.

params.name: temporary_timeout
params.doc: Sets the timeout (in seconds) a temporary security association can be stored in memory until in is confirmed (or used) by the remote endpoint.

functions.name: ipsec_create
functions.doc: Creates an IPSec SA/tunnel according to the Security-Client header and the AKA information received in the 401 reply.

params.name: cert_check_on_conn_reusage
params.doc: This parameter turns on or off the extra checking/matching of the TLS domain (SSL certificate) when comes to reusing an existing TLS connection. Without this extra check, only IP and port of the connections will be check (in order to re-use an existing connection). With this extra check, the connection to be reused must have the same SSL certificate as the one set for the current signaling operation.

params.name: max_msg_chunks
params.doc: Exported by `proto_msrp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: send_timeout
params.doc: Exported by `proto_msrp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: tls_handshake_timeout
params.doc: Sets the timeout (in milliseconds) for the SSL handshake sequence to complete. It may be necessary to increase this value when using a CPU intensive cipher for the connection to allow time for keys to be generated and processed.

params.name: trace_destination
params.doc: Exported by `proto_msrp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: trace_filter_route
params.doc: Exported by `proto_msrp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: trace_on
params.doc: Exported by `proto_msrp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: sctp_port
params.doc: The default port to be used for all SCTP related operation. Be careful as the default port impacts both the SIP listening part (if no port is defined in the SCTP listeners) and the SIP sending part (if the destination SCTP URI has no explicit port).

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database handler where the SMPP connection will be stored. This parameter is mandatory.

params.name: dst_npi_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: dst_ton_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: ip_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: name_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: outbound_uri
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: password_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: port_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: session_type_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: smpp_max_msg_chunks
params.doc: The maximum number of chunks in which a SMPP message is expected to arrive via TCP. If a received packet is more fragmented than this, the connection is dropped (either the connection is very overloaded and this leads to high fragmentation - or we are the victim of an ongoing attack where the attacker is sending very fragmented traffic in order to decrease server performance).

params.name: smpp_port
params.doc: Used to change the default value of the SMPP port used to listen for new connections.

params.name: smpp_send_timeout
params.doc: Time in milliseconds after a TCP connection will be closed if it is not available for blocking writing in this interval (and OpenSIPS wants to send something on it).

params.name: smpp_table
params.doc: The name of the database table containing definitions of the SMSc servers used to connect to.

params.name: src_npi_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: src_ton_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: system_id_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: system_type_col
params.doc: Exported by `proto_smpp`; not documented in the module README.

functions.name: send_smpp_message
functions.doc: This function is used to convert a SIP message received in the OpenSIPS script to a SMPP PDU and send it to the smsc_name (string) received as parameter. The SMPP parameters used to construct the PDU are provisione in the database, and the command sent is either submit_sm or deliver_sm , depending on the type of the SMSc.

params.name: cert_check_on_conn_reusage
params.doc: Exported by `proto_tls`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: tls_async
params.doc: If the TLS connect and write operations should be done in an asynchronous mode (non-blocking connect and write). If disabled, OpenSIPS will block and wait for TLS operations like connect and write.

params.name: tls_async_handshake_timeout
params.doc: Exported by `proto_tls`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: tls_async_local_connect_timeout
params.doc: Exported by `proto_tls`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: tls_async_max_postponed_chunks
params.doc: Exported by `proto_tls`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: tls_crlf_drop
params.doc: Drop CRLF (\r\n) ping messages. When this parameter is enabled, the TLS layer drops packets that contains a single CRLF message. If a CRLFCRLF message is received, it is handled according to the tls_crlf_pingpong parameter.

params.name: tls_crlf_pingpong
params.doc: Send CRLF pong (\r\n) to incoming CRLFCRLF ping messages over TLS. By default it is enabled (1).

params.name: tls_handshake_timeout
params.doc: Sets the timeout (in milliseconds) for the SSL handshake sequence to complete. It may be necessary to increase this value when using a CPU intensive cipher for the connection to allow time for keys to be generated and processed.

params.name: tls_max_msg_chunks
params.doc: The maximum number of chunks that a SIP message is expected to arrive via TLS. If a packet is received more fragmented than this, the connection is dropped (either the connection is very overloaded and this leads to high fragmentation - or we are the victim of an ongoing attack where the attacker is sending the traffic very fragmented in order to decrease server performance).

params.name: tls_port
params.doc: The default port to be used for all TLS related operation. Be careful as the default port impacts both the SIP listening part (if no port is defined in the TLS listeners) and the SIP sending part (if the destination URI has no explicit port).

params.name: tls_send_timeout

In this route you will have information regarding source and destination ips and ports for the current connection. To disable tracing for a specific connection the last call in this route must be drop , any other exit mode resulting in tracing the current connection ( of course you still have to define a and trace must be on at the time this connection is opened.

For each connection that is created an event containing information about http request and reply belonging to web socket protocol handshake and network layer information shall be sent.

params.name: wss_resource

params.name: wss_tls_handshake_timeout
params.doc: Sets the timeout (in milliseconds) for the SSL handshake sequence to complete. It may be necessary to increase this value when using a CPU intensive cipher for the connection to allow time for keys to be generated and processed.

params.name: cluster_id
params.doc: The cluster ID where the PUA data should be replicated/shared. This parameter is to be used only if clustering mode is needed. In order to understand the concept of a cluster ID, please see the clusterer module.

params.name: cluster_sharing_tag
params.doc: The clustering share-tag to be used by the PUA module when creating any new presentity record. The tag will by used to decide which OpenSIPS instance (owning the tag as active) will be responsible for expiring this presentity. This parameter is to be used only if clustering mode is needed. In order to understand the concept of sharing TAG, please see the clusterer module.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The name of the database table.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database url.

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: The default expires value used in case this information is not provisioned.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table used for storing Subscribe and Publish information. This parameter will be used as the power of 2 when computing table size.

params.name: min_expires
params.doc: The inferior expires limit for both Publish and Subscribe.

params.name: update_period
params.doc: The interval at which the information in database and hash table should be updated. In the case of the hash table updating is deleting expired messages.

functions.name: pua_update_contact
functions.doc: The remote target can be updated by the Contact of a subsequent in dialog request. In the PUA watcher case (sending a SUBSCRIBE messages), this means that the remote target for the following Subscribe messages can be updated at any time by the contact of a Notify message. If this function is called on request route on receiving a Notify message, it will try to update the stored remote target.

params.name: default_domain
params.doc: The default domain for the registered users to be used when constructing the uri for the registrar callback.

params.name: header_name
params.doc: The name of the header to be added to Publish requests. It will contain the uri of the user agent that sent the Notify that is transformed into Publish. It stops sending a Notification with the same information to the sender.

params.name: outbound_proxy
params.doc: The outbound_proxy uri to be used when sending Subscribe requests.

params.name: presence_server
params.doc: The address of the presence server - will be used as an outbound proxy when sending PUBLISH requests. It is optional.

params.name: server_address
params.doc: The IP address of the server.

functions.name: bla_handle_notify
functions.doc: The function handles Notify requests sent from phones on the same BLA to the server. The message is transformed in Publish request and passed to presence module for further handling. in case of a successful processing a 2xx reply should be sent.

functions.name: bla_set_flag
functions.doc: The function is used to mark REGISTER requests made to a BLA AOR. The modules subscribes to the registered contacts for dialog;sla event.

params.name: callee_spec_param
params.doc: The name of the pseudovariable that will hold the callee URI. If this variable will not be set, the callee information used will be made of To display uri + RURI. the. The format of the string to set this pseudovariable to is the same as described in caller_spec_param section.

params.name: caller_confirmed
params.doc: Usually the dialog-info of the caller will be "trying -> early -> confirmed" and the dialog-info of the callee will be "early -> confirmed". On some phones the function LED will start blinking if the state is early, regardless if is is the caller or the callee (indicated with the "direction" parameter). To avoid blinking LEDs for the caller, you can enable this parameter. Then the state of the caller will be singaled as "confirmed" even in "early" state. This is a workaround for the buggy Linksys SPA962 phones. SNOM phones work well with the default setting.

params.name: caller_spec_param
params.doc: The name of the pseudovariable that will hold a custom caller URI. If this variable is not set, the information in From header is used. If you want to use another caller definition, you have to fill in this pseudovariable before calling function. The format of the string resemples the format of To/From SIP headers: "display_name" or "sip_uri".

params.name: include_callid
params.doc: If this parameter is set, the optional call-id will be put into the dialog element. This is needed for call-pickup features.

params.name: include_localremote
params.doc: If this parameter is set, the optional local and remote elements will be put into the dialog element. This is needed for call-pickup features.

params.name: include_tags
params.doc: If this parameter is set, the local and remote tag will be put into the dialog element. This is needed for call-pickup features.

params.name: nopublish_flag
params.doc: By default, reINVITEs will trigger a PUBLISH. They are actually the only in-dialog request for which it makes sense. In some cases, it does not make sense to republish a dialog state. (e.g. when handling a B2BUA reINVITE). This setting defines the flag that needs to be set in the request route to prevent the generation of a PUBLISH request in case of a specific reINVITE.

params.name: osips_ps
params.doc: It is advisable to specify if you use a different presence server than OpenSIPS presence server, by setting this parameter to 0. By default, a trick (version in the Publish body is set '0000000') is used when working with Opensips Presence Server to make the processing faster and this might not be accepted by other presence servers.

params.name: presence_server
params.doc: The address of the presence server, where the PUBLISH messages should be sent (not compulsory).

params.name: publish_on_trying
params.doc: Usually the dialog-info of the caller will be "trying -> early -> confirmed". The "trying" state will be triggered as soon as you call on the caller, while "early" is triggered as soon as the callee is ringing (triggered by a 180 or 183 provisional reply). Sometimes, it is advisable to be notified only when the callee reaches the early state and not before. In other cases, it is advisable to notify the early state. This setting allows controlling the behavior.

functions.name: dialoginfo_mute_branch
functions.doc: This function must be called for INVITE messages, in the branch route only, in order to mute the publishing of the dialoginfo information for caller/callee/both parties involved in that branch.

functions.name: dialoginfo_set
functions.doc: This function must be called for INVITE messages that initialize a dialog for which dialoginfo information must be published.

functions.name: dialoginfo_set_branch_callee
functions.doc: This function is to be used only from a branch route for setting a per-branch callee/peer specification. This peer value will be used onyl for the dialoginfo record created for that particular branch.

params.name: presence_server
params.doc: The the address of the presence server. If set, it will be used as outbound proxy when sending PUBLISH requests.

functions.doc: Function that handles Notify messages addressed to a user from an xmpp domain. It requires filtering after method and domain in configuration file. If the function is successful, a 2xx reply must be sent.

functions.name: pua_xmpp_req_winfo
functions.doc: Function called when a Subscribe addressed to a user from a xmpp domain is received. It calls sending a Subscribe for winfo for the user, and the following Notify with dialog-info is translated into a subscription in xmpp. It also requires filtering in configuration file, after method, domain and event(only for presence).

params.name: child_init_method
params.doc: The method called for each child process.

params.name: mod_init_function
params.doc: The method used to initialize the Python module and return the object.

params.name: script_name
params.doc: The script that contains the Python module.

functions.name: python_exec
functions.doc: This function is used to execute a method from the Python module loaded.

params.name: qos_flag
params.doc: Keeping with OpenSIPS, the module will not do anything to any message unless instructed to do so via the config script. You must set the qos_flag value in the setflag() call of the INVITE you want the qos module to process. But before you can do that, you need to tell the qos module which flag value you are assigning to qos.

params.name: algorithm
params.doc: Quality-based destination selection/balancing algorithm to use.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: An SQL database URL.

params.name: decimal_digits
params.doc: The amount of decimal digits to use in logging or MI output.

params.name: event_bad_dst_threshold
params.doc: The minimally accepted quality of a (prefix, destination) combination, given as a quoted floating point number in the [0, 1] interval. Whenever a (prefix, destination) combination receives a score below this threshold, the event will be triggered.

params.name: extra_stats
params.doc: A semicolon-separated list of custom statistics to be additionally kept and monitored by the module. In order to gather these statistics, the module expects the script writer to call whenever they want to increment a custom statistic for a (prefix, destination) tuple.

params.name: history_span
params.doc: The duration (in minutes) that a gateway's statistics for a given call will be kept for.

params.name: min_samples_acd
params.doc: The minimally accepted amount of sampled ACD statistics for each (prefix, destination) pair before they can be taken into account. As long as the number of samples stays below this limit, the ACD statistic of the pair is assumed to be healthy.

params.name: min_samples_asr
params.doc: The minimally accepted amount of sampled ASR statistics for each (prefix, destination) pair before they can be taken into account. As long as the number of samples stays below this limit, the ASR statistic of the pair is assumed to be healthy.

params.name: min_samples_ast
params.doc: The minimally accepted amount of sampled AST statistics for each (prefix, destination) pair before they can be taken into account. As long as the number of samples stays below this limit, the AST statistic of the pair is assumed to be healthy.

params.name: min_samples_ccr
params.doc: The minimally accepted amount of sampled CCR statistics for each (prefix, destination) pair before they can be taken into account. As long as the number of samples stays below this limit, the CCR statistic of the pair is assumed to be healthy.

params.name: min_samples_pdd
params.doc: The minimally accepted amount of sampled PDD statistics for each (prefix, destination) pair before they can be taken into account. As long as the number of samples stays below this limit, the PDD statistic of the pair is assumed to be healthy.

params.name: sampling_interval
params.doc: The duration (in seconds) of the statistics sampling window. Every seconds, the accumulated statistics during the most recent sampling window get added to each gateway, while the oldest sampled interval statistics are subtracted (rotated away) from each gateway.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: The name of the quality-based routing profiles table.

functions.name: qr_disable_dst
functions.doc: Within a given routing rule, temporarily remove the given gateway or carrier from routing, until they are re-enabled via or . The removal effect will be lost on an OpenSIPS restart.

functions.name: qr_enable_dst
functions.doc: Within a given routing rule, re-introduce the given gateway or carrier into the routing process.

functions.name: qr_set_xstat
functions.doc: Provide a new sample value for an extra statistic on a given (prefix, gateway) combination. Extra statistics may be defined using the module parameter.

params.name: connect_timeout
params.doc: The maximally allowed duration (in milliseconds) for the establishment of a TCP connection with a RabbitMQ server.

params.name: server_id
params.doc: Specify configuration for a RabbitMQ server. It contains a set of parameters used to customize the connection to the server, as well as to the messages sent. The format of the parameter is [id_name] param1=value1; param2=value2; . The uri parameter is mandatory.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Indicates the timeout (in milliseconds) of any command (i.e. publish) sent to the RabbitMQ server.

params.name: use_tls
params.doc: Setting this parameter will allow you to use TLS for broker connections. In order to enable TLS for a specific connection, you can use the "tls_domain= dom_name " parameter in the configuration specified through the module parameter.

functions.name: rabbitmq_publish
functions.doc: Sends a publish message to a RabbitMQ server.

params.name: connect_timeout
params.doc: The maximally allowed duration (in milliseconds) for the establishment of a TCP connection with a RabbitMQ server.

params.name: connection_id
params.doc: Specify the configuration for a RabbitMQ connection. It contains a set of parameters used to customize the connection to the server as well as the consumer subscription. The format of the parameter is param1=value1; param2=value2; . The uri , queue and event parameters are mandatory.

params.name: retry_timeout
params.doc: The interval (in milliseconds) after which OpenSIPS will try to re-establish a failed AMQP connection to a RabbitMQ server.

params.name: use_tls

params.name: cachedb_url
params.doc: Enables distributed rate limiting and specifies the backend that should be used by the CacheDB interface.

params.name: db_prefix
params.doc: Specifies what prefix should be added to the pipe name. This is only used when distributed rate limiting is enabled.

params.name: default_algorithm
params.doc: Specifies which algorithm should be assumed in case it isn't explicitly specified in the rl_check function.

params.name: expire_time
params.doc: This parameter specifies how long a pipe should be kept in memory after it becomes idle (no more operations are performed on the pipe) until deleted.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The size of the hash table internally used to keep the pipes. A larger table is much faster but consumes more memory. The hash size must be a power of 2 number.

params.name: limit_per_interval
params.doc: This parameter configures the way that a pipe's limit is specified in the rl_check function and only affects the Taildrop and RED algorithms. A value of 1 means that the limit is set per- timer_interval while a value of 0 means per-second.

params.name: pipe_replication_cluster
params.doc: Specifies the cluster ID where pipes will be replicated to and received from.

params.name: repl_buffer_threshold
params.doc: Used to specify the length of the buffer used by the binary replication, in bytes, when a flush should be performed - the pipes gathered until then should be sent on the network. This is used to avoid using large amount of memory for pipes replication.

params.name: repl_timer_expire
params.doc: Timer in seconds, used to specify when the counter received from a different instance should no longer be taken into account. This is used to prevent obsolete values, in case an instance stops replicating its counters.

params.name: repl_timer_interval
params.doc: Timer in milliseconds, used to specify how often the module should replicate its counters to the other instances.

params.name: slot_period
params.doc: Value of one slot in milliseconds. This parameter determines how granular the algorithm should be. The number of slots will be determined by window_size/slot_period.

params.name: timer_interval
params.doc: The timer interval in seconds when the Network and Feedback algorithms run their queries, and the other algorithms reset their counters.

params.name: window_size
params.doc: How long the history in SBT should be in seconds.

functions.name: rl_check
functions.doc: Check the current request against the pipe identified by name and changes/updates the limit. If no pipe is found, then a new one is created with the specified limit and algorithm, if specified. If the algorithm parameter doesn't exist, the default one is used.

functions.name: rl_dec_count
functions.doc: This function decreases a counter that could have been previously increased by rl_check function.

functions.name: rl_reset_count
functions.doc: This function resets a counter that could have been previously increased by rl_check function.

params.name: file
params.doc: Text file containing the regular expression groups. It must be set in order to enable the group matching function.

params.name: group_max_size
params.doc: Max content size of a group in the text file.

params.name: max_groups
params.doc: Max number of regular expression groups in the text file.

params.name: pcre_caseless
params.doc: If this options is set, matching is done caseless. It is equivalent to Perl's /i option, and it can be changed within a pattern by a (?i) or (?-i) option setting.

params.name: pcre_dotall
params.doc: If this option is set, a dot metacharater in the pattern matches all characters, including those that indicate newline. Without it, a dot does not match when the current position is at a newline. This option is equivalent to Perl's /s option, and it can be changed within a pattern by a (?s) or (?-s) option setting.

params.name: pcre_extended
params.doc: If this option is set, whitespace data characters in the pattern are totally ignored except when escaped or inside a character class. Whitespace does not include the VT character (code 11). In addition, characters between an unescaped # outside a character class and the next newline, inclusive, are also ignored. This is equivalent to Perl's /x option, and it can be changed within a pattern by a (?x) or (?-x) option setting.

params.name: pcre_multiline
params.doc: By default, PCRE treats the subject string as consisting of a single line of characters (even if it actually contains newlines). The "start of line" metacharacter (^) matches only at the start of the string, while the "end of line" metacharacter ($) matches only at the end of the string, or before a terminating newline.

functions.name: pcre_match
functions.doc: Matches the given string parameter against the regular expression pcre_regex, which is compiled into a PCRE object. Returns TRUE if it matches, FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: pcre_match_group
functions.doc: It uses the groups readed from the text file (see ) to match the given string parameter against the compiled regular expression in group number group. Returns TRUE if it matches, FALSE otherwise.

params.name: attr_avp
params.doc: AVP to store specific additional information for each registration. This information is read from the AVP and stored (in memory, db or both) at every registrar 'save'. When a registrar 'lookup' or 'is_registered' function is called, the attr_avp is populated with the value saved at [re]registration.

params.name: case_sensitive
params.doc: If set to 1 then AOR comparison will be case sensitive (as RFC3261 instructs), if set to 0 then AOR comparison will be case insensitive.

params.name: default_expires
params.doc: If the processed message contains neither Expires HFs nor expires contact parameters, this value will be used for newly created usrloc records. The parameter contains number of second to expire (for example use 3600 for one hour).

params.name: default_q
params.doc: The parameter represents default q value for new contacts. Because OpenSIPS doesn't support float parameter types, the value in the parameter is divided by 1000 and stored as float. For example, if you want default_q to be 0.38, use value 380 here.

params.name: disable_gruu

params.name: gruu_secret
