params.name: realm_prefix
params.doc: Prefix to be automatically strip from realm. As an alternative to SRV records (not all SIP clients support SRV lookup), a subdomain of the master domain can be defined for SIP purposes (like sip.mydomain.net pointing to same IP address as the SRV record for mydomain.net). By ignoring the realm_prefix "sip.", at registration, sip.mydomain.net will be equivalent to mydomain.net .

params.name: received_avp
params.doc: Registrar will store the value of the AVP configured by this parameter in the received column in the user location database. It will leave the column empty if the AVP is empty. The AVP should contain a SIP URI consisting of the source IP, port, and protocol of the REGISTER message being processed.

params.name: received_param
params.doc: The name of the parameter that will be appended to Contacts of 200 OK when the received URI was set by nathelper module.

params.name: retry_after
params.doc: The registrar can generate 5xx reply to REGISTER in various situations. It can, for example, happen when the max_contacts parameter is set and the processing of REGISTER request would exceed the limit. In this case the registrar would generate "503 Service Unavailable" response.

params.name: sock_hdr_name
params.doc: Header which contains a socket description (proto:IP:port) to override the received socket info. The header will be search and used only if the flag 's' (Socket header) is set at "save()" time.

params.name: tcp_persistent_flag
params.doc: The parameter specifies the message flag to be used to control the module behaviour regarding TCP connections. If the flag is set for a REGISTER via TCP containing a TCP contact, the module, via the save() function, will set the lifetime of the TCP connection to the contact expire value. By doing this, the TCP connection will stay on as long as the contact is valid.

functions.name: add_sock_hdr
functions.doc: Adds to the current REGISTER request a new header with hdr_name which contains the description of the received socket (proto:ip:port)

functions.name: is_contact_registered
functions.doc: The function returns true if a contact and/or a callid from a certain AOR is registered, false otherwise. The function does not modify the message being process.

functions.name: is_ip_registered
functions.doc: The function returns true if there is at least one contact that has been registered from the IP in the IPvar variable ( and from the optional PORTvar variable ). The IP is matched against the received host, if it exists, or the contact host otherwise. This function does not modify the message being process. This function replaces the old "is_other_contact" function.

functions.name: is_registered
functions.doc: The function returns true if an AOR is registered, false otherwise. The function does not modify the message being process.

functions.name: lookup
functions.doc: The functions extracts username from Request-URI and tries to find all contacts for the username in usrloc. If there are no such contacts, -1 will be returned. If there are such contacts, Request-URI will be overwritten with the contact that has the highest q value and optionally the rest will be appended to the message (depending on append_branches parameter value).

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Explicitly remove contacts behind a given address-of-record.

functions.name: remove_ip_port
functions.doc: Remove all contacts behind a specific IP and Port, optionally filtering by AOR.

functions.name: save
functions.doc: The function processes a REGISTER message. It can add, remove or modify usrloc records depending on Contact and Expires HFs in the REGISTER message. On success, 200 OK will be returned listing all contacts that are currently in usrloc. On an error, error message will be send with a short description in reason phrase.

params.name: connect_poll_interval
params.doc: Only relevant with async requests. Allows complete control over how quickly we want to detect libcurl's completed blocking TCP/TLS handshakes, so the async transfers can be put in the background. A lower may speed up all async HTTP transfers, but will also increase CPU usage.

params.name: connection_timeout
params.doc: The maximum allowed time to establish a connection with the server.

params.name: curl_conn_lifetime
params.doc: Only relevant when is enabled. By setting this parameter, script developers can leverage the connection reusage capabilities of libcURL and entirely skip the "no concurrent transfers" logic on a given SIP worker, should that worker already be known to have a TCP connection to the target URL hostname (established by a previous rest_xxx() function call).

params.name: curl_http_version
params.doc: Use a specific HTTP version for all requests. Possible values:

params.name: curl_timeout
params.doc: The maximum allowed time for any HTTP(S) transfer to complete. This interval is inclusive of the initial connect time window, hence the value of this parameter must be greater than or equal to .

params.name: enable_expect_100
params.doc: Include a "Expect: 100-continue" HTTP header field whenever the body size of a POST or PUT request exceeds 1024 bytes. Once enabled, the timeout for waiting for a "100 Continue" reply from the server is 1 second, after which the body upload will begin.

params.name: max_async_transfers
params.doc: Maximum number of asynchronous HTTP transfers a single OpenSIPS worker is allowed to run simultaneously. As long as this threshold is reached for a worker, all new async transfers it attempts to perform will be done in a blocking manner, with appropriate logging warnings.

params.name: max_transfer_size
params.doc: The maximum allowed size of a single transfer (download). Reaching this limit during a transfer will cause the transfer to stop immediately, returning error -10 at script level. A value of 0 will disable the check.

params.name: no_concurrent_connects
params.doc: Set to true in order to only allow one OpenSIPS worker to connect to a given URL hostname at a time. While a worker is connecting, all other workers will receive error code -4 (already connecting) when attempting to perform any rest_client operation to the same hostname, regardless if the operation is sync or async.

params.name: ssl_capath
params.doc: An optional path for CA certificates to be used for host verifications.

params.name: ssl_verifyhost
params.doc: Set this to 0 in order to disable the verification that the remote peer actually corresponds to the server listed in the certificate.

params.name: ssl_verifypeer
params.doc: Set this to 0 in order to disable the verification of the remote peer's certificate. Verification is done using a default bundle of CA certificates which come with libcurl.

functions.name: rest_append_hf
functions.doc: Append txt to the HTTP headers of the subsequent request. Multiple headers can be appended by making multiple calls before executing a request.

functions.name: rest_get
functions.doc: Perform a blocking HTTP GET on the given url and return a representation of the resource.

functions.name: rest_init_client_tls
functions.doc: Force a specific TLS domain to be used at most once, during the next GET/POST/PUT request. Refer to the tls_mgm module for additional info regarding TLS client domains.

functions.name: rest_post
functions.doc: Perform a blocking HTTP POST on the given url .

functions.name: rest_put
functions.doc: Perform a blocking HTTP PUT on the given url .

params.name: clean_period
params.doc: The period at which to check for expired information.

params.name: contact_user
params.doc: This is the username that will be used in the Contact header for the 200 OK replies to SUBSCRIBE and in the following in-dialog NOTIFY requests, as well as for the SUBSCRIBE requests that are generated by the RLS server. The IP address, port and transport for the Contact will be automatically determined based on the interface where the SUBSCRIBE was received or sent from.

params.name: hash_size
params.doc: The dimension of the hash table used to store subscription to a list. This parameter will be used as the power of 2 when computing table size.

params.name: max_expires
params.doc: The maximum accepted expires for a subscription to a list.

params.name: presence_server
params.doc: The address of the presence server. It will be used as outbound proxy for Subscribe requests sent by the RLS server to bouncing on and off the proxy and having to include special processing for this messages in the proxy's configuration file.

params.name: rlpres_table
params.doc: The name of the db table where notified event specific information is stored.

params.name: rls_event
params.doc: The default event that RLS handles is presence. If some other events should also be handled by RLS they should be added using this parameter. It can be set more than once.

params.name: rlsubs_table
params.doc: The name of the db table where resource lists subscription information is stored.

params.name: to_presence_code
params.doc: The code to be returned by rls_handle_subscribe function if the processed Subscribe is not a resource list Subscribe. This code can be used in an architecture with presence and rls servers collocated on the same machine, to call handle_subscribe on the message causing this code.

params.name: waitn_time
params.doc: The timer period at which the server should attempt to send Notifies with the updated presence state of the subscribed list or watcher information.

params.name: xcap_root
params.doc: The address of the xcap server.

functions.name: rls_handle_notify
functions.doc: This function has to be called for Notify messages sent by presence servers in reply to the Subscribe messages sent by RLS.

functions.name: rls_handle_subscribe
functions.doc: This function detects if a Subscribe message should be handled by RLS. If not it replies with the configured to_presence_code. If it is, it extracts the dialog info and sends aggregate Notify requests with information for the list.

params.name: add_username
params.doc: If set to a non 0 value (which means yes), the username part will be also added in the Record-Route URI.

params.name: append_fromtag
params.doc: If turned on, request's from-tag is appended to record-route; that's useful for understanding whether subsequent requests (such as BYE) come from caller (route's from-tag==BYE's from-tag) or callee (route's from-tag==BYE's to-tag)

params.name: enable_double_rr
params.doc: There are some situations when the server needs to insert two Record-Route header fields instead of one. For example when using two disconnected networks or doing cross-protocol forwarding from UDP->TCP. This parameter enables inserting of 2 Record-Routes. The server will later remove both of them.

params.name: enable_socket_mismatch_warning
params.doc: When a preset record-route header is forced in OpenSIPS config and the host from the record-route header is not the same as the host server, a warning will be printed out in the logs. The 'enable_socket_mismatch_warning' parameter enables or disables the warning. When OpenSIPS is behind a NATed firewall, we don't want this warning to be printed for every bridged call.

params.name: ignore_user
params.doc: Exported by `rr`; not documented in the module README.

functions.name: add_rr_param
functions.doc: Adds a parameter to the Record-Route URI (param must be in ;name=value format. The function may be called also before or after the record_route() call (see ).

functions.name: check_route_param
functions.doc: The function checks if the URI parameters of the local Route header (corresponding to the local server) matches the given regular expression. It must be call after loose_route() (see ).

functions.name: is_direction
functions.doc: The function checks the flow direction of the request. As for checking it's used the ftag Route header parameter, the append_fromtag (see module parameter must be enabled. Also this must be called only after loose_route() (see ).

functions.name: loose_route
functions.doc: The function performs routing of SIP requests which contain a route set. The name is a little bit confusing, as this function also routes requests which are in the strict router format.

functions.name: record_route
functions.doc: The function adds a new Record-Route header field. The header field will be inserted in the message before any other Record-Route header fields.

functions.name: record_route_preset
functions.doc: This function will put the string into Record-Route, don't use unless you know what you are doing.

functions.name: rtp_relay_engage
functions.doc: Engages the RTP Relay engine for the current initial INVITE. After calling this function, the entire RTP relay communication will be handled by the module itself, without having to intervene for any further in-dialog requests/replies (unless you specifically want to).

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The table where the RTPEngines sockets are stored. Used when Database URL is provisioned.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL, used to load RTPEngines sockets from db, instead of specifying them in the script ( module parameter).

params.name: error_pv
params.doc: The parameter defines a variable that shall be populated by rtp when one of the rtpengine_* functions fail.

params.name: extra_id_pv
params.doc: The parameter sets the PV definition to use when the via-branch=extra option is used on the rtpengine_delete(), rtpengine_offer(), rtpengine_answer() or rtpengine_manage() commands.

params.name: notification_sock
params.doc: An UDP socket formatted as IP:port that indicates the listening IP and port OpenSIPS will bind for to receive notifications (such as DTMF events) from RTPengine.

params.name: rtpengine_disable_tout
params.doc: Once an rtp proxy was found unreachable and marked as disabled, the rtpengine module will not attempt to establish communication to that rtp proxy for rtpengine_disable_tout seconds.

params.name: rtpengine_retr
params.doc: How many times the module should retry to send and receive after timeout was generated.

params.name: rtpengine_sock
params.doc: Definition of socket(s) used to connect to (a set) rtp proxy. It may specify a UNIX socket or an IPv4/IPv6 UDP socket. If the protocol part (i.e. udp: ) is missing, the socket is treated as a UNIX socket.

params.name: rtpengine_timer_interval
params.doc: Frequency to scan rtpengine sets for disabled node probing. Probing is done outside the SIP processing context and in a separate timer routine. Disabled nodes are probed for re-enablement after rtpengine_disable_tout seconds. Setting this value too high can lead to unexpectedly large disabled interval as the max interval before probing is (rtpengine_timer_interval + rtpengine_disable_tout) seconds.

params.name: rtpengine_tout
params.doc: Timeout value in waiting for reply from rtp proxy.

params.name: set_column
params.doc: The name of the rtpengine set column in the database table.

params.name: setid_avp
params.doc: The parameter defines an AVP that, if set, determines which rtp proxy set rtpengine_offer(), rtpengine_answer(), rtpengine_delete(), and rtpengine_manage() functions use.

params.name: socket_column
params.doc: The name of the rtpengine socket column in the database table.

functions.name: rtpengine_answer
functions.doc: Rewrites sdp body to ensure that media is passed through an rtp proxy. To be invoked on 200 OK for the cases the SDPs are in INVITE and 200 OK and on ACK when SDPs are in 200 OK and ACK.

functions.name: rtpengine_block_dtmf
functions.doc: This function will block the DTMF media sent from one of the endpoints. The direction to be blocked is controled by the flags parameter, the from-tag value.

functions.name: rtpengine_block_media
functions.doc: This function will block the media sent from one of the endpoints. The direction to be blocked is controled by the flags parameter, the from-tag value.

functions.name: rtpengine_delete
functions.doc: Tears down the RTPEngine session for the current call.

functions.name: rtpengine_manage
functions.doc: Manage the RTPEngine session - it combines the functionality of rtpengine_offer(), rtpengine_answer() and rtpengine_delete(), detecting internally based on message type and method which one to execute.

functions.name: rtpengine_offer
functions.doc: Rewrites sdp body to ensure that media is passed through an rtp proxy. To be invoked on INVITE for the cases the SDPs are in INVITE and 200 OK and on 200 OK when SDPs are in 200 OK and ACK.

functions.name: rtpengine_play_dtmf
functions.doc: This function instructs rtp to send the DTMF code to the participant of the call. The code can be a digit ( 0-9 ) or a special character (one of *,#,A,B,C,D ). Additional parameters can be configured using the flags parameter. For more information, please consult the rtp documentation.

functions.name: rtpengine_play_media
functions.doc: This function will start playing a media file to one of the endpoints.

functions.name: rtpengine_start_forwarding
functions.doc: This function will start forwarding the media to a TLS destination specified in the tls-send-to parmeter of RTPEngine. This function allows you to select the media stream to forward, by specifing the from-tag of the entity you want to forward the media. If missing, all media streams are forwarded.

functions.name: rtpengine_start_recording
functions.doc: This function will send a signal to the rtp proxy to record the RTP stream on the rtp proxy.

functions.name: rtpengine_stop_forwarding
functions.doc: This function will stop forwarding of the media previously started using the rtpengine_start_forwarding() function.

functions.name: rtpengine_stop_media
functions.doc: This function will stop playing a media file previously started by a rtpengine_play_media() call. The meaning of its parameters is similar to the previous functions. Note that this function should be called with similar parameters as its matching rtpengine_play_media() call, otherwise RTPEngine will not be able to stop media playing.

functions.name: rtpengine_stop_recording
functions.doc: This function will send a signal to the rtp proxy to stop recording the RTP stream on the rtp proxy.

functions.name: rtpengine_unblock_dtmf
functions.doc: This function will resume/unblock the DTMF media sent from one of the endpoints. The direction to be blocked is controled by the flags parameter, the from-tag value.

functions.name: rtpengine_unblock_media
functions.doc: This function will resume/unblock the media sent from one of the endpoints. The direction to be blocked is controled by the flags parameter, the from-tag value.

functions.name: rtpengine_use_set
functions.doc: Sets the ID of the rtp proxy set to be used for the next rtpengine_delete(), rtpengine_offer(), rtpengine_answer() or rtpengine_manage() command. The parameter is an integer.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The name of the database table containing definitions of socket(s) used to connect to (a set) RTPProxy.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url. This parameter should be set if you want to use a database table from where to load or reload definitions of socket(s) used to connect to (a set) RTPProxy. The record from the database table will be read at start up (added to the ones defined with the rtpproxy_sock module parameter) and when the MI command rtpproxy_reload is issued(the definitions will be replaced with the ones from the database table).

params.name: default_set
params.doc: The parameter indicates the default RTPProxy set to be used when provisioning an engine in the config file without an explicit set, or when calling one of the rtpproxy_*() functions without an explicit set.

params.name: generated_sdp_media_ip
params.doc: When RTPProxy module needs to generate an SDP body, use this value as the media_ip in the c= and the o= .

params.name: generated_sdp_port_max
params.doc: When RTPProxy module needs to generate an SDP body, use this value as the maximum value of the port.

params.name: generated_sdp_port_min
params.doc: When RTPProxy module needs to generate an SDP body, use this value as the minimum value of the port.

params.name: nortpproxy_str
params.doc: The parameter sets the SDP attribute used by rtpproxy to mark the packet SDP informations have already been mangled.

params.name: rtpp_notify_socket
params.doc: The socket OpenSIPS listens for notifications from RTPProxy. Currently OpenSIPS can receive RTP timeout and DTMF events.

params.name: rtpp_socket_col
params.doc: The name rtpp socket column in the database table.

params.name: rtpproxy_autobridge
params.doc: Enable auto-bridging feature. Does not properly function when doing serial/parallel forking!

params.name: rtpproxy_disable_tout
params.doc: Once RTPProxy was found unreachable and marked as disable, rtpproxy will not attempt to establish communication to RTPProxy for rtpproxy_disable_tout seconds.

params.name: rtpproxy_retr
params.doc: How many times rtpproxy should retry to send and receive after timeout was generated.

params.name: rtpproxy_sock
params.doc: Definition of socket(s) used to connect to (a set) RTPProxy. It may specify a UNIX socket, an IPv4/IPv6 UDP socket or an IPv4/IPv6 TCP socket. If the protocol part (i.e. udp: ) is missing, the socket is treated as a UNIX socket.

params.name: rtpproxy_timeout
params.doc: Timeout value in waiting for reply from RTPProxy.

params.name: set_id_col
params.doc: The name set id column in the database table.

functions.name: rtpproxy_all_stats
functions.doc: This command gathers all RTP statistics available from RTP-Proxy. All the returned values stored in an AVP that can be further read by indexing the AVP.

functions.name: rtpproxy_answer
functions.doc: Rewrites sdp body to ensure that media is passed through an rtp proxy. To be invoked on 200 OK for the cases the SDPs are in INVITE and 200 OK and on ACK when SDPs are in 200 OK and ACK.

functions.name: rtpproxy_engage
functions.doc: Rewrites sdp body to ensure that media is passed through an rtp proxy. It uses the dialog module facilities to keep track when the rtpproxy session must be updated. Function must only be called for the initial INVITE and internally takes care of rewriting the body of 200 OKs and ACKs. Note that when used in bridge mode, this function might advertise wrong interfaces in sdp (due to the fact that OpenSIPS is not aware of the RTPProxy configuration), so you might face an undefined behavior.

functions.name: rtpproxy_offer
functions.doc: Rewrites sdp body to ensure that media is passed through an rtp proxy. To be invoked on INVITE for the cases the SDPs are in INVITE and 200 OK and on 200 OK when SDPs are in 200 OK and ACK.

functions.name: rtpproxy_start_recording
functions.doc: This command will send a signal to the RTP-Proxy to record the RTP stream on the RTP-Proxy.

functions.name: rtpproxy_stats
functions.doc: This command gathers call RTP statistics from RTP-Proxy.

functions.name: rtpproxy_unforce
functions.doc: Tears down the RTPProxy session for the current call.

params.name: create_dialog_flags
params.doc: Flags used when creating dialogs. For details on these flags, please refer to the create_dialog() function of the dialog module.

params.name: sequential_route
params.doc: Optional route to be run just before sequential requests are relayed. If the exit script statement is used inside this route, the module assumes that the relaying logic has been handled.

params.name: use_dialog
params.doc: Enables dialog support. Note that the dialog module must be loaded before this module when setting this parameter.

functions.name: send_reply
functions.doc: For the current request, a reply is sent back having the given code and text reason. The reply is sent stateless or statefull depending on which module is loaded and if a transaction was created, as explained above.

params.name: country_code
params.doc: Country Code that the first part of the number from P-Asserted-Identity is tested against when trying to map the Calling Party Number ISUP parameter from SIP by default. If there is a match, the value assigned to the Nature of Address Indicator subfield is 3 (national), otherwise it is 4 (international).

params.name: default_part_headers
params.doc: The default set of headers (fully defined, including the header termination) to be pushed into the ISUP part together with the Content-Type header.

params.name: isup_mime_str
params.doc: The string to be used for the Content-Type header field of the ISUP MIME body when creating a new ISUP part.

params.name: param_subfield_separator
params.doc: The character to be used as separator in the subname of the $isup_param and $isup_param_str pseudovariables between the ISUP parameter name and subfield name.

functions.name: add_isup_part
functions.doc: Adds a new ISUP part to the SIP message body.

params.name: auth_user_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: authorization_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: callid_aleg_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: callid_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: capture_node
params.doc: Name of the capture node.

params.name: capture_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable capture globaly (on(1)/off(0))

params.name: contact_ip_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: contact_port_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: contact_user_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: content_type_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: cseq_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: date_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Database URL.

params.name: destination_ip_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: destination_port_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: diversion_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: family_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: from_tag_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: from_user_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: hep_capture_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable capture of HEP (on(1)/off(0))

params.name: hep_route
params.doc: Specifies what path your hep messages should take. Possible values are the following:

params.name: id_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: max_async_queries
params.doc: Parameter to set the maximum number of 'INSERT' queries of captured packets to be done in the same time, only if the DB supports async operations. If OpenSIPS is shut down, the remaining queries shall be executed. The query buffer is limited 65535 chars, so probably no more than 30-40 queries can be done in the same time, depending mostly on the size of the inserted sip message, since it's the biggest part of the query.

params.name: method_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: micro_ts_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: msg_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: node_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: originator_ip_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: originator_port_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: pid_user_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: promiscious_on
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: proto_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: raw_interface
params.doc: Name of the interface to bind on the raw socket.

params.name: raw_ipip_capture_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable IPIP capturing (on(1)/off(0))

params.name: raw_moni_bpf_on
params.doc: Activate Linux Socket Filter (LSF based on BPF) on the mirroring interface. The structure is defined in linux/filter.h. The default LSF accept a port/portrange from the raw_socket_listen param. Currently LSF supported only on Linux.

params.name: raw_moni_capture_on
params.doc: Parameter to enable/disable monitoring/mirroring port capturing (on(1)/off(0)) Only one mode on raw socket can be enabled! Monitoring port capturing currently supported only on Linux.

params.name: raw_sock_children
params.doc: Parameter define how much children must be created to listen the raw socket.

params.name: raw_socket_listen
params.doc: Parameter indicate an listen IP address of RAW socket for IPIP capturing. You can also define a port/portrange for IPIP/Mirroring mode, to capture SIP messages in specific ports: "10.0.0.1:5060" - the source/destination port of the SIP message must be equal 5060 "10.0.0.1:5060-5090" - the source/destination port of the SIP message must be equal or be between 5060 and 5090. The port/portrange must be defined if you are planning to use mirroring capture! In this case, the part with IP address will be ignored, but to make parser happy, use i.e. 10.0.0.0

params.name: reason_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: reply_reason_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: rtcp_table_name
params.doc: Name of the table's name where to store packets captured with report_capture function. Since version 2.2 it allows strftime-like suffix for having time formatted table names.

params.name: rtp_stat_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: ruri_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: ruri_user_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: source_ip_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: source_port_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: table_name
params.doc: Name of the table's name where to store the SIP messages. Since version 2.2 it allows strftime-like suffix for having time formatted table names.

params.name: to_tag_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: to_user_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: type_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: user_agent_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: via_1_branch_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: via_1_column
params.doc: Exported by `sipcapture`; not documented in the module README.

functions.name: hep_del
functions.doc: Removes a hep chunk.

functions.name: hep_get
functions.doc: Set a hep chunk. If not exists, it shall be added.

functions.name: hep_relay
functions.doc: Relay a message statefully to destination indicated in current URI. (If the original URI was rewritten by UsrLoc, RR, strip/prefix, etc., the new URI will be taken). The message has to have been a HEP message, version 1, 2 or 3. For version 1 and 2 you can relay only using UDP, for version 3 TCP and UDP can be used.

functions.name: hep_resume_sip
functions.doc: Break hep route execution and resume into the main request route.

functions.name: hep_set
functions.doc: Set a hep chunk. If not exists, it shall be added.

functions.name: report_capture
functions.doc: Save the message into the database. If you want set the protocol type you have to define the table name, even if you pass over it(report_capture($var(cor_id),,$var(proto_type))).

functions.name: sip_capture
functions.doc: Save the message into the database.

functions.name: add_body_part
functions.doc: This function can be used to add a new body part to the message body. If another part already exist, body of the message will be converted to a multi-part body automatically.

functions.name: append_body_to_reply
functions.doc: Append 'txt' as body to all replies that will be generated by OpenSIPS for this request.

functions.name: append_hf
functions.doc: Appends 'txt' as header after the last header field. If 'hdr_anchor' is given, 'txt' will be appended after the first occurrence of 'hdr_anchor' instead.

functions.name: append_time
functions.doc: Adds a time header to the reply of the request. You must use it before functions that are likely to send a reply, e.g., save() from 'registrar' module. Header format is: Date: %a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S GMT , with the legend: %a abbreviated week of day name (locale) %d day of month as decimal number %b abbreviated month name (locale) %Y year with century %H hour %M minutes %S seconds

functions.name: append_to_reply
functions.doc: Append 'txt' as header to all replies that will be generated by OpenSIPS for this request.

functions.name: append_urihf
functions.doc: Append header field name with original Request-URI in middle.

functions.name: codec_delete
functions.doc: This function can be used to delete a codec from inside an sdp payload. It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be deleted from the mapping ("a=...") and from the list of indexes ("m=..."). Returns TRUE if any deletion occurred otherwise it will return FALSE.

functions.name: codec_delete_except_re
functions.doc: This function deletes all the codecs except those specified by the regular expression.

functions.name: codec_delete_re
functions.doc: This function has the same effect as codec_delete ( without the clock parameter ) the only difference is that it takes a POSIX regular expression as a parameter.

functions.name: codec_exists
functions.doc: This function can be used to verify if a codec exists inside an sdp payload. It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will return TRUE otherwise it will return FALSE.

functions.name: codec_exists_re
functions.doc: This function has the same effect as codec_exists ( without the clock parameter ) the only difference is that it takes a POSIX regular expression as a parameter.

functions.name: codec_move_down
functions.doc: This function can be used to move a codec down in the list of indexes ("m=..."). It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be moved to the back of the index list. Returns TRUE if any moves occurred otherwise it will return FALSE. The second parameter is optional, if it is not supplied any clockrate will match and all codecs will be moved to the back while preserving their original ordering. Parameters are CASE INSENSITIVE.

functions.name: codec_move_down_re
functions.doc: This function has the same effect as codec_move_down ( without the clock parameter ) the only difference is that it takes a POSIX regular expression as a parameter.

functions.name: codec_move_up
functions.doc: This function can be used to move a codec up in the list of indexes ("m=..."). It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be moved to the top of the index list. Returns TRUE if any moves occurred otherwise it will return FALSE.

functions.name: codec_move_up_re
functions.doc: This function has the same effect as codec_move_up ( without the clock parameter ) the only difference is that it takes a POSIX regular expression as a parameter.

functions.name: get_glob_headers_values
functions.doc: Populates the hdr_names_avp and hdr_vals_avp AVPs with all the header names and values that match the hdr_name_glob pattern.

functions.name: get_updated_body_part
functions.doc: This function returns into a variable the regenerated body part, meaning the body part updated with all the changes done so far by OpenSIPS. This is helpful if you want to do a sequance of operations over the body parts and some operations require to have all the previous changes applied (like first doing some codec related changes and later to rtpengine insertion).

functions.name: has_body_part
functions.doc: The function returns true if the SIP message has any body part with the given MIME. If there is no MIME given, it will return true if at least one body part is found (with any MIME).

functions.name: has_totag
functions.doc: Check if To header field uri contains tag parameter.

functions.name: insert_hf
functions.doc: Inserts 'txt' as header before the first header field.

functions.name: insert_hf_2
functions.doc: Inserts 'txt' as header before first 'hdr' header field.

functions.name: is_audio_on_hold
functions.doc: The function returns true if the SIP message has an SDP body attached and at least one audio stream in on hold. The return code of the function indicates the detected hold type: 1 - RFC2543 hold type: null connection IP detected 2 - RFC3264 hold type: inactive or sendonly attributes detected

functions.name: is_method
functions.doc: Check if the method of the message matches the name. If name is a known method (invite, cancel, ack, bye, options, info, update, register, message, subscribe, notify, refer, prack), the function performs method ID testing (integer comparison) instead of ignore case string comparison.

functions.name: is_present_hf
functions.doc: Return true if a header field is present in message.

functions.name: is_privacy
functions.doc: The function returns true if the SIP message has a Privacy header field that includes the given privacy_type among its privacy values. See https://www.iana.org/assignments/sip-parameters/sip-parameters.xhtml#sip-parameters-8 for possible privacy type values.

functions.name: is_uri_user_e164
functions.doc: Checks if the username part of the given URI is an E164 number.

functions.name: list_hdr_add_option
functions.doc: Add a new option/token at the end of the list in the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Disposition headers) body format

functions.name: list_hdr_has_option
functions.doc: Checks and returns true if the given option/token is listed in the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Dispsition headers) body format

functions.name: list_hdr_remove_option
functions.doc: Removes an option/token from the list inside the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Dispsition headers) body format

functions.name: remove_body_part
functions.doc: Removes from the message body all the body parts with the given mime. The necessary corrections over the Content-Type and Content-Length headers are automatically done.

functions.name: remove_hf
functions.doc: Remove from message all headers with name hname

functions.name: remove_hf_glob
functions.doc: Remove from message all headers matching the hname_pattern glob pattern.

functions.name: remove_hf_re
functions.doc: Remove from message all headers matching the hname_expr POSIX regular expression.

functions.name: ruri_add_param
functions.doc: Add to RURI an URI parameter formated as "name=value".

functions.name: ruri_del_param
functions.doc: Delete a parameter, its value and any leading ";" from the Request-URI of the current SIP message.

functions.name: ruri_has_param
functions.doc: Find if Request URI has a given parameter. If no value is given, the function will look for the paramter with no value, oherwise it will search for the parameter with the matching value.

functions.name: ruri_tel2sip
functions.doc: Converts RURI, if it is tel URI, to SIP URI. Returns true, only if conversion succeeded or if no conversion was needed (like RURI was not tel URI.

functions.name: sip_to_json
functions.doc: Returns a JSON formatted representation of the current SIP message, containing first_line , headers and body json members Useful in cases when you want to pass a generic SIP message to a SIP agnostic entity, but still want to provide some layer of SIP parsing before sending the full message further.

functions.name: sipmsg_validate
functions.doc: The function returns true if the SIP message is properly built according to SIP RFC3261. It verifies if the mandatory headers for each request/reply and can also check the format of the headers body.

functions.name: stream_delete
functions.doc: This function can be used to delete a whole stream from inside an sdp payload. It will search for the stream inside all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be deleted along with all attributes Returns TRUE if any deletion occurred otherwise it will return FALSE.

functions.name: stream_exists
functions.doc: This function can be used to verify if a stream exists inside an sdp payload. It will search for the stream inside all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will return TRUE otherwise it will return FALSE.

params.name: skip_failover_codes
params.doc: A regular expression used to specify the codes that should prevent the module from failing over to a new SRS server.

functions.name: siprec_pause_recording
functions.doc: Pauses the recording for the ongoing call. Should be called after the dialog has matched.

functions.name: siprec_resume_recording
functions.doc: Resumes the recording for the ongoing call. Should be called after the dialog has matched.

functions.name: siprec_start_recording
functions.doc: Calling this function on an initial INVITE engages call recording to SRS(s) for that call. Note that it does not necessary mean that the call will be recorded - it just means that OpenSIPS will query instruct the SRS that a new call has started, but the SRS might decide that the recording is disabled for those participants.

params.name: enable_stats
params.doc: If the module should generate and export statistics to the core manager. A zero value means disabled.

functions.name: sl_reply_error
functions.doc: Sends back an error reply describing the nature of the last internal error. Usually this function should be used after a script function that returned an error code.

functions.name: sl_send_reply
functions.doc: For the current request, a reply is sent back having the given code and text reason. The reply is sent stateless, totally independent of the Transaction module and with no retransmission for the INVITE's replies. 'code' and 'reason' can contain pseudo-variables that are replaced at runtime.

functions.name: sngtc_callee_answer
functions.doc: Handles the SDP offer from 200 OK responses, intersects both offers with the capabilities of the transcoding card and creates a new transcoding session on the card only if necessary. It then rewrites the 200 OK SDP so that it contains the information resulted from the codec intersection.

functions.name: sngtc_caller_answer
functions.doc: Attaches an SDP body to the caller's ACK request, so that it matches the late SDP negotiation done by the UAS.

functions.name: sngtc_offer
functions.doc: The function strips off the SDP offer from a SIP INVITE, thus asking for another SDP offer from the opposite endpoint (late negotiation). The following error codes may be returned: -1 - SDP parsing error -3 - internal error / no more memory

params.name: MsgQueueMajorThreshold
params.doc: The SNMPStats module monitors the number of bytes waiting to be consumed by OpenSIPS. If the number of bytes waiting to be consumed exceeds a major threshold, the SNMPStats module will send out an openserMsgQueueDepthMajorEvent trap to signal that an alarm condition has occurred. The major threshold is set with the MsgQueueMajorThreshold parameter.

params.name: MsgQueueMinorThreshold
params.doc: The SNMPStats module monitors the number of bytes waiting to be consumed by OpenSIPS. If the number of bytes waiting to be consumed exceeds a minor threshold, the SNMPStats module will send out an openserMsgQueueDepthMinorEvent trap to signal that an alarm condition has occurred. The minor threshold is set with the MsgQueueMinorThreshold parameter.

params.name: dlg_major_threshold
params.doc: The SNMPStats module monitors the number of active dialogs. If the number of active dialogs exceeds a major threshold, the SNMPStats module will send out an openserDialogLimitMajorEvent trap to signal that an alarm condition has occurred. The major threshold is set with the dlg_major_threshold parameter.

params.name: dlg_minor_threshold
params.doc: The SNMPStats module monitors the number of active dialogs. If the number of active dialogs exceeds a minor threshold, the SNMPStats module will send out an openserDialogLimitMinorEvent trap to signal that an alarm condition has occurred. The minor threshold is set with the dlg_minor_threshold parameter.

params.name: sipEntityType
params.doc: This parameter describes the entity type for this OpenSIPS instance, and will be used in determining what is returned for the openserSIPEntityType scalar. Valid parameters are:

params.name: snmpCommunity
params.doc: The SNMPStats module provides the openserSIPServiceStartTime scalar. This scalar requires the SNMPStats module to perform a snmpget query to the master agent. If you have defined a custom community string for the snmp daemon, you need to specify it with this parameter.

params.name: snmpgetPath
params.doc: The SNMPStats module provides the openserSIPServiceStartTime scalar. This scalar requires the SNMPStats module to perform a snmpget query to the master agent. You can use this parameter to set the path to your instance of SNMP's snmpget program.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The URL of database where the table containing speed dial records.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: The name of column storing the domain of the owner of the speed dial record.

params.name: domain_prefix
params.doc: If the domain of the owner (From URI) starts with the value of this parameter, then it is stripped before performing the lookup of the short number.

params.name: new_uri_column
params.doc: The name of the column containing the URI that will be use to replace the short dial URI.

params.name: sd_domain_column
params.doc: The name of the column storing the domain of the short dial address.

params.name: sd_user_column
params.doc: The name of the column storing the user part of the short dial address.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: The parameter specifies wheter or not to use the domain when searching a speed dial record (0 - no domain, 1 - use domain from From URI, 2 - use both domains, from From URI and from request URI).

params.name: user_column
params.doc: The name of column storing the user name of the owner of the speed dial record.

functions.name: sd_lookup
functions.doc: The function lookups the short dial number from R-URI in 'table' and replaces the R-URI with associated address.

params.name: bigint_to_str
params.doc: Controls bigint conversion. By default bigint values are returned as int. If the value stored in bigint is out of the int range, by enabling bigint to string conversion, the bigint value will be returned as string.

params.name: cache_table
params.doc: This parameter can be set multiple times in order to cache multiple SQL tables or even the same table but with a different configuration. The module distinguishes those different entries by an id string.

params.name: columns_delimiter
params.doc: The delimiter to be used in the columns subparameter of the caching entry specification provided in the cache_table parameter to separate the desired columns names. It must be a single character.

params.name: full_caching_expire
params.doc: Expire period for the values stored in cache for the full caching type in seconds. This is the longest time that deleted or modified data remains in cache.

params.name: pvar_delimiter
params.doc: The delimiter to be used in the $sql_cached_value pseudovariable to separate the caching id, the desired column name and the value of the key. It must be a single character.

params.name: reload_interval
params.doc: This parameter represents how many seconds before the data expires (for full caching) the automatic reloading is triggered.

params.name: spec_delimiter
params.doc: The delimiter to be used in the caching entry specification provided in the cache_table parameter to separate the subparameters. It must be a single character.

params.name: sql_fetch_nr_rows
params.doc: The number of rows to be fetched into OpenSIPS private memory in one chunk from the SQL database driver. When querying large tables, adjust this parameter accordingly to avoid the filling of OpenSIPS private memory.

params.name: attribute_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the attribute name (AVP name).

params.name: bigint_to_str
params.doc: Exported by `sqlops`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: db_scheme
params.doc: Definition of a DB scheme to be used for accessing a non-standard User Preference -like table.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: DB URL for database connection. As the module allows the usage of multiple DBs (DB URLs), the actual DB URL may be preceded by an reference number. This reference number is to be passed to AVPOPS function that what to explicitly use this DB connection. If no reference number is given, 0 is assumed - this is the default DB URL.

params.name: domain_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the domain name.

params.name: ps_id_max_buf_len
params.doc: The maximum size of the buffer used to build the query IDs which are used for managing the Prepare Statements when comes to the "sql_select|update|insert|replace|delete()" functions

params.name: type_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the AVP type.

params.name: use_domain
params.doc: If the domain part of the a SIP URI should be used for identifying an AVP in DB operations.

params.name: username_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the username.

params.name: usr_table
params.doc: DB table to be used for user preferences (AVPs)

params.name: uuid_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the uuid (unique user id).

params.name: value_column
params.doc: Name of column containing the AVP value.

functions.name: sql_avp_delete
functions.doc: Deletes from DB the AVPs corresponding to the given source .

functions.name: sql_avp_load
functions.doc: Loads from DB into memory the AVPs corresponding to the given source . If given, it sets the script flags for loaded AVPs. It returns true if it loaded some values in AVPs, false otherwise (db error, no avp loaded ...).

functions.name: sql_avp_store
functions.doc: Stores to DB the AVPs corresponding to the given source .

functions.name: sql_delete
functions.doc: Function to perform a structured (not raw) SQL DELETE operation. IMPORTANT: please see all the general notes from the function.

functions.name: sql_insert
functions.doc: Function to perform a structured (not raw) SQL INSERT operation. IMPORTANT: please see all the general notes from the function.

functions.name: sql_query
functions.doc: Make a database query and store the result in AVPs.

functions.name: sql_query_one
functions.doc: Similar to , it makes a generic raw database query and returns the results, but with the following differences:

functions.name: sql_replace
functions.doc: Function very similar to function, but performing an SQL REPLACE operation instead. Note that not all SQL backend in OpenSIPS may support a REPLACE operation.

functions.name: sql_select
functions.doc: Function to perform a structured (not raw) SQL SELECT operation. The query is performed via OpenSIPS internal SQL interface, taking advantages of the prepared-statements support (if the db backend provides something like that). The selected columns are returned into a set of AVPs (one to one matching the selected columns).

functions.name: sql_select_one
functions.doc: Similar to , it makes a SELECT SQL query and returns the results, but with the following differences:

functions.name: sql_update
functions.doc: Function to perform a structured (not raw) SQL UPDATE operation. IMPORTANT: please see all the general notes from the function.

params.name: enable_stats
params.doc: If the statistics support should be enabled or not. Via statistic variables, the module provide information about the dialog processing. Set it to zero to disable or to non-zero to enable it.

params.name: min_se
params.doc: The value is used to set the proxies MIN-SE value and is used in the 422 reply as the proxies MIN-SE: header value if the sstCheckMin() flag is set to true and the check fails.

params.name: reject_to_small
params.doc: In the initial INVITE if the UAC has requested a Session-Expire: and it's value is smaller then our local policies Min-SE (see min_se above), then the PROXY has the right to reject the call by replying to the message with a 422 Session Timer Too Small and state our local Min-SE: value. The INVITE is NOT forwarded on through the PROXY.

params.name: sst_flag
params.doc: Keeping with OpenSIPS, the module will not do anything to any message unless instructed to do so via the opensips.cfg script. You must set the sst_flag value in the setflag() call of the INVITE you want the sst module to process. But before you can do that, you need to tell the sst module which flag value you are assigning to sst.

params.name: sst_interval
params.doc: The sst minimum interval in Session-Expires header if OpenSIPS request the use of session times. The used value will be the maximum value between OpenSIPS minSE, UAS minSE and this value.

functions.name: sstCheckMin
functions.doc: Check the current Session-Expires / MIN-SE values against the sst_min_se parameter value. If the Session-Expires or MIN_SE header value is less then modules minimum value, this function will return true.

params.name: stat_groups
params.doc: A comma-separated values string, specifying the statistic groups that may be used throughout the OpenSIPS script. Groups cannot contain leading or trailing whitespace characters.

params.name: stat_series_profile
params.doc: Used to define a statistic series profile. Has the following format: name: [attr=value]* , where name represents the name of the profile, and attr=value contains multiple settings of the defined profile. Possible attributes and their values are: algorithm - indicates the way data should be stored and accumulated over the specified timeframe. Possible values are: accumulate , average and percentage , as described in the paragraph (default is accumulate ) hash_size - each statistic defined/used is stored in a hash map attached to the profile; this setting tunes the size of the hash (default is: 8) group - indicates the group where the statistics beloging to this profile are grouped (as described in (default is to use the same group as the profile) window - the number of seconds a timeframe has; all older values (out of the specified window) are discarded (default is 60 seconds) slots - the number of slots per window; used to tune the granularity of the circular buffer; the higher the number of slots is, the more accurate the resulted statistic; (default is the same value of the window parameter) percentage_factor - used for percentage algorithm profiles to specify the percentage factor to be used (defaults to 100 )

params.name: variable
params.doc: Name of a new statistic variable. The name may be followed by additional flag which describe the variable behavior:

functions.name: reset_stat
functions.doc: Resets to zero the value of the statistic variable.

functions.name: stat_iter_init
functions.doc: Re-initializes "iter" in order to begin iterating through all statistics belonging to the given "group".

functions.name: stat_iter_next
functions.doc: Attempts to fetch the current statistic to which "iter" points. If successful, the relevant data will be written to "name" and "val", while also advancing "iter". Returns negative when reaching the end of iteration.

functions.name: update_stat
functions.doc: Updates the value of the statistic variable with the new value.

functions.name: update_stat_series
functions.doc: Updates the value of a series statistic.

params.name: script_sr_group
params.doc: Name of a new Status/Report group to be created and later used from script level.

functions.name: sr_add_report
functions.doc: Adds a new report/log to a Status/Report group.This must have been defined via this module too.

functions.name: sr_set_status
functions.doc: Sets a new status (and details) for a Status/Report group.

params.name: auth_date_freshness
params.doc: The maximum number of seconds that the value in the Date header field can be older than the current time.

params.name: ca_dir
params.doc: Path to a directory containing trusted CA certificates for the verifier. The certificates in the directory must be in hashed form, as described in the openssl documentation for the Hashed Directory Method .

params.name: ca_list
params.doc: Path to a file containing trusted CA certificates for the verifier. The certificates must be in PEM format, one after another.

params.name: crl_dir
params.doc: Path to a directory containing certificate revocation lists (CRLs) for the verifier. The CRLs in the directory must be in hashed form, as described in the openssl documentation for the Hashed Directory Method .

params.name: crl_list
params.doc: Path to a file containing certificate revocation lists (CRLs) for the verifier.

params.name: e164_max_length
params.doc: This parameter allows the 15-digit number length restriction of the E.164 format to be bypassed. Especially useful in scenarios where various telephony number prefixes are in use, causing some numbers to exceed the standard maximum length.

params.name: e164_strict_mode
params.doc: Require a leading "+" to be present in the originating/destination SHAKEN identity, on top of mandating an E.164 telephone number by default. Additionally, require the URI to be either a tel URI or a sip / sips URI with the user=phone parameter.

params.name: require_date_hdr
params.doc: Specifies whether the Date header is mandatory when doing verification with the function.

params.name: verify_date_freshness
params.doc: The maximum number of seconds that the value in the Date header field can be older than the current time. Also, if the iat value in the PASSporT is different than the Date value, but remains within the permitted interval, it will be used in the verification process (for the reconstructed PASSporT) instead of the Date value.

functions.name: stir_shaken_auth
functions.doc: This function performs the steps of an authentication service. Before calling this function though, you must ensure:

functions.name: stir_shaken_check
functions.doc: This function checks the Identity header in order to validate the STIR/SHAKEN information in terms of format. It detects issues such as: missing or badly formated PASSporT claims, unsupported extensions etc.

functions.name: stir_shaken_check_cert
functions.doc: This function checks if the current time falls within the given certificate's validity period.

functions.name: stir_shaken_verify
functions.doc: This function performs the steps of an verification service.

params.name: alternate_ip
params.doc: Another IP from another interface. This is a mandatory parameter.

params.name: alternate_port
params.doc: The port used by the STUN server for the second interface. The default value is 3478 (default STUN port).

params.name: primary_ip
params.doc: The IP of an interface which is configured as an UDP SIP listener in OpenSIPS. This is a mandatory parameter, unless is enabled.

params.name: primary_port
params.doc: The port configured (together with the primary_ip ) as an UDP SIP listener in OpenSIPS. The default value is 5060.

params.name: use_listeners_as_primary
params.doc: Setting this parameter to 1 will allow all configured UDP SIP listeners to be automatically used as "primary" STUN sockets.

params.name: alias_mode_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: attrs_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: con_lifetime_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: connect_timeout_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: The name of the table holding the TCP paths (rules).

params.name: db_url
params.doc: Mandatory URL to the SQL database.

params.name: direction_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: id_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: keepalive_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: keepcount_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: keepidle_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: keepinterval_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: local_addr_col
params.doc: Exported by `tcp_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: local_port_col

functions.name: replace
functions.doc: Replaces the first occurrence of re with txt.

functions.name: replace_all
functions.doc: Replaces all occurrence of re with txt.

functions.name: replace_body
functions.doc: Replaces the first occurrence of re in the body of the message with txt.

functions.name: replace_body_all
functions.doc: Replaces all occurrence of re in the body of the message with txt. Matching is done on a per-line basis.

functions.name: replace_body_atonce
functions.doc: Replaces all occurrence of re in the body of the message with txt. Matching is done over the whole body.

functions.name: search
functions.doc: Searches for the re in the message.

functions.name: search_append
functions.doc: Searches for the first match of re and appends txt after it.

functions.name: search_append_body

functions.name: search_body

functions.name: subst

functions.name: subst_body

functions.name: subst_uri
functions.doc: Runs the re substitution on the message uri (like subst but works only on the uri)

functions.name: subst_user
functions.doc: Runs the re substitution on the message uri (like subst_uri but works only on the user portion of the uri)

params.name: ca_dir
params.doc: Directory storing trusted CAs. The certificates in the directory must be in hashed form, as described in the openssl documentation for the Hashed Directory Method . The domain part represents the name of the TLS domain.

params.name: ca_dir_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: ca_list
params.doc: List of trusted CAs. The file contains the certificates accepted, one after the other. It MUST be a file, not a folder. The domain part represents the name of the TLS domain.

params.name: ca_list_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: certificate
params.doc: Public certificate file for OpenSIPS. It will be used as server-side certificate for incoming TLS connections, and as a client-side certificate for outgoing TLS connections. The domain part represents the name of the TLS domain.

params.name: certificate_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: ciphers_list
params.doc: You can specify the list of algorithms for authentication and encryption that you allow. The domain part represents the name of the TLS domain. To obtain a list of ciphers and then choose, use the openssl application:

params.name: ciphers_list_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: client_domain
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: client_sip_domain_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP that sets the SIP domain used in the TLS client domain matching process.

params.name: client_tls_domain_avp
params.doc: Name of the AVP used for enforcing the selection of a specific TLS client domain. Setting this AVP to the name of a TLS client domain will result in using that specific domain regardless of the standard matching mechanism.

params.name: crl_check_all
params.doc: Setting this parameter with a non-zero integer value enables CRL checking for the entire certificate chain.

params.name: crl_check_all_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: crl_dir
params.doc: Directory storing certificate revocation lists (CRLs). The domain part represents the name of the TLS domain.

params.name: crl_dir_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: db_table
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: db_url
params.doc: The database url. It cannot be NULL.

params.name: dh_params
params.doc: You can specify a file which contains Diffie-Hellman parameters as a PEM-file. This is needed if you would like to specify ciphers including Diffie-Hellman mode. The domain part represents the name of the TLS domain.

params.name: dh_params_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: domain_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: ec_curve
params.doc: You can specify an elliptic curve which should be used for ciphers which demand an elliptic curve. The domain part represents the name of the TLS domain.

params.name: ec_curve_col

params.name: match_ip_address
params.doc: The IP addresses and ports used to match a TLS connection with a virtual TLS domain. For TLS server domains, these values will be mathced against the socket on which the connection is received. For TLS client domains, the values will be compared with the destination socket of the connection.

params.name: match_ip_address_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: match_sip_domain
params.doc: The SIP domains used to match a TLS connection with a virtual TLS domain. For TLS server domains, these values will be matched against the hostname provided in the TLS Servername extension(SNI). For TLS client domains, the values will be compared with the value of the AVP.

params.name: match_sip_domain_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: private_key
params.doc: Private key of the above certificate. I must be kept in a safe place with tight permissions! The domain part represents the name of the TLS omain.

params.name: private_key_col
params.doc: Exported by `tls_mgm`; not documented in the module README.

params.name: require_cert_col

params.name: tls_library
params.doc: Selects which TLS library to use. Possible values are:

params.name: verify_cert_col
